description:
A Singing Sligo is an inclusive, interactive choral workshop celebrating the joy of collective singing, led by award-winning conductor and Sligo native Ciara Murphy with support from Sligo Orpheus Choir.

Open to adults of all musical backgrounds, from complete beginners to experienced singers, the workshop will explore catchy canons and rounds from a range of cultural traditions, including Irish folk melodies, African chants, Scandinavian rhythms and contemporary global canons.

Participants will learn together through guided warm-ups and rehearsals before joining in a relaxed final group performance. No previous singing experience is needed.

Free, welcoming and accessible, A Singing Sligo celebrates collective singing as a way of connecting people across different backgrounds, abilities and experiences.

title: ‘Headspace’ screening in partnership with Run of the Mill
description:
HEADSPACE is an award-winning Irish short film written and directed by Aisling Byrne and produced by Killian Coyle for Run of the Mill, in association with Arcade Film. Filmed entirely on location in Celbridge, Co. Kildare, the film stars local actor Mark Smith in a breakout lead performance as a young man with Down syndrome who, as the tensions and frustrations of life in a community house begin to close in on him, realises he may have to cross a line to end a nightly disturbance.

Produced by Kildare-based inclusive arts organisation Run of the Mill, HEADSPACE won the Oscar®-qualifying Grand Prix for Best Irish Short at Cork International Film Festival 2022, before screening at dozens of international film festivals, receiving numerous awards and accolades, and premiering nationally on RTÉ Player. Funded by the Arts Council of Ireland, the film reflects Run of the Mill’s distinctive collaborative approach to filmmaking, creating bold, artist-led work with and by artists with intellectual disabilities. Founded in Kildare in 2014, Run of the Mill is one of Ireland’s leading inclusive arts organisations and is proudly supported by Kildare County Council.

No booking required. The film will be screened on the upstairs Mezzanine in Celbridge library, accessible by stair lift.

title: ‘Soundscape of the Artist’ with Mike Dowd and Guests, Bewick Collection, Library Place, Killorglin
description:
‘Soundscape of the Artist’ with Mike Dowd and Guests, Bewick Collection

The ‘Seven Ages’ collection, one of Kerry’s most exciting cultural treasures, is a permanent art exhibition featuring the work of renowned artist, Pauline Bewick. The collection of work is internationally unique – no other artist has the range and depth of works which explore seven decades of an artist’s and a woman’s life.

On turning 70 in 2005, Pauline Bewick decided to donate a 500-piece master collection to the State, which President Mary McAleese described as ‘one of the loveliest acts of generosity ever given to our nation’. Two vast collections, representing the first seven decades of her life, are permanently exhibited in Killorglin and in the South East Technological University in Waterford. Pauline Bewick drew much inspiration from her Kerry surroundings and from Irish life and mythology. This work is thought- provoking, humorous, and reflective, and is an invaluable social and cultural record of twentieth-century Ireland. It is perpetually available for the enjoyment of the Irish public and international audiences.

title: ‘Taking the Long Road’ Launch at Chapters
description:
This Culture Night, join award-winning author, curator, and activist Oein DeBhairduin at Chapters Bookshop for the launch of a new podcast ‘Taking the Long Road’.

This series will explore the harmful legacy of the Commission on Itineracy Report, 1963 and its impact on the Traveller community, Ireland’s indigenous ethnic community. The series will be launched by Oein in conversation with leading human rights activist, cultural consultant and theatre maker Catherine Joyce.

The event is part of Skein’s ‘Thinking Aloud, Thinking Together’ initiative, which encompasses cross-disciplinary discussions between artists, writers and thinkers, touching on current points of connection and concern in contemporary culture.

Oein DeBhairduin is a writer, activist and educator with a passion for preserving the beauty of Traveller tales, sayings, retellings and historic exchanges. Oein is the author of the award-winning ‘Why the moon travels’. His other works are ‘Weave’, ‘The Slug and the Snail’ and ‘Twiggy Woman’. He is the Curator of Traveller Culture with the National Museum of Ireland and seeks to pair community activism with cultural celebration, recalling old tales with fresh modern connections and, most of all, he wishes to rekindle the hearth fires of a shared kinship.

Catherine Joyce is a leading Traveller human rights activist and spokesperson. She has represented the community at the United Nations and was appointed by the Irish government to the Task Force on Travelling community and its National Monitoring Committee and is the manager of Blanchardstown Travellers Development Group. She is a cultural consultant and theatre maker collaborating on The Trailer of Bridgit Dinnigan and The Rose Tattoo and films Worlds Apart and Float like a Butterfly. Catherine received the people of the year award in 1991 from the Rehab Group.

 

Advance booking is advised however walk-ins may be admitted if capacity allows.

title: ‘Grounded in Nature’ Exhibition Opening
description:
Grounded in Nature brings together the work of three West Cork artists, Etain Hickey, Jim Turner and Laura Wade, whose practices are rooted in a deep engagement with landscape, place and the natural world. Opening on Culture Night at 6.30pm in The Loft Gallery, Clonakilty, this exhibition creates a conversation between clay and ink, material and mark-making, observation and imagination.

Ceramic artist Etain Hickey has spent decades responding to the rich visual tapestry of her West Cork surroundings. Known for her highly decorated ceramics, she draws inspiration from the rhythms of nature, native flora and fauna, and the patterns that shape both landscape and memory. Her colourful, expressive work combines a love of texture, ornament and storytelling, celebrating the vitality and beauty found in the everyday natural world. Her ceramics have been exhibited nationally and internationally and are included in public and private collections including the Design & Crafts Council Ireland collection, the Ulster Museum and the Fujita Museum in Japan.

For Jim Turner, clay offers an ongoing dialogue with environment, experience and form. A graduate of Camberwell College of Art who has lived and worked in West Cork for over forty years, his sculptural vessels and paper-clay constructions explore texture, geology and the transformative nature of the ceramic process. Influenced by the West Cork landscape and seascape, as well as architecture, ancient pottery traditions and sailing, his work occupies a space between object and landscape, inviting contemplation and discovery.

Working primarily in ink and paper, Laura Wade creates evocative works that explore themes of resilience, wonder and reconnection with nature. Originally from Cork and now based in the west of Ireland, Wade is recognised for her distinctive visual language of silhouettes, shadow forms and delicate geometric interventions. Drawing inspiration from trees, plant life and the quieter aspects of the landscape, her work invites viewers into contemplative spaces where the boundaries between the seen and unseen become fluid and poetic.

Together, these artists present three unique yet complementary perspectives on our relationship with the natural world. Through clay and ink, Grounded in Nature reflects on the enduring influence of landscape on creative practice and offers a thoughtful meditation on place, belonging and the beauty that surrounds us.
fullAddress: The Loft Gallery, Western Road, Tawnies Upper, Clonakilty, County Cork, Ireland

title: ‘In the Opinion of the Censor’ Screening and Q&A
description:
This Culture Night, the Irish Film Classification Office (IFCO) will be opening its doors for a special screening of the documentary ‘In the Opinion of the Censor’ followed by a Q&A.

The feature-length documentary tells the story of the Censorship of Films Act 1923 and how one canny term in that statute has allowed consecutive holders of the role of Film Censor to reflect the prevailing values of Irish society over the last 100 years.

In the documentary, John Kelleher, Ireland’s last Film Censor and first Director of Film Classification, presents and narrates the fascinating story of Irish film censorship. Drawing on contributions from historians, filmmakers, movie archivists and media commentators, as well as film clips from titles such as Gone With the Wind, Casablanca, Ulysses, The Graduate, and Monty Python’s Life of Brian – including scenes Irish Audiences would not have seen – John illustrates how the story of Irish film censorship mirrored the evolution of Irish society over the course of the last one hundred years.

Directed by Andrew Gallimore and Lydia Monin, this critically acclaimed film blends rare archival footage, expert interviews, and scenes from iconic censored films.

‘In the Opinion of the Censor’ is produced by John Kelleher Media and supported by IFCO, Oireachtas TV, Coimisiún na Meán and Caireann Associates.

Rating: 12A
fullAddress: Irish Film Classification Office, Blackhall Walk, Smithfield, Dublin, Ireland

title: ‘Som do Brasil’ A Celebration of Brazilian Popular Music
description:
Som do Brasil—meaning The Sound of Brazil—celebrates the music and rhythms that have shaped Brazil’s rich musical heritage.

Brazilian musicians Cairo Rocha, Tony Sozza and André Alexandre join Ennis singer-songwriter Amanda Ní Sheannáin to perform songs by some of Brazil’s most celebrated composers and performers, including Tom Jobim, Maria Bethânia, Rita Lee, Lenine, João Gilberto, Gilberto Gil, Elizeth Cardoso, Emílio Santiago, Vinicius de Moraes, Maria Creuza and Toquinho.

From the gentle sway of bossa nova to the vibrant energy of samba and the timeless songs of Brazilian Popular Music (MPB), the programme offers a journey through some of Brazil’s most iconic music. Beloved around the world for its warmth, melody and infectious rhythms, this repertoire captures the richness, joy and soul of Brazilian musical culture.

To mark this special Culture Night performance, subtle moments of the Irish language will be woven into selected songs, offering a unique local touch while celebrating the enduring spirit of Brazilian music

‘Som do Brasil’- Ceiliúradh ar Cheol Coitianta na Brasaíle Ciallaíonn Som do Brasil—“Fuaim na Brasaíle”—ceiliúradh ar an gceol agus ar na rithimí atá fite fuaite le croí agus le cultúr na Brasaíle.

Tagann na ceoltóirí Brasaíleacha Cairo Rocha, Tony Sozza agus André Alexandre le chéile leis an amhránaí is scríbhneoir amhrán as Inis, Amanda Ní Sheannáin, chun cuid de na hamhráin is ansa le lucht ceoil na Brasaíle a chur i láthair, le saothair ó chuid de na cumadóirí agus na healaíontóirí is mó le rá sa tír, ina measc Tom Jobim, Maria Bethânia, Rita Lee, Lenine, João Gilberto, Gilberto Gil, Elizeth Cardoso, Emílio Santiago, Vinicius de Moraes, Maria Creuza agus Toquinho.

Ó bhláth bog an bossa nova go fuinneamh an tsamba agus amhráin mhóra Cheol Coitianta na Brasaíle (MPB), tugann an clár blaiseadh do lucht éisteachta de shaol saibhir ceoil na Brasaíle. Ceol a bhfuil aithne air ar fud an domhain mar gheall ar a theas, a mhilseacht agus a rithimí beoga, tugann na hamhráin seo léargas ar spiorad agus ar áilleacht cheol na Brasaíle.

Mar chuid den léiriú speisialta seo d’Oíche Chultúir, beidh blaiseadh beag den Ghaeilge fite fuaite trí chuid de na hamhráin, ag tabhairt nasc áitiúil beag don cheol agus ag ceiliúradh draíocht bhuan fhuaim na Brasaíle.

title: “Though they never returned, their story has found its way home.”
description:
The Tudor Artisan Hub presents a profound Culture Night event in the Long Gallery, Ormond Castle, honouring 34 forgotten women from Carrick-on-Suir and the Suir Valley, Co. Tipperary, transported to Australia in the 19th century.

Central to this event is the work of Waterford’s Transported Convict Women, A Herstory. Partnering with SETU Library, the Digital Repository of Ireland (DRI), and the Roses from the Heart project, the bonnets, research, and stories behind them are now digitally preserved and accessible to a global audience. On the night, they will deliver an insightful overview of their ongoing work and plans.

🌿 Though They Never Returned, Their Story Has Found Its Way Home – Film & Exhibition, Ormond Castle.

From Monday 14th to Sunday 20th September, Tudor Artisan Hub, in association with Waterford’s Transported Convict Women, A Herstory and Roses from the Heart, and in collaboration with SETU Library, Writing Changes Lives and local composer Marian Ingoldsby, is remembering 34 women transported to Australia and Tasmania in the 18th and 19th centuries.

Many had connections to Carrick-on-Suir and the wider Suir Valley. This is an important part of our history that has often been overlooked, behind each name is a woman, a life, a family, a journey and a story.

🎥 VIDEO PRESENTATION – AV Room, Ormond Castle
A specially created 45-minute film featuring historian Dr Joan Kavanagh, descendants from Australia, Historiands Dr Christina Henri and  Ann Fitzgerald, local poet Shirley O’Shea and stories from the Roses from the Heart bonnet makers.
Screenings daily at 11am & 3pm – FREE

👒 EXHIBITION – LONG GALLERY
34 handcrafted Tribute Bonnets, each representing one of the women, accompanied by her individual story. QR codes allow visitors to explore the full stories digitally through SETU Library and the Digital Repository of Ireland (DRI).

🎭 Culture Night performance – Friday 18th September: FULLY BOOKED

But you can still come along next week to watch the film, see the bonnets and discover the stories.

👥 GROUPS VERY WELCOME

📅 Monday 14th – Sunday 20th September
🎥 11am & 3pm daily (Other time slots may be available upon request).
🎟️ FREE

description:
Legacy is celebrating more than 60 years of craftsmanship by master potter Con Lynch in a unique exhibition at ‘The Canopy’.

For decades, Con has used locally sourced materials for his glazes and drawn inspiration from the surrounding bogland for the shapes, colours and textures of his work.

This ‘Ceramic Poem’ presentation, entitled ‘Legacy’, brings Con’s workshop directly to the public, and the ‘Cube’ showcases his craftsmanship – a free exhibition open to all, which everyone can experience during Culture Night.

title: 500 Miles
description:
Teenager Finn and his younger brother Charlie are extremely close to their grandfather
John. However, a heartbreaking accident has led to their parents cutting off all contact with
John. Devastated by the estrangement, Finn and Charlie decide to run away and make the
trip from their English home to their grandfather’s home on the west coast of Ireland. With
limited funds and constant worries over Charlie’s fragile health, it proves to be a risky and
emotional journey for the boys.
Based on Mark Lowery’s book Charlie and Me, 500 Miles is a deeply affecting road-trip and

title: 7th Annual ÍOVA Culture Night Exhibition – Human Touch
description:
For its 7th annual Culture Night exhibition, ÍOVA Photography Collective presents Human Touch, a celebration of the creativity, care and connection that define the human experience.

Founded in 2018 through conversations at John Gunn Camera Shop, ÍOVA has grown into a vibrant community of photographers, artists and analogue enthusiasts who believe in the value of learning, making and sharing together.

In a time when so much of our lives is mediated by technology, Human Touch reflects on the importance of physical presence, craftsmanship and genuine human connection. The exhibition invites audiences to slow down and consider the moments that shape our lives through touch, memory, observation and shared experience.

From the warmth of sunlight on skin and the smell of rain on dry ground to the comfort of a hug, a helping hand or a reassuring smile, the works explore the everyday experiences that cannot be replicated or replaced.

Bringing together artists working across photography and lens-based practices, Human Touch celebrates imagination, community and the enduring importance of people creating with and for one another.

Don seachtú taispeántas bliantúil dá gcuid do Oíche an Chultúir, cuireann Comharchumann Grianghrafadóireachta ÍOVA Human Touch i láthair – ceiliúradh ar an gcruthaitheacht, ar an gcúram agus ar an nasc a shainíonn an taithí dhaonna.

Agus é bunaithe in 2018 de bharr comhráite ag Siopa Ceamaraí John Gunn, tá ÍOVA tar éis fás ina phobal bríomhar grianghrafadóirí, ealaíontóirí agus díograiseoirí na grianghrafadóireachta analóige a chreideann i luach na foghlama, na cruthaitheachta agus na comhroinnte le chéile.

Agus an oiread sin dár saol á stiúradh ag an teicneolaíocht sa lá atá inniu ann, tugann Human Touch cuireadh dúinn machnamh a dhéanamh ar thábhacht na láithreachta fisiciúla, na ceirde agus an naisc dhaonna dhílis. Spreagann an taispeántas an lucht féachana chun moill a chur ar an luas agus machnamh a dhéanamh ar na chuimhneacháin a mhúnlaíonn ár saol trí thadhaill, trí chuimhní cinn, trí bhreathnóireacht agus trí eispéiris chomhroinnte.

Ó theas na gréine ar an gcraiceann agus boladh na báistí ar an talamh tirim go dtí an sólás a bhaineann le barróg, le lámh chúnta nó le gáire misniúil, déanann na saothair iniúchadh ar eispéiris an lae a bhfuil sé dodhéanta iad a mhacasamhlú nó a chur ina n-ionad.

Ag tabhairt ealaíontóirí le chéile a oibríonn i réimse na grianghrafadóireachta agus na gcleachtas lionsa-bhunaithe, déanann Human Touch ceiliúradh ar an samhlaíocht, ar an bpobal agus ar an tábhacht bhuan a bhaineann le daoine a bheith ag cruthú le chéile agus ar son a chéile.

title: A Céilí in the Kitchen with John Dungan CCÉ
description:
Join John Dungan CCÉ for Céilí in the Kitchen, a special Culture Night celebration on 18 September, where the rich traditions of Irish music, song, dance and storytelling come to life in a warm and welcoming community setting.

Inspired by the tradition of neighbours gathering in the kitchen to share tunes, songs, stories and conversation, this event celebrates the heart of Ireland’s cultural heritage. Visitors can enjoy an evening of live performances from talented local musicians, singers, dancers and storytellers, showcasing the vibrant traditions that continue to thrive in Granard and throughout County Longford. Light refreshments will be served in keeping with the Céilí in the Kitchen theme, creating an authentic and relaxed atmosphere for all to enjoy.

Granard has played a significant role in the history and development of traditional Irish music, song and dance in County Longford. This event celebrates that proud legacy while highlighting the dedication of today’s performers, who continue to preserve and share these treasured traditions with new generations.

Whether you are a lifelong enthusiast of traditional arts or discovering them for the first time,Céilí in the Kitchen offers something for everyone. Sing along, tap your feet to lively tunes, listen to captivating stories and experience the warmth, hospitality and community spirit that define a traditional Irish céilí.

Come along for an evening of culture, connection and craic as we celebrate our shared heritage as part of Culture Night 2026. Admission is free, and everyone is welcome.

Bí páirteach le John Dungan CCÉ do Céilí sa Chistin, ceiliúradh speisialta Oíche Chultúir ar an 18 Meán Fómhair, áit a dtagann traidisiúin shaibhir na ceoil, amhráin, damhsa agus scéalaíochta Éireannaí beo i dtimpeallacht phobail te agus fáilteach. Spreagtha ag traidisiún na gcomharsan a bhailíonn sa chistin chun melóidí, amhráin, scéalta agus comhrá a roinnt, ceiliúrann an t-imeacht seo croí oidhreachta chultúrtha na hÉireann. Is féidir le cuairteoirí sult a bhaint as oíche de léirithe beo ó cheoltóirí, amhránaithe, damhsóirí agus scéalaiteoirí áitiúla a bhfuil tallann acu, ag léiriú na dtraidisiún bríomhar a mhaireann go láidir i nGranard agus ar fud Chontae Longfoirt. Beidh cócónta éadrom ar fáil de réir téama Céilí sa Chistin, ag cruthú atmaisféar barántúil agus relaxed le go mbainfidh gach duine taitneamh as.

Tá ról suntasach ag Granard i stair agus i bhforbairt ceol, amhrán agus rince traidisiúnta na hÉireann i gContae Longfort. Ceiliúrann an ócáid seo an oidhreacht bhródúil sin agus ag an am céanna taispeánann sé díograis lucht léirithe an lae inniu, a leanann de na traidisiúin luachmhara seo a chothú agus a roinnt le glúine nua.

Cibé an lucht leanúna fadscéalta tú de na healaíona traidisiúnta nó iad á gcumadh don chéad uair, tá rud éigin ann do chách ag Céilí sa Chistin. Can leat, tap do bhosa chuig fonn beoga, éist le scéalta tarraingteacha agus bain taithneamh as teas, fáilteachas agus spiorad pobail a shainíonn céilí traidisiúnta na hÉireann.

Tar agus bain sult as oíche lán de chultúr, nasc agus craic agus muid ag ceiliúradh ár n-oidhreacht choiteann mar chuid de Oíche na hEalaíne 2026. Tá an iontráil saor in aisce, agus tá fáilte roimh chách.

title: A Chip Odyssey 造山者 | Taiwanese Film Extravaganza at the Savoy Cinema
description:
Behind every chip lies a human story. Behind every breakthrough, a cross-generational gamble.
This Culture Night, the Dublin School of Mandarin Chinese (DSMC) proudly presents a special screening of the acclaimed documentary, A Chip Odyssey《造山者》. Organised in close collaboration with the Taipei Representative Office in Ireland and the Taiwan Ireland Association, and generously supported by the Overseas Community Affairs Council, this annual cinematic event is celebrating 21st edition of Ireland’s culture night.

About the film:
Though Taiwan accounts for less than 0.02% of the world’s landmass, it has become an indispensable force in the era of AI and advanced chipmaking. Directed by two-time Golden Horse Award-winner Hsiao Chu-Chen, A Chip Odyssey is an epic, five-year documentary project that traces Taiwan’s transformation into a global semiconductor leader.

Moving beyond dry technology, the film uncovers the deeply human stories behind the “Silicon Shield.” Through the eyes of pioneering engineers, frontline policymakers, and visionary scientists, it reveals how an entire island came together half a century ago in a high-stakes gamble to shape its own destiny and the future of global technology.

Join us for an unforgettable evening of cinema that celebrates innovation, resilience, and cross-generational determination.

Running Time: 106 minutes

title: A Concert of  Oriel Irish Traditional Music with Gerry O’Connor  renowned fiddle player at the Old Courthouse Rathcoole, accompanied by Paul Meehan on Guitar
description:
The Old Courthouse are delighted to present this live music concert for Culture Night with renowned musicians , Gerry O’Connor and Paul Meehan . Gerry O’Connor is a traditional Irish fiddle player, producer, composer, teacher, and founding member of Skylark and Lá Lúgh. He has toured internationally as a solo performer and collaborator, and has lectured in Traditional Music Performance at Dundalk Institute of Technology, where he completed an MA under Dr. Fintan Vallely. His research was published in 2018 as The Rose in the Gap: The Dance Music of Oriel, and in 2020 he received the CCE Gradam Award for lifetime service to the traditional arts. Gerry is also a qualified violin maker, restorer, and supplier of fine instruments, and has worked as a fiddle coach and on projects including Compánach with Fintan Vallely. Paul Meehan is an acclaimed Irish musician whose career spans more than 30 years of international touring, recording and collaboration. A former full-time member of Lunasa, Karan Casey Band, North Cregg, Na Dorsa and founding member of Buille, he has performed throughout Europe, North America, Australia, Russia and Japan. He has collaborated with renowned artists including Liz Carroll, Natalie Merchant, Tommy Peoples, Paddy Keenan, Brian Finnegan and Altan. Paul has recorded numerous award-winning albums, including his solo release The Lower Road and appeared on major television and radio networks worldwide.

Is ceoltóir Éireannach mór le rá é Paul Meehan a bhfuil gairm bheatha níos mó ná 30 bliain aige i gcúrsaí camchuairte idirnáisiúnta, taifeadta agus comhoibrithe. Iarbhall lánaimseartha de chuid Lúnasa, Banda Karen Casey, North Cregg, Na Dorsa agus ball bunaithe de Buile é. Tá sé tar éis seinm ar fud na hEorpa, Mheiriceá Thuaidh, na hAstráile, na Rúise agus na Seapáine. Tá go leor albam buaite duaiseanna taifeadta ag Paul, lena n-áirítear a albam aonair The Lower Road, agus tá sé le feiceáil ar mhór-líonraí teilifíse agus raidió ar fud an domhain._*

Is fiddleoir Tradisiúnta Éireannach è Gerry O Connor/Léiritheoir/ Cumadoiragus Múinteoir. Agus ball bunaithede Lá Lu agus Skylark. Déanamn sè camchuairt ar fud an domain mar fhidleoir aonair agus mar chomhoibrí. Tá sé tar éis léachtaí a thabhairt ar fheidhmíochtai ceol ag Institiud Teicneolaíochta Dhun Dealgan âit ar chríochnaigh sé MA faoi mhairseacht an Dr. Fintan Vallely. Foilsíodha thaighde mar The Rose in the Gap, The Dance Music of Oriel. Sa bhliain2020 bronnadh Gradam CCE air as seirvís saoildon Ealaíon Tradisiúnta. description:

The workshop invites audience intergenerational engagement using the artefacts in the story and atmospheric setting of Cash and Co, a familiar shopping space for both generations to engage and relate through stories from memory and thus grow in appreciation for the bonds formed through active intergenerational engagement.

title: A Night at The Moving Crib Museum: History, Curiosities & Wonder
description:
Step beneath the streets of Dublin this Culture Night and discover one of the city’s most fascinating and unexpected museums. Recently refurbished and expanded, The Moving Crib Museum will be open from 16:00 – 20:00, welcoming visitors of all ages to explore its unique collection.

Housed in the atmospheric basement of a historic Georgian building, the museum leads you through the original kitchens, meat store and coal stores, where history comes to life through an extraordinary collection of vintage curiosities, historic artefacts and over 120 working mechanical figurines dating from the 1950s.

Marvel at an authentic 1890s dolls’ house, discover fascinating objects from medieval times, the 1800s and the 1916 Rising, and meet Fred, the heroic dog who saved three people from the River Liffey. Along the way, uncover original features of the Georgian house and learn the stories behind this much-loved Dublin attraction, captivating visitors for almost 70 years.

Whether you’re a history enthusiast, a lover of nostalgia, or simply looking for something different to experience this Culture Night, The Moving Crib Museum promises an evening of discovery, craftsmanship and wonder.

title: A Night of Arabian Dreams – Crystalline
description:
A Night of Arabian Dreams invites audiences on a journey through the rich worlds of Middle Eastern dance, live music, and storytelling. Inspired by the tradition of the tales of One Thousand and One Nights, the performance weaves together Bellydance, Saidi, Dabke, contemporary dance, narration, and live darbuka (Arabic drum) rhythms to create an immersive theatrical experience.

Created by dancer and choreographer Mar Decena, this evolving production blends traditional Middle Eastern dance forms with contemporary movement, creating a dialogue between heritage and innovation. Featuring local dancers, live music, and, in its expanded version, a unique fusion of Middle Eastern and Irish dance traditions, the work explores themes of identity, belonging, love, resilience, and imagination.

Accessible to both dance enthusiasts and first time audiences, A Night of Arabian Dreams celebrates the power of movement to connect cultures. Through storytelling, rhythm, and dance, the performance invites audiences to discover a living artistic tradition while experiencing a vibrant exchange between communities, histories, and creative practices.

title: African Culture Night
description:
We would like to bring our performance to the County Museum Hall, Dundulk, on the 18rd of Sept. 2026 for African Culture Night between 4 and 7pm.
Our programs will include:
1. African cultural shows:
• African music: Our group will be able to play African music with different types of stepping and dancing to show   our African heritage with different types of attires.
• Masquerade dance: We are going to perform African masquerade dance in this event. The history of African   masquerade goes as follows:
Masquerades are traditional events that involved in masked dancers or in a face covered dress to look like spirits.   They happen during festivals, ceremonies, or rituals and can also involve songs, dances, drama, and poetry.   Masquerades reclaim the African heritage that was lost during colonial times, by embracing the likes of the spirit   of African culture and customs and giving meaning to aspects of African history.
• Drama: On every event or ceremony in Africa, there must be a way of showing culture by entertaining visitors/viewers. We will be able to perform a short African drama for the youth. The drama is believed to be educative and teach morals to the youth.
2. Art exhibition:
• There will be an exhibition of various African arts and crafts at the event and an instructor will be able to go             through it with everyone.
• There will be a particular artwork showing the creator the centre of Mombasa in Kenya in Africa and many   artifacts which will be part of the exhibition.
3. African Games:
• Ayo (A fun African game made up of a carved wooden box and seeds)

title: Alliance Francaise de Cork: Screening of Jacques Offenbach’s Opera “Robinson Crusoe”
description:
Screening of Jacques Offenbach’s opera “Robinson Crusoe” at Alliance Française de Cork, project led by the Rennes Opera.

Daniel Defoe’s world-famous story of Robinson Crusoe, the talent of Jacques Offenbach, Laurent Pelly’s debut production at the Rennes Opera, and a particularly promising cast… an exceptional event to close out the season.

While Offenbach’s operettas are regularly featured on opera house programs, his more serious works are rarely performed, with the exception of The Tales of Hoffmann.

The music of Robinson Crusoe reveals a wealth of imagination and colour, performed by the Orchestre National de Bretagne and conductor Guillaume Tourniaire, one of the foremost specialists in French music. Who better than Laurent Pelly to stage this little-known score and strike the subtle balance between laughter and poetry, while exploring our relationship with the unknown and the foreign?

Running time: approximately 2 hours and 30 minutes.
Opera sung in French, with English subtitles.
fullAddress: Alliance Française de Cork, Mary Street, Cork, Ireland

title: Along the Coast and Through the Trees by Pamela Leonard.
description:
Fingal County Council is proud to present a special Culture Night exhibition celebrating the works and artistic legacy of prolific Fingal artist Pamela Leonard. The exhibition, ‘Along the Coast and Through the Trees’,
showcases artworks recently acquired from the artist for inclusion in Fingal County Council’s Municipal Art
Collection. The Irish Times has described Pamela as a master of capturing light and dark across the Irish
landscape. While her work features much-loved landscapes all over Ireland, it is Pamela’s connection to her
home in Howth that has inspired her depictions of local coastal scenes and local flora and fauna.

Visitors will have the rare opportunity to explore the breadth of her expert printing and drawing techniques, including her pioneering methodology of layering vibrant, multi-colour schemes using just two plates. Alongside her critically acclaimed landscapes, Leonard’s work was featured on 16 An Post stamps and won a prestigious
international award in Japan. This dedication to her lifetime body of work reflects Fingal’s ongoing
commitment to support and preserve the legacies of local artists at every stage of their careers.
All welcome.

title: ALT WEST / ALT THIAR – Exhibition launch and performance
description:
ALT WEST / ALT THIAR is a new exhibition by the Office for Joint Administrative Intelligence (O.J.A.I.). Operating between Brussels and Berlin, the O.J.A.I.  is the collaborative practice of artists Chris Dreier and Gary Farrelly. They work at the intersection of art, bureaucracy, architecture, fact and fiction.
For ALT WEST / ALT THIAR, they have drawn on local research, conversations, archives, and encounters across the Mid-West region to create a temporary headquarters. Furthered by their research residency in March earlier this year, the project explores the infrastructures of Ireland’s Mid-West region and the stories, systems, and histories that shape everyday life.
For Culture Night, visitors are invited to attend special a live performances by the O.J.A.I. This informal event offers audiences a unique introduction to the world of O.J.A.I and includes the premier screening of a new film about the nearby Sarsfield House. This film considers the architectural merits of this contentious brutalist edifice. This event provides visitors with an opportunity to gain a deeper insight into this new site-responsive project that is speculative reimagining of the Mid-West region through art, research, and performance.

description:
We are delighted to announce the launch of the 3rd Annual Exhibition at An Chéad Tine, taking place on Culture Night, Friday 18 September 2026, from 6pm-8pm.

This year’s exhibition brings together the work of 50 Irish artists, selected through an open call by our invited guest selector, Maurice Quillinan (Artist and Curator at Limerick Museum Art Gallery @limerickhistorymuseum)

With an exceptionally strong response to the open call, the selection process was both challenging and exciting, bringing together a diverse group of artists working across a wide range of approaches, perspectives and artistic practices.

We are thrilled to present this collection of contemporary Irish art at An Chéad Tine and to provide a platform for artists to share their work with audiences in our community and beyond.

Everyone is warmly invited to join us for the opening evening which takes place on this Culture Night. Come along, meet the artists and enjoy an evening celebrating contemporary Irish art and creativity.

The exhibition will continue at An Chéad Tine until 19th October 2026.

We look forward to welcoming you and celebrating the wonderful range of talent represented in this year’s exhibition.

All are very welcome.

title: An evening of live music, DJs and collaboration at Ár n-Áit
description: Ár n-Áit present an afternoon and evening of live music, DJs and collaboration, celebrating the cultures and creative communities of contemporary West Cork and beyond. The programme begins at the Rock Amphitheatre with local talent Múiris, before moving to Ár n-Áit for an eclectic evening of music. Cork drummer and composer Dan Walsh brings FIXITY, his acclaimed experimental project where free jazz, rock, noise and improvisation collide. Dublin’s Living Things bring their genre-defying Afro-soul sound, fusing Afropunk energy, progressive grooves and soul. Formed by musicians from diverse cultural and musical backgrounds, their music is built around groove, connection and a shared belief in music’s ability to bring people together. The evening culminates with Yankari Afrobeat Collective, led by Nigerian composer and bandleader Segun Akano. Their high-energy sound draws on Nigerian musical traditions, combining driving Afrobeat rhythms with jazz-infused horns, guitars, organ and voices. Yankari have performed at Cork Jazz Festival, All Together Now and TradFest, and appeared on RTÉ’s Tommy Tiernan Show and Radio 1’s Arena. title: An Evening of Poetry and Music with the Innyside Singers
description:
Music and poetry lovers are in for a treat this Culture Night, when The Innyside Singers, a versatile mixed-voice choir from Ballymahon, present ‘An Evening of Poetry and Music’ in the historic surroundings of The Goldsmith Room, Ballymahon Library.

The choir will perform a rich and varied programme, ranging from songs in the Irish language and stirring modern choral pieces to the ever-popular songs of Percy French. They will be joined by a group of local traditional musicians whose lively jigs and reels are sure to have toes tapping. Between the music, the evening will be woven through with poetry inspired by our Irish heritage.

Many of the songs will be old favourites with choruses to join in on, and the audience will be warmly encouraged to sing along throughout the night. More than a concert, this is an invitation to come together, to share in something familiar and joyful, and to celebrate the songs, tunes and verses that have been handed down through the generations.

Admission is free and everyone is welcome, and the Goldsmith Room is fully wheelchair accessible. Whether you come to listen, to sing, or simply to enjoy the company, this promises to be a heartfelt tribute to – and celebration of – our wonderful cultural heritage. We look forward to welcoming you.

Beidh lucht ceoil agus filíochta i leataobh le haghaidh cóisir spraoiúil an Oíche Cultúir seo, nuair a chuirfidh The Innyside Singers, cor idirghnéasca ilghutha ó Bhaile Uí Mhatháin, ‘Oíche Filíochta agus Ceoil’ i láthair i suíomh stairiúil Seomra an Óir, Leabharlann Bhaile Uí Mhatháin. Beidh clár saibhir agus éagsúil á sheinm ag an gcor, ó amhráin sa Ghaeilge agus píosaí chorla nua-aimseartha spreagúla go dtí amhráin shuaimhneacha Percy French.

Beidh grúpa ceoltóirí traidisiúnta áitiúla leo, a bhfuil a n-imeachtaí beoga agus rithimeanna cinnte go gcuirfidh siad cluas mhór ag preabadh. Idir na ceoil, beidh filíocht spreagtha ag ár n-oidhreacht Éireannach á hathléiriú tríd an oíche. Beidh go leor de na hamhráin ina sean-réimeanna is fearr le rannchuidiú ag an lucht éisteachta, agus spreagfar an lucht féachana go fonnmhar chun canadh leo tríd an oíche. Níos mó ná ceolchoirm amháin é seo; is cuireadh é teacht le chéile, rud éigin eolach agus sona a roinnt, agus ceol, melóidí agus véarsaí atá á n-iompar tríd na glúine a cheiliúradh.

Tá an t-iontráil saor in aisce agus tá fáilte roimh cách, agus tá Seomra Goldsmith lán-inrochtana do dhaoine ar chathaoireacha rothaí. Cibé an téann tú chun éisteacht, chun canadh, nó díreach chun taitneamh a bhaint as an gcomhluadar, geallann sé seo a bheith ina ómós d’ár n-oidhreacht chultúrtha iontach agus ina cheiliúradh uirthi. Táimid ag súil le fáilte a chur romhat.

A multi-instrumentalist, accomplished singer-songwriter and no stranger to the old songs, Ger has recorded 12 songs from the Bailebhúirne Song Collection made by A.Martin Freeman in 1913-14: one of our most important collections of traditional song, contaning gems of song like the well-known ‘Aisling Geal’  and brought back to the people of Múscraí Gaeltacht by Seán Ó’ Riada in the 1960’s.

Come and join Ger and a gost of other musicians…. celebrating Culture Night this September 18th for a great evening of music and song in An Tigin……

“Ger Wolfe is the Dylan Thomas of Cork in the singular sincerity and purity of his words” (Seán Mac Carthy)

title: An Evening with Miriam Mulcahy: Walking the Beara Breifne Way
description:
Join acclaimed writer, editor and Irish Times journalist Miriam Mulcahy in conversation with Dorothy Brophy as they explore the discoveries made about landscape, history, time, art and self during Miriam’s remarkable 700km journey along the Beara Breifne Way, from Cork to Cavan.

Miriam’s latest book, Walking to the Foot of the Sky (2026), chronicles her experience of walking this historic trail over three seasons. Part memoir, part exploration of nature, history and place, the book captures the beauty and significance of some of Ireland’s lesser-known landscapes while reflecting on an inward journey of personal discovery. Following both the physical line of the walk from south to north and an internal line of reflection, Miriam considers themes of belonging, memory, technology, creativity and the passage of time.

A bestselling author whose debut book, This is My Sea, was nominated for an Irish Book Award and named an Irish Times Book of the Year, Miriam brings her keen eye for storytelling and observation to this engaging discussion. Together, Miriam and Dorothy will reflect on what it means to walk through a landscape with attention and curiosity, and how a long journey can deepen our understanding of Ireland, its history and ourselves.

Spaces are limited. Booking through Castletownbere Library in person or by phone on (027) 70233

Miriam Mulcahy is a writer, editor and journalist, contributing to The Irish Times. Her debut non-fiction, This is My Sea published in 2023 with Eriu / Bonnier was a no 1 bestseller, nominated for an Irish Book Award and was an Irish Times book of the year. Her second book, Walking to the Foot of the Sky, published in May 2026, is an account of how she walked the Beara Breifne Way, a historical trail of 700km through Ireland over three seasons. A memoir about walking, nature, history, time, technology and art, it captures the stunning and resounding beauty of lesser-known parts of Ireland, and centres on the following of two lines, the line of the walk from south to north and an internal line of discovery within the author.

title: ARCHIVE!!! PUBLISHING !!! PING-PONG!!!
description:
Isn’t counter culture still culture?

Pop by and argue the case with our brand-new, for one-day, and one-day-only, publishing studio. The co-directors have been pouring blood, sweat and tears into reviving the 33-year archive of Catalyst, and we can’t keep COUNTER CULTURE PHENOMENA OF BELFAST to ourselves.

At its core is the rejuvenated archive, reimagined by the co-directors as a series of faux newspapers printed directly onto wooden boxes. These boxes are not just for display, but function as sites of absurdity and experimentation. Arranged in configurations, they will become ping-pong tables, introducing a layer of irony where play, print, and counterculture can collide.

The space expands into three stations forming our temporary publishing studio: a writing station, where participants can contribute short, surreal, or silly stories; a doodle station for spontaneous visual creations and illustrations; and the third station is a surprise activation, an evolving dept. designed to respond to the energy of the night.

Throughout the evening, we’ll be collecting the contributions, which will be curated into a freshly assembled newspaper documenting Counter-Culture Night 2026. There will only be two editions produced: one for the organisers of culture night, and one to go straight into the Catalyst Archive (after being carefully catalogued, of course).

title: Argentine Tango Experience
description:
Discover the world of Argentine Tango through a unique immersive experience presented for Culture Night 2026.
This event offers an engaging introduction to one of Argentina’s most celebrated cultural traditions. Doors open at 5pm – Visitors will explore a photographic exhibition of authentic milongas in Buenos Aires and a short video presentation (starting at 5.15pm) tracing tango’s journey from its origins in the city’s immigrant neighbourhoods to its worldwide recognition as a living cultural expression.

The experience continues at 6pm with a 90 minutes Argentine Tango class for complete beginners. No previous dance experience or partner is required. Participants will be introduced to the fundamental elements of tango, including connection, musicality, posture, and partner communication, in a welcoming and supportive environment.

Following the class, guests are invited to experience a milonga, the social heart of Argentine Tango. Members of Ireland’s tango community will be present, creating an authentic atmosphere where visitors can watch, participate, dance, or simply enjoy the music and social interaction. Everyone is welcome.

Organised by Lucia & Gerry, Corresponding Academicians of the National Tango Academy of Argentina, with more than 20 years of experience teaching and promoting Argentine Tango through their unique multidisciplinary tango school.
Experience tango as a vibrant cultural tradition that brings people together through music, movement, and community.

title: Art Workshop: A Creative Exploration of Celtic Mythology through painting, printing and clay modelling
description:
1st workshop session: 5pm-6:30 pm
2nd workshop session: 6:30pm-8pm

Art making workshop (divided in two sessions of one hour and a half each) for people to explore the mediums of paint, print and clay around the themes of Celtic mythology and biodiversity. Our project focuses on a multi-media exploration of Irish mythology and Ogham alphabet in relation to human’s deep-rooted connection to the natural environment. Celtic mythology celebrates the intrinsic belief that all of nature’s elements, from mountains to rivers, trees to stones, plants to animals and humans, are interconnected. This symbiotic spiritual relationship is embedded in myths and rituals which once formed an essential part of people’s lives. This legacy lives on through Ireland’s active environmental policy making within the European Union.

Seisiún 1: 5pm-6:30 pm

title: Art Workshop: Surrealist Universe
description:
The Instituto Cervantes invites Culture Night guests on an artistic journey filled with imagination, colour, and creativity for children aged 5 to 10.

Through the work of Maruja Mallo, Remedios Varo, Ángeles Santos, and Frida Kahlo, participants will get to know extraordinary women who transformed their dreams, emotions, and ideas into unique works of art. Children will discover their stories, explore some of their most surprising creations, and delve into the magical universe of surrealism.

The workshop will use different materials and techniques to shape original works, inspired by fantasy, nature, and imagination—without limits and letting creativity take flight.

It is a workshop designed to look at art with fresh eyes, discover the legacy of great artists, and enjoy creating in a playful, inspiring, and participatory environment.

title: Arthur Duignan in conversation with Noel Molloy
description:
A talk with Artist Noel Molloy and Arthur Duignan on Noel Molloy’s development of his Art Practice in Roscommon and related topics plus the 25th Anniversary of Roscommon Arts Center and its beginnings / development and the parties involved.

Arthur Duignan

Originally from Main St Roscommon, now happily retired in Shankill Dublin, Arthur started a design and publishing company in the 1980s and went on to manage Ireland’s premier arts centre in the 1990s. In 1994 he joined Create (then CAFE) as a Project Manager and over 30+ years helped design and deliver innovative collaborative and socially engaged arts projects at local national and EU level, including training arts trainers, producing the Irish Fundraising Handbook, devolving the Artist in Community Scheme, fostering a specialist library & archive, and providing admin, research, financial and moral support to many artists and producers, including fellow Rossie and friend the late Jacinta Lynch and Broadstone Studios.

Noel Molloy

Since the late 70s, Roscommon multidisciplinary artist Noel Molloy has made strange, challenging works out of found objects and domestic detritus. Visit his website

https://www.noelmolloyart.com/ and you’ll find contorted scrap metal sculptures of soldiers, dancers, kings and bears. You’ll see an Irish flag, painted across three bottles of holy water. You’ll see a baby’s pram, crudely repurposed into a sort of military vehicle. A rusty mask will stare back at you with a grotesque metallic grin.

title: Arthur Miller’s Elegy For A Lady
description:
Shed by the Road brings Tennessee Williams’ poignant one-act drama Elegy for a Lady to the stage in an intimate and emotionally charged production. Set within a doctor’s waiting room, the play unfolds through a chance encounter between a celebrated writer and a determined woman seeking answers from her past. As memories surface and long-held truths emerge, Williams explores themes of loss, regret, love, and the enduring power of human connection.

Rich in poetic language and emotional depth, Elegy for a Lady is a moving reflection on missed opportunities and the fragile nature of memory. This compelling production by Shed by the Road invites audiences into a world where past and present collide, revealing the complexities of relationships and the resilience of the human spirit.

A thoughtful and captivating evening of theatre, Elegy for a Lady offers a rare opportunity to experience one of Tennessee Williams’ lesser-known yet deeply affecting works.

title: Arts Alive: Connect & Celebrate Culture Night 2026 at Siamsa Tire
description:
For Culture Night 2026, Siamsa Tire will activate the venue as a vibrant, accessible and inclusive cultural hub, presenting a diverse programme of performances, workshops and participatory activities that celebrate creativity, community and cultural expression. designed to engage audiences of all ages and backgrounds, the programme will provide free opportunities to experience, explore and participate in a wide range of artistic disciplines including circus, music, theatre, dance,
literature, visual arts and craft. Circus acts will add a playful high energy element that will animate the building and create a sense of excitement throughout the evening. The Literary Lounge Unplugged Open Mic will provide an inclusive platform for writers, poets, actors and emerging talent to share original work and allow participation from attendees.

The Indian Association will present a showcase of traditional dance celebrating cultural diversity and promote intercultural understanding within local community. Next Stage Theatre Kerry in collaboration with MTU choir will present a youth led ensemble performance, creating opportunities for young people to develop and showcase their artistic talents. NEWKD will facilitate knitting, crochet and craft workshops led by professional artists, encouraging active participation from attendees. a family friendly puppet theatre performance will introduce younger audiences to live theatre, while Irish dance workshops will provide an accessible and enjoyable introduction to Irelands rich dance heritage.

By combining high quality artistic programming with meaningful opportunities for participation, Arts Alive will foster community connection, support cultural inclusion and encourage audiences to experience the arts in new and accessible ways. The programme reflects the core aims of Culture Night by removing barriers to participation, showcasing local talent and creating shared cultural experiences that bring people together through the arts.

This event forms part of Cultúr 2026: Sharing Ireland’s Culture, the national cultural programme for Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union, and is supported by the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport through Culture Ireland.

title: Arts Council Collection Showcase
description:
For Culture night 2026 the Arts Council will proudly showcase a selection of works from its extensive visual art Collection.

The Arts Council Collection was established in 1962 and now comprises over 1,400 works of modern and contemporary Irish art.

This year they are delighted to once again welcome audiences to the Arts Council buildings on Merrion Square, Dublin to engage with a new display of collection works spanning a period from 1978 to 2024.

Works by many of Ireland’s leading artists will be shown on the night including pieces by: Tinka Berchert, Gabhann Dunne, Mary Farl Powers, Richard Gorman, Patrick Hall, Catriona Leahy, Anne Madden, Theresa McKenna, William McKeown, Paul O’Keefe, Casey Walshe and Ruby Wallis.

As well as this glimpse into the Arts Council Collection for Culture Night, artworks can be seen all year round throughout the country as part of exhibitions and long-term loans in public buildings such as hospitals, universities and schools.

title: As I Lay Dreaming
description:
Using spoken word and music, visitors will be given a sneak preview of extracts from a new play that will tour four Donegal venues in October. As I Lay Dreaming is a poignant memory play by Shaun Byrne, centred on Annie McGinley, a Donegal woman reflecting on the news of American artist Rockwell Kent’s death in 1971. Kent spent four months in the Gleann Choilm Cille area, immersed in its culture, community and landscape. The narrative weaves between the present of 1971, Kent’s nostalgic 1958 return and the idyllic summer of 1926 when he first arrived in the remote valley of Glenlough.

The project is supported by the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport through the Local Authority Commemorative Fund 2026.

title: Athenry in Colour
description:
Athenry in Colour is a relaxed drop-in art session inviting participants to creatively reinterpret Athenry’s heritage and historic landmarks through expressive colour and drawing.
Using prepared outline illustrations and visual references inspired by local sites such as Athenry Castle, the Abbey, and the town’s historic buildings, participants will be encouraged to experiment with bold, imaginative colour choices and create their own unique interpretations rather than focusing on realistic representation.
During the session, Tanya McGarry will also demonstrate her artistic process, showing how colour, composition, and expressive techniques can be used to transform familiar places and create a more vibrant interpretation of the town.
The workshop explores how colour can transform familiar heritage spaces and encourages people to look at Athenry from a fresh and creative perspective. The activity is designed to be welcoming and accessible to all ages and abilities, with an emphasis on imagination, participation, and enjoyment of the creative process.
Alongside the workshop, a small exhibition of Tanya McGarry’s Athenry-inspired artworks will be displayed in the library, celebrating the town’s character, history, and visual identity.

title: Backwater Artists Group: Studio Tours and Artist Talks
description:
Join Backwater Artists Group for an opportunity to explore artists’ studios and visit the Studio 12 gallery.

Studio Tours
Take part in guided half-hour tours of artists’ studios, offering a rare glimpse inside working studio spaces, meet resident artists, and hear directly about their practices and day-to-day creative lives.

Tours will take place at 5pm, 5.40pm, 6.20pm and 7pm. Booking is essential.

Studio 12 Gallery (no booking required)
The Studio 12 gallery will be open throughout the evening, where you can visit Room Innate by Backwater Moving Image Bursary recipient Danny Foley. From 6.30–7.30pm, Danny will be present in the gallery to meet visitors and share insights
into the exhibition and his wider practice.

Room Innate explores artistic play as a creative strategy for negotiating the self as shapeshifting, multifaceted and inherently vulnerable. The installation brings together black-and-white paintings on canvas, stop-motion video, re-edited archival footage
from Foley’s childhood and small-scale clay sculptures. Through making, experimentation and repetition, Foley engages with uncertainty, doubt and ambiguity rather than seeking to resolve them.

“We are delighted to welcome visitors to Wandesford Quay on Culture Night and to share what we do. Visitors will experience studio tours, exhibitions, workshops, poetry readings and more.”

title: Bantry: A Mirror to Its Past (Part 2)
description:
Step back in time and rediscover Bantry through the archive collection of renowned local photographer Ian Vickery, whose photographic archive has captured the people, places, events and everyday life of the town over many decades. Ian’s collection forms a remarkable visual record of a changing Bantry, preserving moments that might otherwise have been lost to time. 

On Culture Night, Friday, September 18th, visitors are invited to view over 50 photographs from the Ian Vickery Photographic Collection, showcasing familiar faces, community celebrations, local businesses, streetscapes and scenes of daily life from Bantry’s recent past. The exhibition offers a unique opportunity to reflect on how the town has evolved while celebrating the people and memories that helped shape its character.

The exhibition will be open until 7.30pm on Culture Night and will remain on display afterwards in the foyer of Bantry Library, allowing the wider community to enjoy this fascinating glimpse into Bantry’s rich social and cultural heritage.

Whether you are searching for a familiar face, recalling a bygone era, or discovering Bantry’s history for the first time, Bantry: A Mirror to Its Past, Part 2 promises a nostalgic and engaging journey through the town’s collective memory.

title: Barrack Street Concert Band
description: The Barrack Street Concert Band has been making music in Waterford since its formation in 1870 in the Mount Sion Christian Brothers School on Barrack Street. In those 156 years, the Band has played on through two world wars, and numerous changes of premises and a long parade of members. The Band has remained popular with the people of Waterford across the generations, and this living heritage continues today with two or three generations of several families continuing in the footsteps of their great-grandparents. The Barrack Street Concert Band is one of Waterford’s living treasures, playing a regular part in the cultural and leisure life of the city and lending its considerable musical skills to local charities and organisations. title: Bee Signs: Buzzing for Biodiversity
description:
On Culture Night, Athy Sing and Sing are planning to organise a creative and engaging event focused on bees and their importance for biodiversity and the wider ecosystem, using Irish Sign Language (ISL) as a central part of the experience. This year also marks the 100-year anniversary of Winnie the Pooh by A.A. Milne, and the event will take inspiration from that world, bringing in a sense of storytelling, nature, and imagination.
The activity will bring together environmental awareness, creativity, and communication in a way that is accessible and enjoyable. Participants will work together to create a large bumble bee as a shared visual piece, helping to set the theme and provide a strong creative starting point.
At the beginning, they will introduce simple ISL signs linked to bees and nature, such as bee, flower, plants, food, help, protect, grow, and earth. These will be taught in a relaxed, interactive way to build confidence and encourage participation.
Participants will then work in small groups to create short stories about bees, such as following a bee collecting nectar and helping plants grow, or exploring what might happen if bees disappeared and how people can help protect them.
These stories will be shared through ISL, movement, and expression rather than spoken words, making the activity inclusive for both deaf and hearing participants. At the end, groups will present their work and reflect on what they have learned. Overall, the event highlights the importance of bees and encourages everyone to play a role in protecting biodiversity.
fullAddress: Athy Youth Café, Meeting Lane, Athy, County Kildare, Ireland

This Culture Night event at Daughters of Charity Community Services uncovers how the iconic mansions of the wealthy were transformed into bustling, crowded tenement homes. 

Come along for a fascinating look at these deeply contrasting eras. Explore how daily life, work, and community evolved within these historic structures.

Architecture & Memory: Discover how the classical columns and fanlights of the Georgian era framed the lives of the newly independent state’s citizens.

Census Secrets: Dive into the details of the 1926 Census records and uncover the stories of the people who occupied these iconic Dublin streets.

This event will launch the artist book Beyond the Ditch, Beside the Road, from visual artist Marie Phelan.

The publication was created to mark the land based film screening of her short film Me&You&Us&Them, that took place on Culture Night 2025 in a field at Kilcumney Cross along the Borris to Bagenalstown road, site of a battle during the 1798 Rebellion.

During the book launch there will be a combination of readings and conversations that consider the publication, and the film, reflecting on memory and how a place like a field sits within the thinking of those who inhabit it, or pass it by. Tea and biscuits will be served.

This publication features invited essays from writer and curator Catherine Marshall, who will join the conversation on Culture Night, and Rosie O’Gorman, artist and director of Cow House Studios.

title: Beyond The Lake
description:
Beyond The Lake, a new book of words and images will be launched on Culture Night with readings by members of the Oughterard Writers Group. Hosted by Pete Mullineaux.

Join Oughterard Writers Group to celebrate the launch of their new collection of poetry and images. Beyond the Lake is an anthology of words and images that express multiple reflections, perceptions and inspirations that have resulted from encounters with our wonderful Lough Corrib. There is celebration and gratitude for what the lake and its surroundings offer and teach us, as well as concern for its wellbeing in facing challenges such as pollution and the impact of global warming. The book focuses on the importance of the lake for humans and non-humans, holding an ear to its past, present and future.
This event will be hosted by Pete Mullineaux who will launch the book and introduce the readers.

title: Black History Walking Tour of Dublin
description:
Discover over 300 years of Black history in Dublin on a unique guided walking tour created by design historian, researcher and anti-racism activist Jess Majekodunmi. Presented as part of Culture Night Dublin 2026, the tour traces the often overlooked presence of Black people in the city from the eighteenth century to the present day. 

Drawing on archival research and personal family history, the tour reveals how Black Irish stories are woven into the fabric of the city. The walk follows stories of performers, writers, students and activists whose lives were connected to Dublin’s streets and landmarks. Stops include Temple Bar, College Green, Trinity College, O’Connell Bridge and Grafton Street. 

This two-hour walk offers a fresh perspective on Dublin’s past and highlights the rich diversity that has shaped the capital for centuries.

Two tours will run on Culture Night at 16:00 and 18:30. It covers a compact, walkable route of approximately 2km taking in Christchurch, Temple Bar, College Green, Trinity College, O’Connell Bridge, and Grafton Street.

This tour requires advance booking. It begins outside the Lord Edward pub, 23 Christchurch Place, D08 RK00.

 

Filming and photography may be taking place at this event. By attending we assume permission unless a member of our team is explicitly notified.

title: Boheh Stone with Emily Bracken
description:
Join us for a Culture Night ‘Design Charette’ led by Emily Bracken, ATU School of Creative Arts. Part-talk and part hands-on-workshop inspired by Mayo’s ancient Boheh Stone, which stands as a vital piece of our rich, pre-colonial cultural landscape. This famous monument contains beautiful carvings relating to the sun. Considered to be one of Ireland’s best collections of petroglyphs (prehistoric rock carvings), the Boheh contains over 250 motifs. It is believed to date back to around 3,800BC!

A ‘Design Charette’ brings people together to explore design options in a fun enjoyable way. Come along to learn more about Mayo’s prehistoric rock art, protecting our indigenous heritage, and let’s imagine new design solutions to engage the public by incorporating local needs, culture, rituals and tradition.

No experience necessary. All Welcome.

About the host
Emily Bracken teaches Interior Design at ATU School of Creative Arts, Galway. Her perspective is heavily shaped by over 20 years managing complex, large-scale commercial and public infrastructure projects within multidisciplinary teams. As an NCIDQ and BIID registered interior designer, she has spent decades looking at how space can reflect community identity and culture—most notably during a formative decade delivering remote infrastructure alongside Indigenous communities in Canada. Her focus now is bringing those international lessons home to Irish design.
Culture Night is strategically funded by Mayo County Council and the Arts Council and is supported by Creative Ireland and participating groups & venues in Mayo.
fullAddress: The Linenhall, Linenhall Street, Knockthomas, Castlebar, County Mayo, Ireland

The bags contain gems from different genres: the free treasures could be a great story, poems, an audio book, a music CD, a history book or a book on art.

After they have picked their bag, Culture Night visitors can browse the shelves of the Goethe-Institut Irland’s library. This beautiful space with a spectacular ceiling and cosy seating is open to the public and offers a wide range of media in German or English translation – including a corner just for kids and young adults. On Culture Night, visitors can apply for their free library card and borrow language learning material, movies, books, and more.

description:

title: Bray’s Hidden Gems & Secrets
description:
Join this team of passionate local guides who know Bray inside and out. and more importantly, who love sharing that knowledge.

Each walk is crafted to feel less like a lecture and more like a conversation – relaxed, engaging, and full of surprising details you won’t find in a guidebook.

Whether you’re visiting for the first time or rediscovering Bray from a fresh perspective, the goal is simple: to help you see the town differently.
To slow down, take it in, and connect with the place in a meaningful way.
Join us for a walk — and let Bray tell its story.

Today it’s known as a seaside resort and commuter town, but Bray’s history stretches back thousands of years. The area has evidence of human activity dating back to prehistoric times and even has links to the Romans. The name “Bray” is believed to come from the Irish Brí Chualann, meaning “hill of Cualu”, referring to the nearby headland known as Bray Head.

title: Broken Record’s RPM Series: Planxty – The Black Album Listening Party
description:
Newbridge has played an important role in Ireland’s musical story, yet this heritage is not always celebrated as widely as it deserves. This special Culture Night event shines a light on that legacy through a communal listening experience centred on Planxty’s landmark self-titled debut album.
Hosted by music broadcaster Joe Donnelly, the evening will feature a complete playback of the album through a high-quality sound system, allowing audiences to hear the music in a shared and immersive setting. Alongside the listening session, invited guests will discuss the album’s creation, its musical influences, its enduring cultural significance and the connections of Planxty members Donal Lunny, Christy Moore, Liam O’Flynn and Andy Irvine to Newbridge and the wider Kildare area.
The event invites both long-time fans and newcomers to discover why Planxty remains one of the most influential groups in Irish music. Through storytelling, discussion and collective listening, audiences will gain a deeper appreciation of Irish folk traditions, the evolution of contemporary Irish music and the contribution of local communities to Ireland’s cultural life.
Complementing the listening event, audiences can explore a curated exhibition of Planxty photographs and memorabilia before concluding the evening with a DJ set celebrating the breadth and diversity of Kildare’s musical heritage, connecting Planxty’s legacy with the county’s vibrant musical story.
Free and open to all, the event encourages participation, conversation and cultural discovery while celebrating Newbridge’s place within Ireland’s rich musical heritage.

title: Caomhnú Lú – For the Birds
description:
Debuting as part of Boyne TradFest 2026, Caomhnú Lú – For the Birds,
is a newly commissioned work by composer Donnchadh MacAodha.
“For the Birds” is a musical response to the birdlife of County Louth in
2025, drawing on the Louth Bird Report and its record of activity along
the county’s coastline over a twelve-month period. Dundalk Bay and the
wider Louth coast are vital habitats for the many species that pass through
and settle here, and this piece meditates on the fragility of that world in
the face of climate change. Bird calls and songs are evoked throughout,
tracking the arrival and departure of different species from spring to
winter.
This event also features solo harp performances & discussion with local
activists on climate change, and is hosted by Music Generation Louth
Harp Ensemble & Harp Ireland.

This free event offers a unique opportunity to discover and reflect on the history, traditions and identity that have shaped our area while sharing in the spirit of Culture Night, a nationwide celebration of creativity, heritage and community. Light refreshments will be served, and all are warmly welcome.
fullAddress: Castlemagner, County Cork, Ireland

title: Castletown Culture Night Celebration
description:
Following the outstanding success of last year’s Culture Night, Castletown Tidy Towns returns with another memorable community celebration. Building on the warm response and record attendance, this year’s expanded programme will shine a light on even more local creativity.

In partnership with Evengy, the community will take part in workshops to create larger artistic sculptures for the Slí Shibhéal Walkway. Illuminated especially for Culture Night, these pieces will transform the route into an atmospheric outdoor gallery.

The amphitheatre stage area will once again be beautifully lit, creating a magical setting for local performances. The programme will feature four local acts, including a singer, a traditional Irish music group, a teenage vocalist and pupils from Castletown Primary School.

Bringing together art, music, light and community, the evening invites all generations to experience the creativity and welcome of Castletown.

genres.title: Visual Arts (Painting, Photography, sculpture, Digital Art, Print, etc)

title: Cathedral Quarter Night Market
description:
Culture Night | Cathedral Quarter Night Market

One night. One square. One not to miss!

For one of Belfast’s biggest nights of the year, Writer’s Square transforms into a bustling open-air night market at the heart of the Cathedral Quarter.

Cathedral Quarter Night Market brings together an exciting mix of independent makers, artists, street food, speciality drinks, performers and Live DJ’s for an evening of browsing, eating, drinking and discovering something new.

With glowing lights, great food, incredible local talent and the unmistakable energy that only Belfast can create after dark. Whether you’re taking a break between Culture Night venues, meeting friends for the evening, or simply exploring the city, the Night Market offers the perfect place to gather, shop local and soak up the atmosphere.

Good food. Great people. Great Night.

Writer’s Square, Cathedral Quarter, Belfast
fullAddress: Writer's Square, Belfast, UK

title: Cathedral Quarter Open Office
description:
Celebrate Culture Night with a free open evening at the Letterkenny Cathedral Quarter Office, home to an extensive collection of local heritage materials charting the history and development of the area.

Browse historic photographs, newspaper articles, exhibition posters, maps and memorabilia showcasing the Cathedral Quarter’s rich heritage.

Volunteers will be on hand throughout the evening to share the stories behind the collections and highlight ongoing work to preserve and promote Letterkenny’s history.

6.00pm – 9.00pm
fullAddress: Letterkenny Cathedral Quarter, Church Lane, Letterkenny, County Donegal, Ireland

title: Cathy’s Call
description:
Inspired by Kate Bush’s iconic Wuthering Heights, this large-scale participatory performance invites the public to become part of a haunting sea of dancers dressed in red. Throughout the evening, participants will be guided through a simplified version of the famous choreography, with instructions delivered in both Gaeilge and English, creating a playful and accessible introduction to movement and language.

Drawing inspiration from Kate Bush’s Irish roots and her connection to Belfast, the event blends music, performance, community participation and spectacle in a uniquely Belfast way. Elements inspired by Running Up That Hill will also feature, creating moments of gathering, movement and collective energy throughout the experience.

No dance experience is required and audiences are welcome to join at any point. Whether you come to dance, watch or simply soak up the atmosphere, Cathy’s Call offers a joyful, surreal and unforgettable Culture Night experience.

Red clothing is encouraged but not essential.
venueName: Saltwater Square (outside Belfast Grand Central Station)
fullAddress: Grand Central Station, Belfast, UK

title: Ceilí na nÓg
description:
Live music from children/family & friends of our dance school .All ages groups welcome (Intergenerational event)

Irish supper served

Join us for a heartwarming Ceilí na nÓg, where tradition, community and friendship come together in the heart of our rural community.

Hosted by the Browne–McGranaghan Academy of Irish Dance, this special intergenerational event welcomes children, parents, grandparents and friends of all ages to enjoy an evening of music, laughter and togetherness. Whether you’re stepping onto the dance floor for the first time or reliving cherished memories, everyone is welcome.

Enjoy a delicious traditional Irish supper, while Niamh McGranaghan, Bean an Tí, and the talented dancers of the Browne–McGranaghan Academy of Irish Dance guide you through basic Irish dance steps and fun, easy céilí dances that everyone can join in. No experience is needed—just bring your enthusiasm!

Come along to celebrate our rich Irish heritage, make new connections, create lasting memories and experience the warmth of true Irish hospitality. We look forward to welcoming you for an evening filled with music, dancing, conversation and community spirit.

Bígí linn le haghaidh Ceilí na nÓg croíúil, áit a mbailíonn traidisiún, pobal agus cairdeas le chéile i gcroílár ár bpobail thuaithe.

Arna óstáil ag Acadamh Rince Gaelach Browne-McGranaghan, cuireann an t-imeacht speisialta idirghlúineach seo fáilte roimh leanaí, tuismitheoirí, seanathar agus seanmháthair agus cairde de gach aois chun sult a bhaint as oíche cheoil, gháire agus mhuintearas. Is cuma má tú ar an urlár damhsa den chéad uair nó ag athmhúscailt cuimhní dílse, tá fáilte roimh gach duine.

Bain sult as dinnéar traidisiúnta blasta Éireannach, agus Niamh McGranaghan, Bean an Tí, agus na rinceoirí ealaíonta ón Acadamh Rince Gaelach Browne-McGranaghan do do threorú trí chéimeanna bunúsacha rince Gaelach agus trí chéilí spraíúil simplí  ar féidir le gach duine páirt a ghlacadh ann. Níl aon taithí ag teastáil- ní ga ach do dhíograis a thabhairt leat!

Bígí linn chun ár n-oidhreacht shaibhir Éireannach a cheiliúradh, nascanna nua a dhéanamh, cuimhní buana a chruthú agus croíúlact fíor óstachais na hÉireann a bhlaiseadh. Táimid ag tnúth le fáilte a chur romhat le haghaidh oíche lán de cheol, dhamhsa, chomhra agus spiorad pobail.
host: Browne-Mc Granaghan Academy of Irish Dance

title: Ceiliúradh ar Ealaíontóirí Taibhsín
description:
This Culture Night, An Taibhdhearc throws open its doors and welcomes people into the theatre to experience the work in-progress of its Taibhsín artists, with a celebration of a year spent dreaming, writing and making at the National Irish Language Theatre.

The free event gives audiences a first look at works in progress by some of the artists supported through Taibhsín, An Taibhdhearc’s development programme for artists working professionally in the Irish language.

New stories will move from page to stage for the first time with works in progress from Ciara Ní É, Louisa Ní Éidean and Seán Mac Dhonnagáin, alongside a new spoken-word piece as Gaeilge, Litir do Mhacasamhail, by Ola Majekodunmi.

Directed by Em Ball / O’Ceallaigh with a cast that includes Ann Marie Horan and Diarmuid de Faoite, Taibhsín: Ó Bhrionglóid go Beo offers audiences the chance to encounter these works at a pivotal moment – as they make the leap from development to performance. Audiences are welcome to attend the entire evening or for individual performances.

Ar Oíche Chultúir i mbliana, beidh doirse na Taibhdheirce ar oscailt agus beidh fáilte roimh dhaoine teacht chun saothair atá á gcruthú ag na healaíontóirí atá mar chuid de Taibhsín a fheiceáil, le ceiliúradh ar an mbliain atá caite acu ag brionglóideach, ag scríobh agus ag cruthú san Amharclann Náisiúnta na Gaeilge.

Beidh an t-imeacht saor in aisce agus beidh deis ag an lucht féachana breathnú ar shaothair atá cruthaithe ag na healaíontóirí atá mar chuid de Taibhsín, an clár forbartha d’ealaíontóirí na Taibhdheirce, do scríbhneoirí, d’amharclannóirí agus d’ealaíontóirí taibhithe atá ag obair go gairmiúil i nGaeilge.

Beidh scéalta nua le Ciara Ní É, Louisa Ní Éidean agus Seán Mac Dhonnagáin, agus filíocht ó bhéal as Gaeilge, Litir do Mhacasamhail, le hOla Majekodunmi.

Beidh Em Ball / O’Ceallaigh ag stiúradh agus beidh Ann Marie Horan agus Diarmuid de Faoite mar chuid den chliar. Tugann Taibhsín: Ó Bhrionglóid go Beo deis don lucht féachana an saothar seo a fheiceáil ag uain chinniúnach – agus iad ag bogadh ó fhorbairt go léiriú. Beidh fáilte roimh dhaoine fanacht don imeacht ar fad nó freastal ar léirithe ar leith.

description:
