title: Central Plaza: BENCH-7 | Rat Race by Simone O’Toole
description:
Take a breath. Just be here. Find a moment of joy.

BENCH-7 | Rat Race is a short outdoor solo interrogating the tension between economic survival and artistic freedom. Through repetition, rhythm, and interruption, Simone O’Toole explores the physicality of a body trapped in a 9-to-5 grind. To Kíla’s driving music, exhaustion yields to a joyous, interactive burst of play and connection with passers-by as she surrenders to instinct, movement and the wisdom of her own body. With warmth and a touch of mischief, the work asks what happens when we stop, look up, and remember we’re more than our jobs.

Commissioned by CoisCéim Dance Theatre as part of BENCH, a collection of dance works highlighting everyday spaces as creative places.

 

Simone O’Toole is an Irish Contemporary Dance Artist. She trained at Fontys Dance Academy (Netherlands), subsequently working with Guilhermo Miotto, Catherine Young, John Scott, Fibin Teo and Pan Pan Theatre. As a choreographer, she is the recipient of awards from Arts Council Ireland, Dance Ireland and Backstage Theatre. Her practice is highly collaborative and strongly socially engaged. In 2025, as part of the Perform Europe collaboration, PERFORMING MEMORY, Simone contextualised and localised Sasha Kurmaz’s “Untitled” for an Irish audience, in a groundbreaking participation project. 

 

Image by Mark Henderson

 

This event is part of the Culture Night Dublin programme at Central Plaza. Please note that photography and filming will take place throughout the event. By attending, visitors consent to being photographed or filmed unless they notify a member of the Culture Night Dublin team otherwise.

title: Ceol Ársa Cláirsí – A Celebration of Irish Harp Music from the 17th & 18th Centuries
description:
Step into the rich and atmospheric world of early Irish harpers’ music with Ceol Ársa Cláirsí, a musical experience that brings the unique sound of the 17th and 18th centuries vividly to life. This performance showcases the music of legendary harper-composers such as Turlough Carolan, Thomas Connellan, and Ruairí Dall Ó Catháin, taken from original Irish and Scottish sources.
Featuring a remarkable ensemble of leading musicians – Cormac Breatnach, Steve Cooney, Aisling Ennis, Malachy Robinson, and Eamon Sweeney – the programme showcases the distinctive textures of gut-strung and wire-strung instruments alongside traditional instrumentation, anchored by the unmistakable voice of the modern Irish harp.
With a sound described by audiences as “unique and mesmerising,” Ceol Ársa Cláirsí offers a rare opportunity to experience Ireland’s harp tradition, and how it has permeated the repertoire, through a historically-informed and immersive performance.

The community, across the generations, are invited to come together in The Book Café i nGuaire from 7pm – 9pm on Oíche Chultúir for an evening of traditional song, music, stories, poetry and dance, while supporting the Irish language.

To open the Ceol Mo Chroí Culture Club 2026, and to mark the 100th year anniversary of the final publication of An tAthair Pádruig Breathnach (1904-1926), traditional singer and folklorist Rachel Uí Fhaoláin will present some of her research outcomes from her Artlink’s 2025 Bursary, local recordings she unearthed pertaining to a repertoire of 1798 Wexford Ballads that she has been working on from the songbooks of An tAthair Pádruig Breathnach. The sharing of this important material back into the community of North Wexford and an opportunity for participants to learn these local songs, will be delivered by Rachel Uí Fhaoláin in collaboration
with family members of the recorded local singers who have since passed.

This is a wonderful opportunity for the community to get involved in the transmission of important cultural material across the generations in Co. Wexford. Fáilte roimh chách!

title: Christchurch Bellringing
description:
Come visit the Bell Tower at Waterford’s
Christchurch Cathedral to see the bell
chamber where the ancient tradition of
bellringing happens. Bells have been
ringing in Waterford since the 1600s.
The first mention of bells in Christchurch is
from 1650, when bells were hidden in the
crypt of the cathedral to save them from
being taken as booty by the Cromwellians.
In 1668, six bells were cast and in 1721,
the Bishop of Waterford Rev Thomas Millar
had them recast. In 1872, the set was
completed to give us our current set, a peal
of 8 bells, with the largest bell (the tenor)
weighing just over 1 ton.

 

Tours will be every 15 minutes from outside
the Bell Tower at Christchurch Cathedral.
Due to the size of the tower, numbers will
be restricted to 20 on each tour.

title: Circus Factory: Circus of Selves by Enable Ireland Adult Disability Service
description:
Enable Ireland and Circus Factory Cork co-created A Circus of Selves, to support adults with disabilities to explore identity, expression, and wellbeing through physical theatre. Workshops are taking place now to empower participants to tell their own
stories through creative engagement.

The event will feature a walk-through experience to showcase the project in its entirety.

Visitors will explore the creative process of the participants. Identity Corners, Story Stations and Playful Interaction Areas will help the visitor learn about creating a narrative of self, using costume and props to explore identity within disability.
Participants will showcase their work through a documentary and a display of costumes they created. Photos and written information will communicate the vision behind the project which aims to foster greater visibility of adults with disabilities as
creatives.

The exhibition hopes to deepens understanding of participants’ experiences, and strengthens partnerships between Enable Ireland, local creative organisations and the wider community.

The event culminates in a sharing circle – a relaxed, optional moment where participants can share what they enjoyed from the workshops.

There will be a joyful catwalk around the room with music, finishing with a closing reflection circle with participants, staff, and visitors.

The night aims to be a celebration of identity, creativity, and community.

A Circus of Selves is supported through Cork City Council by the Creative Ireland Programme.

description:
We celebrate 20 years of our group residency at this historic house with a typically eclectic progamme. Please come early – capacity very limited!

We look forward to welcoming Akel at Home to Civic Trust house to feed hungry visitors on Culture Night this year. Weather permitting we will have tables and seating outside, soft drinks also available from the stand.

Come out to play with Crawford Art Gallery. Experiment with drawing, colour and transparencies using old-school overhead projectors. Project artwork from the Gallery collection and introduce your own playful imaginings. All materials supplied.

St. George’s Georgian Orthodox Parish Choir, Cork presents traditional chants from the renowned Gelati School, and Cork Georgian Ensemble presents a selection of songs from the Georgian folk tradition.

6.30-7.30pm Welcome to Civic Trust House
With Artist-in-Residence Cónal Creedon and Building Manager Nicki ffrench Davis. Readings and chat.

7.30-7.45 When I Was God (Play excerpt)
Lost in the Canon Theatre Company presents an excerpt from When I Was God by Cónal Creedon Directed by Niall Holland. It’s FAI Cup Final day. Referee Dino Keegan is retiring from the game. At half-time the spotlight of self-doubt shines directly down on Dino as the ghosts of his past visit him in his dressing room. On the field of dreams the referee is God, but what happens when God is made man?

7.45-8pm Poetry of Tony Desmond
We are delighted to welcome Tony’s brother, Cormac Desmond, to the house to read a selection of Tony’s poetry. Tony Desmond from Turner’s Cross had been a well known figure about town for many years until he moved to China in 2013. Activist, poet, musician and general hell-raiser he was much loved by many and after an accident in
2023 was the subject of a fundraiser to bring him home for rehabilitation in Ireland where he now lives again.

 

8-9pm Launch of Gearr Short Film Festival with Screenings

Launch of a new short film festival resident at the house with film screenings (Gearr takes place 7-11th October).

 

9-10.30 – Cónal Creedon celebration

A selection of short performances and readings with actors Mark D’Aughton, Dominic MacHale, Áine Ní Laoghaire and Alison Teahan.

title: Clay & Culture: Stories in Clay
description:
Discover the Craft. Shape the Story.

Join Leitrim School of Art for a special Culture Night evening exploring the rich connection between ceramics, storytelling and Irish heritage.

Clay has been used for thousands of years to create objects that preserve memories, celebrate traditions and tell stories about people, places and communities.

In this welcoming, hands-on event, you’ll discover how ceramics have played a part in Ireland’s cultural story, from ancient pottery to the work of contemporary Irish ceramic artists.

You’ll then have the opportunity to create your own unique piece using Irish clay, inspired by a personal memory, family tradition, favourite place, local landscape or something that has special meaning to you. With guidance from experienced ceramic tutors, you’ll explore accessible hand-building and decorative techniques to transform your ideas into a personal story in clay.

No previous experience is needed—just curiosity and a willingness to have a go.

Your finished piece will be professionally glazed and kiln-fired and will be available to collect after the event.

Come along, get your hands in the clay, discover something about Ireland’s ceramic heritage and create a piece that tells your story.

title: Clodhoppers Exhibition Opening and Open Studios
description:
Clodhoppers presents recent work by Stradbally-born artist Niamh Coffey, including ceramics, small-scale mixed-media collages, signature textile sculptures and a new hanging textile piece.

Taking its title from Marina Carr’s play The Boy, the exhibition explores our connection to nature and the cosmos through playful, imagined ecological relationships. Drawing on Irish folklore and myth, Coffey brings together forms of flesh, fur, flower and feather across textile, drawing and ceramic work. Scenes of metamorphosis and blurred boundaries create humorous, sometimes uneasy encounters that invite audiences to imagine new ways of living within the wider natural world.

The exhibition coincides with Clodhopper Clodclobber, a commission by Laois Arts Service and Connect Laois, in association with Laois Pride. Created with local LGBTQ+ young people, the project features a series of tufted masks to be worn in the Laois Pride Parade 2026.

Niamh Coffey is a Dublin-based artist working across textiles, drawing and sculpture. Their practice combines ecology, queer theory and Irish folklore to create imagined relationships between people, other beings and the natural world. A 2016 graduate of NCAD’s Sculpture and Expanded Practice programme, Coffey presented their debut solo exhibition, Siúnta, in 2025 at Cultúrlann Belfast, Pallas Projects and Súil Gallery, Co. Clare. Find out more at niamhcoffey.ie.

title: Collage Workshop
description:
The artist Anthony D. Kelly frequently intermingles collage and literary techniques as a way to cross-pollinate inspiration and foster greater creative momentum and flow. The “changing of creative channels” in this way can help plant the seeds for further projects and inspire unexpected directions for creative inquiry.
This 3 hour workshop will begin with the intuitive selection of a prompt word, followed by a short guided visualization that will aid participants in connecting with the rich field of associations, images and potential that can spring from a single word.
From this reflective starting point, Anthony will invite participants to write a short reflective passage to solidify their experiences. He will then lead a hands-on collage session using carefully selected materials, offering gentle guidance on technique and composition as participants develop their work toward a finished piece.
Participants will finish this workshop with new collage techniques, have engaged in a rich sharing of ideas and meaning, and will have direct experience of a technique which can help foster new ideas and create forward momentum even in times of stuckness.”
Participants are welcome to bring a notebook, though this is entirely optional — all other materials will be provided. Participants are advised to dress warmly and bring their own food and drinking water. Tea and Coffee will be provided.

title: Commerce and Conflict: Ireland and Continental Europe, 1550-1650
description:
During Ireland’s turbulent Plantation Era, trade continued to thrive throughout the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries between Ireland and continental Europe from ports such as Castille, Bordeaux, Antwerp and Hamburg.

Irish exports included hides, woollen cloth, linen, salted beef and fish. Imports from Europe encompassed manufactured high-end metalware, playing cards, silk, spices, dyes, wine, salt, lead, brass and iron.

For Culture Night 2026 Claíomh Mobile Museum will present a unique collection of original and museum-grade replica artefacts at Portumna Castle including armour, powder horns, coinage, dyes, ceramics and glassware to demonstrate the links between Ireland, Britain and Continental Europe c. 1550-1650.

title: Confluence
description:
Open air sculpture/ light interactive installation situated in Fr. Burke Park (the dimensions of which will be approximately 2m x 2m x 2m. It will consist of a solid timber frame structure in the shape of two interlocking cubes with a semi-translucent polyvinyl canvas layer stretched across the external frame of the cube. Internally the cube will house a series of LED light strips which will emanate sequences of colour and light patterns through the polyvinyl exterior, creating a visual spectacle that will engage audiences and invite them to contemplate the deeper conceptual meaning of the work. The sculpture is symbolic of the ever evolving nature of culture and identity, and speaks to the strength, diversity and unity that Galway embodies. The idea is that audiences will be confronted with this otherworldly type object emitting light synced to an ambient audio track which will be composed by a local musician and collaborator.

title: Cór Mhagh Ealla with special guests Natasha O’Brien and Shona Murphy
description:
St James’ Church, Mallow will provide a fitting setting for an evening of choral music when Cór Mhagh Ealla takes to the stage, joined by special guests Natasha O’Brien and Shona Murphy.

Founded in Mallow and long regarded as one of North Cork’s leading community choirs, Cór Mhagh Ealla has built a reputation for musical excellence through performances across Munster and beyond. The choir recently achieved further acclaim by winning the Community Choir section at the Limerick Choral Festival and is celebrated for its diverse repertoire, ranging from traditional Irish music and contemporary arrangements to sacred and classical works.

The concert takes place in the beautiful surroundings of St James’ Church, one of Mallow’s most distinctive landmarks. Originally constructed in the 1820s, the church combines striking Gothic architecture with an intimate and atmospheric interior renowned for its warmth, light and exceptional acoustics, making it a much-loved venue for live music and cultural events.

Joining the choir will be local vocalist Shona Murphy, whose rich and expressive voice has become familiar to audiences across the region. Based in Mallow, Shona has established herself as a versatile performer, bringing sensitivity and warmth to every performance.

Special guest Natasha O’Brien will also feature as part of the evening’s programme, adding another unique musical voice to what promises to be a memorable collaboration.

Audiences can look forward to a programme of uplifting choral music, beautiful harmonies and special guest performances in one of Mallow’s most atmospheric venues, making this a highlight of the Culture Night celebrations.

title: Cork Centre for Architectural Education: MARSEILLE: Master in Architecture Exhibition
description:
Discover this year’s Master of Architecture Exhibition. Visitors can expect an array of drawings, models and films that describe new architectural proposals for the city of Marseille.

Surrounded by the Mediterranean and a transit point into Europe from North Africa, Marseille is both a space of crisis and of communication. It is, in a sense, full of contradiction and paradox.

The city has its own epistemic kind of latitude; a strange type of milieu or middle-space between Eastern and Western Europe that hinges and ensnares the populations and spaces of Northern and Southern Africa around it.

The focus this year evolves distinct architectural positions that produced new poetic types of architecture – centred around urban incompletions and alternative natures.

title: Cork City Hall – Atrium: PlaySpaces Pop-Up Trail
description:
After a highly successful summer-long run in venues across Cork City, PlaySpaces comes to City Hall for Culture Night.

PlaySpaces is a multi-year participatory arts project demonstrating genuine child collaboration in civic design.

Beginning in early 2025 with creative workshops at St. Vincent’s Convent Primary School, Blackpool, children imagined child-only spaces through drawing, collage, storytelling and model-making.

The collaboration emerged from Cork Child Friendly City consultancy revealing children’s desire for spaces authentically designed for them. Led by artist Chris Finnegan in partnership with Cork Midsummer Festival, the project expanded in late 2025 to include three Múin Afterschool centres across Cork City, with accessibility consultation from the Crann Centre.

PlaySpaces demonstrates that participatory arts can fundamentally shift children’s relationship with public space and civic life – not through symbolic consultation but through sustained collaboration where young voices genuinely shape outcomes. A public trail of child-designed play spaces launched in summer 2026 across Cork Opera House, The Everyman, St. Peters, Cork City Library and The Lord Mayor’s Pavilion.

A Cork Midsummer Festival production, the project is supported by the Arts Council’s Arts in Early Learning and Childcare Scheme and Cork City Council through Creative Communities Scheme. With support from Sample Studios.

title: Cork City Hall – Concert Hall: The Devil’s In The Dance Hall
description:
‘The Devils in the Dance Hall’ is inspired by the true story of Jimmy Gralton and the suppression of Ireland’s rural dance halls in the early 20th century. Drawing on oral history, folk memory, and the energy of the big-band era, the performance celebrates the collective joy of dance as a form of defiance.
Through spoken word, song, and the roaring sounds of The Gralton Big Band, it tells how Ireland’s old dance halls became centres of community life, offering music, learning, debate, and freedom of expression, until church and state moved to close them down through the introduction of the 1935 Dance Hall Act. As the performance unfolds, the boundary between stage and floor dissolves, and the audience are invited to dance the night away.
Choreographer and creator of the piece Edwina Guckian will teach the gathered audience dance steps across swing, trad, foxtrot, slow sets, sean-nós, lindy hop and set-dance, inviting the audience to dance, move, or observe – providing an
experience for those with dance experience and with none, including people with reduced mobility.
This event is now sold out. Walkups will be accepted where capacity exists.

TUMTHA

Directed by Mary Keane, TUMTHA is a documentary about the Coláistí Ullmhúcháin. These were seven all-Irish second-level boarding schools that were established in the early years of the State to support the revival of the Irish language. Keane interviews the last generation to experience the schools, capturing their memories of their time there and in doing so tells the story of this cultural experiment, as well as showing how language itself shapes identity and memory.

description:
Before Metal: Meet, Make & Chat

Join Cork artist Hannah McGrenera for a relaxed Culture Night evening exploring the beginnings of her creative practice.

Best known for her handcrafted metalwork and jewellery, Hannah will share the quieter origins behind her work — drawing, line, ink and the mindful practice of making.

For the first time, visitors will see Hannah’s original complete line drawing from her Making Home collection, a playful yet thoughtful reflection on Irish life and the everyday moments that make a place feel like home.

Alongside the exhibition, Hannah invites visitors to slow down, pick up a pen or brush, and create their own marks, words or images inspired by home, memory and connection.

No previous experience is needed.

Enjoy a cup of tea, meet the artist, explore the work and take part in a gentle creative
activity that can be continued anywhere with simple materials.

Meet the artist and informal conversation
View the Making Home exhibition and original drawing
Explore sketchbooks and creative process
Chinese calligraphy and drawing demonstration
Mindful mark-making: create your own word, line or image
Tea, chat and creative exchange

title: Cork City Libraries – Grand Parade – Children and Young People’s Library: Sweet Dreams: Lullabies Across the World-Exhibition
description:
This is a project of the Women’s Programme at Nasc, the Migrant and Refugee Rights Centre. The programme brings together more than 160 women from diverse backgrounds who share the experience of forced displacement, creating a
space for community, connection and solidarity.

Inspired by similar initiatives in the US, the UK and Denmark, Sweet Dreams was developed in response to rising racism and xenophobia, highlighting the shared experiences that unite people across cultures and languages. At the heart of the project
are lullabies. These universal expressions of love, hope and protection transcend borders and generations.

Drawing on childhood memories and cultural traditions, participants created artworks inspired by lullabies from their home countries. For some women, these songs evoke hopes for their children’s futures in Ireland; for others, they recall the loss of
home and family caused by displacement.

Each postcard features original artwork, a participant’s interpretation of the lullaby’s meaning in English, and a QR code linking to a recording of the song and its story. Together, the works celebrate cultural heritage, resilience and shared
humanity while offering a powerful response to division. Visitors are invited to contribute their own reflections, drawings, songs or lullabies on the blank postcards provided.

title: Cork City Libraries – Grand Parade – Foyer: Still Not Safe: Life in Gaza During the ‘Ceasefire’ – Documentary Premiere
description:
Two million people in Gaza are still not safe. Every day, they face challenges most of us would find unimaginable: finding
food, getting clean water, identifying hospitals that are still functioning so children can receive medicines and treatments, and
finding the strength to mourn family members and friends lost amid the devastation of collapsed homes, schools and
universities. In the midst of such loss, urgent questions remain: where is dignity, and where is justice?

Still Not Safe: Life in Gaza during the ‘ceasefire’ is a 2026 short documentary by Trócaire that follows the daily lives of
Mahmoud, a father; Yasmin, a mother; and several others as they try to hold on to hope in circumstances that often feel
hopeless. Above all, they are asking us to listen to their voices.

“We are not asking for your support in money. We are asking for your support to restore our dignity.” – Mahmoud, Gaza.

6pm (Foyer) – educational stand with activities for children and simple actions for adults, inviting reflections on dignity, compassion and care for all

7.30pm (Main Library) – documentary screening

title: Cork City Libraries – Grand Parade – Local Studies & Learning: Uncovering Treasures: An Evening of Discovery
description:
For the first time, the Local Studies & Learning Department will open its doors to the public on Culture Night, offering a unique opportunity to discover some of the hidden treasures held within the library that are not normally on public display.

Visitors are invited to explore a rich and diverse collection of books, newspapers, manuscripts, maps and photographs, showcasing the breadth of the library’s special collections.

The evening also provides an opportunity to learn more about accessing online resources, including the Irish Newspaper Archive, genealogy websites and census records, which can help uncover family histories and support local and historical research.

To mark Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union, the library will showcase contemporary newspaper coverage of significant European events, including Ireland’s accession to the E.E.C. in 1973, offering a glimpse into how these landmark moments were reported and experienced at the time.

Join the Local Studies & Learning Department for an evening of discovery and explore the stories, collections and resources that lie beyond the bookshelves.

Alternatively, they can create beauty, humour, and unexpected connections. Each piece offers a glimpse into lives shaped by change—where identities are tested, boundaries are crossed, and new perspectives emerge.

“When Two Worlds Collide” invites the audience to reflect on their own encounters—with others, with change, and with themselves. ‘SunMakerS’ is a group of emerging writers who are looking forward to sharing their insights and writings at Mayfield Library on Culture Night 2026.

title: Cork International Film Festival Online: Short Films All Evening
description:
Curated together with the Estonian Film Institute, this special online Culture Night presentation celebrates the richness of Estonian short filmmaking through two programmes. Together, these programmes offer audiences of all ages a unique opportunity to discover Estonia’s rich cinematic heritage through compelling documentary storytelling and charming family-friendly films.

Programme 1: ’Tallinn Time Capsule’: A 90-minute programme of gorgeous documentary shorts from Estonia, presented in chronological order from 1968 and 1985. A fascinating journey through the country’s history, culture and changing society, via daily scenes that feel strikingly universal.

Programme 2: Estonian Family Shorts: A 45-minute selection of vintage short films for younger audiences (age 6+). Featuring imaginative stories and engaging animation, it offers a fun introduction to Estonian animation heritage for viewers of all ages.

Following Culture Night, the programme will be available to watch online throughout the weekend until midnight Sunday.

title: Counsel to the Nation: A Historical Tour of the Office of the Attorney General
description:
For the first time in its history, the Office of the Attorney General will open its doors to the public as part of Culture Night, offering a rare opportunity to step inside one of the State’s most significant legal institutions.

The Attorney General attends Cabinet as the legal adviser to the Government and is the chief law officer of the State, leading significant litigation on behalf of the Irish State before domestic and international courts.

The Office of the Attorney General building, located on Upper Merrion Street, adjacent to the Department of the Taoiseach, is steeped in history and tradition. The building itself has played a quiet but vital role in shaping the legal landscape of modern Ireland.

For one night only, tours will run on a pre-booked, first come, first served basis. A limited number of places are available across three time slots throughout the evening. Visitors on the night will get a unique insight into the day-to-day workings of the Office and the role it plays at the heart of Irish public law.

Whether visitors have an interest in law, history, architecture, or simply enjoying a walk around the building, this tour promises something a little different for Culture Night.

Strictly, one ticket per person. Spaces are limited, early booking is strongly recommended.

title: CRAICLY STORIES of “The Cow”
description:
CRAICLY STORIES is one of Ireland’s most innovative, community storytelling projects celebrating memoir style tales, true stories and some Irish folklore. Founded in 2023 by writer Jane Gormley in response to both a rise in loneliness levels, and a love of storytelling – this project has since travelled to unique Irish places all over the island from Stradbally Hall, to Glenbrook Farm, to Smyths Shop in County Clare!  For Culture Night 2026, CRAICLY is back in their first ever venue, and homeplace – Derrymullen Farm, Allenwood. This special evening will take place in the Cow Shed, and celebrate multiple stories of “The Cow”. Derrymullen is a 200 acre organic operation, with a herd of Speckled Park Cattle and home to generations of farmers! Storytellers will include people working with cattle, writing about cows, some works of fiction focused on “the Cow”… there are many angles! We will also welcome food writer Kate Ryan, who will speak to her writing on the tradition of Irish food and read from her soon to be published book. 

There will be some local musicians on hand to keep the atmosphere and conversation flowing after the stories finish.

description:

Using a VR headset, visitors will step inside a series of 360-degree films offering unique insights into Traveller life, from sharing a barrel-top wagon with Traveller women to joining Martin and Richie McCarthy as they pass on horse care skills to the next generation. Developed by Cork Traveller Women’s Network in collaboration with artist Linda Curtin, the project offers an engaging and personal introduction to Traveller heritage.

The experience runs from 16:00–19:00 in half-hour viewing slots. Please note that the experience is not recommended for people with photosensitive conditions or vertigo, as it is viewed using a VR headset while seated in a swivel chair.

Commissioned by the Traveller Accommodation Unit, Cork City Council, funded by Dormant Accounts Fund.

title: Creative Workshop: Gelli Plate Printing & Handmade Notebook Making
description:
Discover the colourful and creative world of Gelli Plate printing in this fun, hands-on workshop in Gort.

Gelli Plate printing is a form of mono-printing that allows you to create one-of-a-kind prints using acrylic paints, a soft gel printing plate, a brayer (roller), and a variety of simple tools and techniques.

In the workshop, you will experiment with creating some textures, making patterns, and incorporating natural or everyday objects to produce unique printed papers.

No previous experience is needed, this workshop perfect for beginners as well as anyone looking to explore a new creative process. Participants will be encouraged to experiment freely, with guidance. Every print is different, resulting in a beautiful collection of personalised papers to take home. Once you’ve produced a bunch of pages, you’ll make them into a handmade notebook using a simple bookbinding technique. This easy method creates a practical and unique notebook that can be used as a journal, sketchbook, or thoughtful handmade gift.

The workshop is suitable for adults and children aged 8 years and over.

Children must be accompanied by a participating adult throughout the session.

Please be aware – the workshop can get a little messy. Please wear old clothes or bring an apron to protect your clothing.

Come along, experiment with colour and texture, and leave with beautiful original prints and a handcrafted notebook to treasure.

title: Creative Writing Workshop in Spanish: Food, Rhythm, and Sensory Memory
description:
Instituto Cervantes invites Culture Night guests to explore the fiesta as a playground where literature, dance, and memory join hands to ignite our imagination and help us get our hands dirty.

Through reading excerpts from “Fiebre de carnaval” (Yuliana Ortiz Ruano) and “Like Water for Chocolate” (Laura Esquivel), we will analyse how the festive spirit permeates both the body and literature. We have all eaten and danced; our physicality processes information and stores stories through movement and flavour.

Through step-by-step guided practical exercises, attendees will activate these stimuli as creative triggers. The goal is to reconnect with sensory memory to translate the experience of food and rhythm into an original text, filled with vivid imagery, textures, and dynamism in record time.

This workshop is delivered in Spanish.

The workshop is taught by Luciana de Mello, an Afro-indigenous writer born in Buenos Aires. She has written about literature, feminism, and queer culture for the Argentine newspaper Página/12. Her novel Mandinga was published in Spain in 2025 by Penguin Random House and was selected as one of the best books of the year. She currently resides in Belfast and teaches writing workshops at The Crescent Arts Centre.

 

This event is part of the European Culture Trail brought to you by EUNIC Ireland (European Union National Institutes for Culture). You can download the EUNIC passport here and collect stamps at each stop to enter a draw for wonderful prizes!

See other participating venues in the European Culture Trail here.

title: Crossroads of Sound
description:
Join us for Crossroads of Sound, a special Culture Night celebration bringing together classical music, contemporary influences and sounds from across cultures.

The evening begins with The Starlings Quartet, formed in 2025 by four Clare-based musicians and friends from Ennistymon, Corofin, Miltown Malbay and Kildysart. With roots in Ireland, France and Finland, the quartet draws on a rich mix of musical backgrounds and influences.

Their varied repertoire moves from classical favourites by Dvořák and Haydn to contemporary artists and composers including Galway-based Katharina Baker and Billie Eilish. By happy coincidence, many of their chosen pieces are inspired by birds — giving the quartet its feathered name.

United by a love of classical music and a desire to move beyond its more “stuffy” associations, The Starlings Quartet creates warm, relaxed and accessible performances for audiences of all ages.

The night concludes with Quentin Cooper and Floriane Blancke, a County Clare-based duo whose music brings together harp, guitar, piano and vocals. Drawing on their French and Peruvian roots, their original songs and instrumental pieces weave Irish traditional music with blues, rock, Latin and jazz influences.

With years of international performance and recording experience, Quentin and Floriane combine exceptional musicianship with a spirited and playful stage presence. Their performances invite audiences into an immersive musical journey that is both invigorating and soul-stirring — grounded in craft, curiosity and adventure.

title: Culture Night 2026 at Mary Immaculate College
description:
Mary Immaculate College (MIC) Limerick is delighted to open the doors to its campus for Culture Night 2026—hosting numerous free events encompassing Irish language, culture, heritage, art, music and history.
Events include:

1.Join Dr Paul O’Brien for a guided tour of Summerville House @4.30pm. Meeting at MIC Main Reception.Summerville House is one of the oldest and most historically significant buildings on the Mary Immaculate College (MIC) campus. The house was originally built in the 1780s by Joseph Massey Harvey, a prominent Quaker merchantSummerville House is a fine example of a late eighteenth-century Georgian suburban villa with symmetrical proportions, an elegant façade, and classical detailing. The house originally stood within a substantial estate on the outskirts of Limerick city, in an area known as Quaker’s Fields.

The property became part of the Mary Immaculate College campus in the twentieth century

2.Ogham Workshop | Ceardlann Oghaim @ 5pm

Discover the fascinating tradition of Ogham, Ireland’s earliest form of writing, at this bilingual workshop. Participants will learn the history and significance of Ogham before getting the chance to design their own Ogham inscription.

title: Culture Night 2026: Breaking The Narrative Workshops with Emma Ray
description:
Breaking the Narrative: A tactile workshop exploring digital ennui, led by Artist in Residence Emma Ray.

We live in a visual culture of “endless scrolling,” where we are constantly bombarded with high-gloss, hyper-curated images of perfection. In this workshop, participants will take a piece of curated social media imagery and dissect it using a combination of heavy acrylic paints and traditional embroidery threads, you are invited to physically “break” the narrative..

6pm Workshop (Teens: Ages 13–18) A fast-paced, hands-on session focusing on the pressure of the curated feed. Teens are invited to visceral, creative deconstruction—using paint and thread to rebel against the pressure of the “perfect” digital aesthetic.

7.30pm Workshop (Adults: 18+) A relaxed, slow-paced session focusing on digital exhaustion. Adults can use methodical, meditative embroidery and painting to slow down the consumption of an image, pushing back against the fatigue of the endless scroll. No previous painting or embroidery experience is required.

title: Culture Night 2026: CHOP
description:
CHOP — Absurd Comedy Theatre by Cian Kinsella and Lords of Strut

CHOP is a dangerously funny, wildly absurd descent into fragile masculinity, environmental collapse, and the insatiable hunger for more. Expect real danger, real questions, zero solutions…. and a lot of laughs. This is the kind of show you come out buzzing from: funny, physical, slightly dark, and full of heart.

At its centre is a lonewood-chopperstuck in a strange, end-of-the-world loop, hacking away as everything around him falls apart. Blending slapstick, clowning, and high-energy physical comedy… with real axes and real wood chopping!CHOP turns eco-anxiety, masculinity, and our messy relationship with the planet into a fast, joyful, and surprisingly moving experience. Part absurd spectacle, part urgent provocation, it sits at the turning point between collapse, connection, and change.

title: Culture Night at Abbey Presbyterian Church (Findlaters)
description:
This Culture Night, Abbey Presbyterian Church welcomes visitors to step inside and discover the rich history and stories of this landmark building on Parnell Square as we collaborate with the Hugh Lane Gallery for Culture Night.

The Hugh Lane Gallery presents:
Culture Night from the Abbey Presbyterian Church

6.15pm
Marmosets

Marmosets is a duo-cello project from Mary Barnecutt and Lioba Petrie, both acclaimed cellists, producers and singers based in Dublin and Wicklow. The musicians draw on their experience as multi-genre players to fuse folk traditions, song, contemporary composition and dronescapes to create an unworldly music which is at the same time grounded in very earthly traditions. Using electronics, shruti boxes, vocals and cellos the resultant sounds are magical soundscapes of ancient and contemporary music firmly rooted in place.

7.15pm
Unshaped Form – Lift Off

Unshaped Form : Lioba Petrie (cello/vocals), Cameron Doyle (guitar/effects) with special guests Sam Perkin (piano), Matthew Jacobson (percussion) bring their unique cinematicsoundscapes to the Abbey Presbyterian Church as part of the Hugh Lane Gallery’s event
programme for Culture Night.

Unshaped Form’s new project LIFT OFF is a a live audio-visual adventure through space. Expect an immersive mix of modern acoustic instruments, dynamic percussion, spatial cosmic textures and inspiring visuals from the voyager space project, Nasa and animation
from the 1920’s and 1980’s. For this unique event Unshaped Form present a programme of short films, varying from cartoon animation to original footage form the Voyager space mission all based around the
theme of outer space.

Musicians
Matt Jacobson – percussion
Lioba Petrie – cello
Sam Perkin – piano
Cameron Doyle – guitar, effects

8.15pm
Matthew Jacobson : percussionist+synths

Matthew Jacobson is an Irish drummer, improviser, composer, educator and producer. Matthew leads his own groups ReDiviDeR (free improv quartet) and Insufficient Funs (ebullient drums and bass saxophone duo) and has recently developed a solo drums+synths
project. He co-leads Roamer (quartet of Ireland’s most internationally recognised improvisers), hyperlynx (trio with Swiss-based collaborators), Origin Story (contemporary piano trio) and regularly tours, performs and records with leading creative musicians around
the world.

Whether you are a history buff, a music lover, or simply looking for a welcoming place to pause, there is something for everyone. Visitors are invited to explore the historic architecture on a relaxed self-guided tour, browse a pop-up second-hand book sale, and enjoy live music throughout the evening.

Guests are also welcome to chat with members of the community or simply find a quiet pew and take in the peaceful atmosphere of this sacred space. From the music filling the rafters to the stories found within its walls, Abbey Presbyterian Church offers a warm welcome and the opportunity to experience one of Parnell Square’s historic landmarks at a leisurely pace.

title: Culture Night at Castletown House
description:
nrityā nazākhat is an original Kathak production by rāas featuring four dancers and a live Hindustani classical musician (tabla). The performance explores nazākhat—subtlety, grace and emotional nuance—through intricate footwork, live music and dialogue between dancers and musicians. Structured across seven short acts, the work moves from expressive storytelling into increasingly virtuosic rhythmic exchanges, culminating in a high-energy finale. It has been conceived as a site-responsive performance, where the architecture of Castletown House becomes an active part of the experience, creating a dialogue between heritage, movement and music.

For Culture Night, this event will take place on the Steps of Castletown House as the sun begins to set. The House will give a beautiful back drop to this wonderful performance of dance and music. This performance will be for 30 minutes and is free. People are welcome to bring a picnic blanket to sit on our lawn and watch or just stand and be mesmerised by the performance.

title: Culture Night at Cobh Heritage Centre – Ireland’s Influence on America’s History
description: Join us for a special Culture Night experience at Cobh Heritage Centre, beginning at 6:00pm with an engaging talk by our resident genealogist and local historian, Christopher Keating. In his presentation, “Ireland’s Influence on America’s History,” Christopher will explore the remarkable impact Irish people have had on the political, social, cultural and economic development of the United States. Drawing on fascinating stories, historical connections and Cobh’s unique place in Ireland’s emigration history, this talk offers fresh insights into the enduring links between Ireland and America. Following the presentation, visitors are invited to enjoy a self-guided tour of Cobh Heritage Centre, exploring our exhibitions and discovering the stories of emigration, migration and maritime history that have shaped Cobh and connected Ireland to the wider world. This free Culture Night event offers a unique opportunity to learn, reflect and celebrate our shared heritage in one of Ireland’s most significant historical locations.

title: Culture Night at Cullenswood House
description:
This Culture Night, Cullenswood House welcomes visitors to explore this important late Georgian structure, dating from around 1800, and discover its remarkable place in Ireland’s cultural and revolutionary history.

Cullenswood House was the original home of Scoil Éanna (St Enda’s School), founded by Pádraig Pearse in 1908. Guided tours will reveal the building’s rich history, where Pearse, Willie Pearse, Con Colbert, and Thomas MacDonagh all taught, and where notable figures including Roger Casement, Maud Gonne MacBride, W.B. Yeats, and Countess Markievicz were among its many visitors.

As they walk the same hallways as these influential figures, visitors will gain a unique insight into the atmosphere and legacy of this historic building. Throughout the evening, traditional Irish music performed in different rooms of the house will add to the experience.

Oíche den scoth a bheidh ann.

Nowadays, DIAS astrophysicists study explosions on the Sun, search for new stars and planets, and search the universe for exotic astronomical objects. title: Culture Night at Dublin City Hall
description:
Celebrate Culture Night 2026 with an evening of live music in the magnificent surroundings of Dublin City Hall. This event brings together some of Ireland’s finest established and emerging musicians for a programme that celebrates the city’s rich musical heritage while showcasing the diversity and creativity of its contemporary music scene.

 

**Please note this is a standing only event.**

 

18:00 – Dublin Youth Choir

Founded in 2017, Dublin Youth Choir is an award-winning organisation that provides high-quality choral music education for young people across Dublin and the surrounding areas. Through its progressive programme of choirs, DYC nurtures musicianship, vocal technique and ensemble skills, inspired by the Kodály approach. Under the artistic direction of Dr Lynsey Callaghan, the choir has earned national and international acclaim, including being named Ireland’s Choir of the Year at the Cork International Choral Festival in 2022 and 2024 and winners of the youth choir category at the European Choir Games in Sweden in 2019.

 

18:45 – Stellar Choir

Featuring in this year’s City Hall programme is Stellar Choir, a talented four-part mixed-voice choir based in Upper Rathmines. Established in 2018, the ensemble quickly grew into a thriving community choir and now boasts more than 60 members. Known for their engaging performances and wide-ranging repertoire, Stellar Choir performs everything from sacred music and traditional Irish songs to jazz and contemporary favourites. Last year, Stellar travelled to New York to perform in the world-renowned Carnegie Hall and in 2027, they will represent Ireland at the We Are Singing festival in Kraków.

 

19:30 Belle Harmonics

Belle Harmonics is an award-winning pop-rock choir based in Synge Street, Dublin. Known for its powerful vocals, original arrangements, and infectious energy, the 35-member group performs fresh takes on songs by a wide range of artists, from Belinda Carlisle and Fleetwood Mac to Chappell Roan and Adele. Formed in 2018, the choir has built a strong reputation for its dynamic live shows, regularly appearing at sold-out venues and festivals across the country.

 

20:20 The Ramparts 

The Ramparts are an all-male Dublin based a cappella group set up in February 2016.  They love to sing a wide range of traditional Irish folk songs, classic hits, old school barbershop ballads, contemporary classical and sacred music.

The Ramparts are versatile performers who know how to keep an audience entertained with their big sound and even bigger personalities. Whether on stage, on the street, on the bus, or in the pub, The Ramparts always guarantee their audiences a unique and memorable show. 

 

21:00 Dublin Fire Brigade Pipe Band

The Dublin Fire Brigade Pipe Band was founded in 1985. The membership of the band is drawn from serving and retired members of the brigade. The band represents Dublin Fire Brigade at civic events, national and international parades and commemorations. Don’t miss the opportunity to experience the Dublin Fire Brigade Pipe Band live as they close out this special Culture Night at Dublin City Hall.

 

Move through the building as music unfolds across the evening, discover established artists alongside emerging talent, community ensembles and cross-cultural collaborations that celebrate the many voices shaping Dublin’s musical identity. Visitors will also have the opportunity to explore the historic Council Chamber, where they can sit in the Lord Mayor’s chair.

title: Culture Night at Dublinia
description:
Culture Night visitors are invited to step back in time at Dublinia, located in the heart of Viking and Medieval Dublin. Journey through the city’s past and discover what life was like for the people who lived here centuries ago.

Experience life on board a Viking warship, explore a Viking house, walk along a Viking street, and uncover the myths, mysteries, and legacy of the Vikings in Ireland. Continue through Medieval Dublin, where the sights, sounds, and smells of a busy city are brought to life. Visit a wealthy merchant’s kitchen, stroll down a bustling medieval street, and gain insight into daily life during this fascinating period of Dublin’s history.

Visitors can also view a remarkable collection of Viking and Medieval artefacts and enjoy an immersive audio-visual experience that follows one man’s journey growing up in Medieval Dublin.

A visit to Dublinia offers a unique opportunity to explore over a thousand years of Dublin’s history in an engaging and interactive setting.

As you make your way through, you’ll stamp your EPIC passport in each gallery, marking your journey through Ireland’s global story.

Set in the atmospheric vaults of Dublin’s CHQ Building, EPIC is self-guided, allowing you to explore at your own pace, and our visitor experience team are always on hand to answer questions, share stories and help you get even more from your visit.

A three-time winner of Europe’s Leading Tourist Attraction, EPIC sits in the heart of Dublin’s vibrant Docklands.

title: Culture Night at GPO Museum
description:
This Culture Night, visitors are invited to step into the story of modern Ireland at the GPO Museum. Located in one of the country’s most significant historic buildings, the museum explores the key events that shaped Ireland’s journey to independence and beyond.

Discover the major moments of Irish history, from the Cultural Revival and the Home Rule Crisis to the 1916 Easter Rising, the Irish Civil War, and the Troubles, culminating in the peace process in Northern Ireland. Through immersive exhibitions and interactive displays, visitors can engage with the people, ideas, and events that helped shape the nation.

As part of the Culture Night programme, the evening will also feature a series of specially researched talks delivered by the museum’s expert guides, offering additional insights into Ireland’s revolutionary history.

title: Culture Night at Irish Whiskey Museum

Discover the people, places, and traditions that have shaped one of Ireland’s most iconic exports through interactive exhibits and captivating storytelling. The experience concludes with a guided whiskey tasting, where visitors can sample a selection of Irish whiskeys and learn how to appreciate their unique flavours and character.

Whether whiskey enthusiasts or simply curious about an important part of Ireland’s heritage, visitors will find this Culture Night experience offers a memorable introduction to the story of Irish whiskey.

The evening begins with a bilingual guided farm walk led by Ionia Ní Chróinín, exploring the measures taken on the farm to support and increase biodiversity. Meet the hens, wander the fields, and hear about the living ecosystems that shape the farm before gathering together for an intimate concert featuring singer-songwriters and traditional musicians Tuán Ó Baoill (Gradaím NÓS nominee 2026) agus Muireann Ní Bhaoill.

title: Culture Night at MERITS: Cybernetic Ecologies with Serena Devereux
description:
Join artist Serena Devereux, recipient of the 2026 VECTOR Digital Arts Residency, for a special Culture Night event at MERITS Innovation Hub, Naas.
Cybernetic Ecologies is a digital art installation exploring the evolving relationship between nature, technology and data. Drawing on local weather conditions and 3D scans of plant species from Kildare, the work uses live weather data to generate moving digital imagery in real time, creating an artwork that continuously changes in response to the environment. The installation invites audiences to consider how digital systems, natural processes and human experience are increasingly interconnected.
The event will include an informal artist’s talk (from 4-5pm) by Serena Devereux, offering insight into her research, creative process and residency experience, as well as the technologies and ecological themes that underpin the work. Devereux is a multidisciplinary visual artist from Kildare whose practice spans video, CGI, AI, creative coding and immersive installation, examining how technology shapes our understanding of reality, identity and place.
This free event is open to all and will be of interest to audiences engaged with art, technology, climate action, biodiversity, digital innovation and placemaking.

title: Culture Night at MoLI: Where Irish Writing Comes Alive
description:
Celebrate Culture Night at MoLI (Museum of Literature Ireland), where Irish writing comes alive. This year, visitors can explore the museum after hours, wander through its historic buildings and gardens, and discover Irish literature in an immersive and inspiring setting.

Housed in UCD Newman House on St Stephen’s Green, MoLI brings the stories of Ireland’s greatest writers to life through exhibitions featuring manuscripts, letters, first editions and rare literary treasures. Don’t miss the chance to see Copy No. 1 of James Joyce’s Ulysses, Joyce’s own first printed copy, displayed in the very building where he studied.

Visitors can also experience Wild Earth, MoLI’s exhibition exploring the relationship between Irish writing and the natural world, featuring more than 90 texts spanning from the sixth century to today.

Step outside into the peaceful Readers Garden, home to a 200-year-old ash tree featured in Joyce’s graduation photograph and connected to Maeve Binchy’s Circle of Friends. Browse the MoLI Bookshop for Irish books and crafts, or relax in The Commons Café, open throughout the evening with food and drinks available to purchase.

The MoLI team will be on hand to welcome visitors, share stories about the museum and provide information about MoLI Membership, which supports the museum while offering year-round access, exclusive events and other benefits.
fullAddress: MoLI – Museum of Literature Ireland, 86 St Stephen's Green, Saint Kevin's, Dublin, D02 XY43, Ireland

title: Culture Night at Seamus Heaney: Listen Now Again
description:
The Seamus Heaney: Listen Now Again exhibition invites Culture Night visitors on a fascinating journey exploring the highlights of Seamus Heaney’s poetry and life, donated to the National Library of Ireland. The exhibition allows guests to explore Seamus Heaney’s rural origins through to his remarkable career as a poet and noble prize winner. Explore the exhibition at your own pace, with expert staff at key areas in the exhibition to help you.

Heaney’s own writing desk is the focal point of an experience that explores Heaney’s creative process through original manuscripts, as well as letters, unpublished works, diary entries, photographs, personal artefacts and multimedia recordings, revealing the internal and external forces that shaped his work.

title: Culture Night at Shelbourne Park Museum
description:
Celebrate Culture Night at Shelbourne Park and discover the story of one of Dublin’s best-known sporting venues. Located in the heart of Ringsend, Shelbourne Park has been woven into the social and sporting fabric of the area for more than a century. Visit the Shelbourne Park Museum and explore the history of a venue that is preparing to mark 100 years of greyhound racing in 2027.

Before becoming Ireland’s premier greyhound racing stadium, the grounds hosted some of the most notable events in Irish sporting history. Named after Shelbourne FC, it staged football matches from 1913, welcomed Manchester United for their first game on Irish soil in 1914, and hosted a major four-day fête opened by Éamon de Valera in 1921. Rugby league was played here for the first time in 1934, while more recently the venue featured on Top Gear and hosted a fan zone for the 2024 UEFA Europa League Final.

Today, Shelbourne Park is best known as the home of the Irish Greyhound Derby, Ireland’s richest and most prestigious greyhound race. Through photographs, memorabilia and stories from across the decades, this special Culture Night event offers the opportunity to explore the people, occasions and sporting moments that have shaped Shelbourne Park and secured its place in Dublin’s history. Come along for an evening of heritage, community and culture at this famous Dublin landmark.

Booking is recommended to attend, however walk-ins may be admitted if capacity allows.

Suite i gcroílár na Rinne, tá Páirc Shelbourne mar chuid de stair shóisialta agus spóirt an cheantair le breis agus céad bliain. Imríodh rugbaí sraithe ann den chéad uair i 1934, agus le blianta beaga anuas bhí an suíomh le feiceáil ar Top Gear agus mar chrios lucht leanúna do Chraobhchluiche Shraith Europa UEFA 2024.

title: Culture Night at St Andrew’s Church: Sacred Space in Time, Space and Culture
description:
This Culture Night, St Andrew’s Church welcomes visitors to discover nearly 200 years of history, architecture, music, and community in the heart of Dublin.

A place of peace, prayer, and sacred music since the early nineteenth century, St Andrew’s has witnessed many defining moments in Irish history, from Daniel O’Connell and Pádraig Pearse to Éamon de Valera. Celebrated in James Joyce’s Ulysses and long associated with the Archbishops of Dublin, the church continues to serve local residents, daily commuters, and Dublin’s Lithuanian and Chinese communities.

Throughout the evening, visitors can enjoy guided tours exploring the church’s art, architecture, and history, alongside a talk on notable figures associated with St Andrew’s, including Archbishop Daniel Murray, Daniel O’Connell, Catherine McAuley, Sir Dominic Corrigan, and the Pearse brothers.

The programme also features musical performances by the Lithuanian and Chinese communities, an organ recital by resident organist Mark McCrystal, and sacred music performed by St Andrew’s Parish Choir.

Managed by the Office of Public Works (OPW), the site will host an extended evening opening from 17:30 to 19:30. Guests can explore the historic nave and visitor centre at their own pace.

A highlight of the evening features a special live musical performance by the Society of Recorder Players from 18:00 to 19:00.

Admission is completely free, and drop-in visits are welcome throughout the evening until final entry at 19:30.

Women in History Highlights Tour:

Discover the stories of extraordinary women buried in Glasnevin Cemetery, many of whom played key roles in shaping Irish history and the country’s political landscape. The tour explores the lives and achievements of women who helped shape modern Ireland, including one Irishwoman who became one of the first women in the world to hold a cabinet position.

Dead Interesting Highlights Tour:

Join a highlight tour of the cemetery’s oldest areas and reveal the remarkable stories and monuments that make Glasnevin such a unique landmark. Visit the ornate crypt of Daniel O’Connell and learn about the cemetery’s early history and some of its more unusual stories!

Tours will run throughout the evening from 16:00–20:30. The exhibitions in the Visitor Centre will also remain open until 20:00.

title: Culture Night Late | Galway City Night-Time Economy – 8 Bits of Galway by Media Artist Serhii Khadzhava
description:
8 Bits of Galway by media artist Serhii Khadzhava 

8 Bits of Galway is a playful and visually captivating 3D mapping experience that reimagines the façade of Lynch’s Castle, one of Galway’s most iconic historic landmarks. Transforming the building into a vibrant, arcade-inspired world, the artwork draws on the visual language of classic 1990s platform games. Through a series of short visual “levels”, the artwork offers a glimpse of Galway in an 8-bit aesthetic. 

Sergey Khadzhava is a Ukrainian media artist based in Ireland, working across immersive audiovisual installations, projection mapping, and live visuals. With over ten years’ experience, he has created works for Electric Picnic, All Together Now, Beyond The Pale, Night And Day Festival and other events across Ireland and worldwide, transforming public environments into engaging visual experiences, blending of physical and digital worlds, creating memorable shared experiences for audiences. 

8 Bits of Galway forms part of the Arts Council’s Culture Night Late and the Galway City Night-Time Economy Programme funded by Department of Culture, Communications and Sport, with support from the Galway City Council Night-Time Economy and Arts Office.

8 Bits of Galway leis an ealaíontóir meán Serhii Khadzhava

Déanfar domhan spleodrach a bheidh faoi anáil ionaid siamsaíochta den fhoirgneamh féin agus beidh an saothar ealaíne bunaithe ar theanga amhairc na gcluichí ardáin clasaiceacha ó na 1990idí. Trí shraith de “leibhéil” ghearra amhairc, tabharfar léargas ar Ghaillimh in aeistéitic 8-ngiotán leis an saothar ealaíne.
Beidh 8 Bits of Galway mar chuid d’Airneán na hOíche Cultúir na Comhairle Ealaíon agus de Chlár Geilleagair Oíche Chathair na Gaillimhe atá maoinithe ag an Roinn Cultúir, Cumarsáide agus Spóirt, le tacaíocht ó Oifig Geilleagair Oíche agus Ealaíon Chomhairle Cathrach na Gaillimhe.

title: Culture Night Tours 2026 at the Registry of Deeds
description:
This Culture Night, Tailte Éireann invites visitors to explore more than 300 years of Irish history through a guided tour of the historic Registry of Deeds building.

Led by members of the Archives Team, the tour will introduce visitors to Tailte Éireann’s collections, which document land and property in Ireland from 1708 to the present day. Featuring property records, maps, and valuation books, the archives are an invaluable resource for family, local, social, and economic history. Visitors will also learn how to search the collections and discover some of the notable people, places, and historic signatures preserved within the records.

The tour includes access to the beautiful Registry of Deeds building, including the vault, the cantilever staircase, the Public Room with its pitch pine shelving (designed c.1829) and original parquet floors, and the second-floor Reading Room, with its views across Dublin city.

title: David Murphy
description:
Join us at St. Finbarr’s Oratory for an evening of music with David Murphy, supported by Nóra and Ellen de Búrca. Set against the beautiful surroundings of St. Finbarr’s Oratory, this is sure to be a memorable and magical evening of live music!

 

David Murphy takes the pedal steel guitar outside the confines of its traditional roots with frequent ventures into a range of genres, spanning Americana and Traditional Irish to ambient, experimental music and film soundtracks. Alongside his solo work, he is also known as a frequent collaborator with artists such as The Lost Brothers, Arborist and The Delines, accompanying M.Ward or Jolie Holland or contributing sonic soundscapes to the writings of modern literary greats like Patrick McCabe and Willy Vlautin. His critically acclaimed debut album ‘Cuimhne Ghlinn: Explorations in Irish Music for Pedal Steel Guitar’ (Rollercoaster Records) takes the pedal steel from the well-worn roads of the dusty American south to a new place in contemporary Irish music, resulting in numerous Album of The Year shortlists for 2024. This all-instrumental record recasts ancient Irish harp tunes and historic airs into the 21st century with the swelling, expressive and mournful sounds of the pedal steel guitar. This continues Murphy’s quest to expand the vocabulary of the instrument, taking it deeper into a world much closer to home and, for the very first time, present it in a modern Irish framework.

Murphy’s live show presents these ancient Irish harp tunes and historic airs voiced by the mysterious and emotive sound of the pedal steel guitar and accompanied with his band Ether Ensemble: all-star musicians from across contemporary, modern-classical and traditional/folk worlds. Here the pedal steel ably takes its place alongside cello, violin, piano, harp and lush electronic textures and synths. Murphy and his band conjure a palette of sparse, dreamlike, atmospheric soundscapes and stirring, cinematic takes of these culturally significant compositions and melodies from Ireland’s great harpists, composers, and song collectors. Recent appearances include Kilkenny Arts Festival, Electric Picnic, Another Love Story, Cork Opera House, Galway and Doolin Folk Festivals, National Concert Hall (Dublin), Celtic Connections (Glasgow), Sounds From A Safe Harbour (Cork), Other Voices (Dingle/Wales), Quiet Lights Festival and national television appearances at TG4’s Fleadh Cheoil and RTE’s Other Voices.

Sisters Nora and Ellen de Búrca come from Cill na Martra in the Múscraí Gaeltacht. Nora plays fiddle, while Ellen is a multi-instrumentalist on harp, flute and whistle. They sing songs from Múscraí in the sean-nós style and are delighted to be opening for David Murphy at this year’s Culture Night in Gougane Barra!

Cuimhne Ghlinn: Explorations in Irish Music for Pedal Steel Guitar
“Irish traditional rendered ghostly by washes of pedal steel and almost subliminal piano… widescreen and structured, like an early Celtic Ólafur Arnalds… 8/10” UNCUT

“A sonic experiment of narcotic enchantment… blossoming with old world charm in luminous modernity.” SONGLINES – ALBUM OF THE MONTH *****

“An intriguing proposition… very moving, at times oddly Balearic, the Hawaiian roots of his warm pitch-shifting instrument spangling through.” THE GUARDIAN

“An incredibly confident debut album. Balanced against its elegance and the dreamlike sound of his pedal steel is a quietly adventurous spirit that is beautifully judged and unpretentious – an extraordinarily great album.” KLOF MAGAZINE

“A brave and pioneering undertaking… a landmark in ambient Irish traditional music” LONESOME HIGHWAY

“Gives a unique and new life to traditional Irish melodies, with ethereal effect” IRISH EXAMINER

“Sensational… deliciously sun-drenched and weary… takes you to a completely different place” BBC NIGHT TRACKS

“Murphy and collaborators have fashioned something new and authentic, building lush, full-band renditions around swelling, heart-aching reaches into Ireland’s musical psyche” EVENING ECHO (TOP 10 IRISH ALBUMS 2024)

“TOP 5 IRISH ALBUMS 2024” THE THIN AIR

“Contemporary classical compositions that bask in the pedal steel’s humming glow and bridge it comfortably into the Irish canon… totally at home in its expansion of traditional forms.” ANOIS, OS ARD

title: Diaries, Travel Accounts and Memoirs of Co. Monaghan

This talk by Grace Maloney, will explore a fascinating range of written accounts from different periods, including accounts by visitors to County Monaghan and diaries written by farmers, women, clerics, political activists and soldiers. It will also look at extensive memoirs reflecting on people’s lives, including experiences of life in other countries.

The topic will also encourage the audience to think about the importance of recording their own experiences, whether through keeping a daily diary or writing memoirs of their own lives.

Blending timeless jazz classics with contemporary favourites, the group takes audiences on a journey through the rich history of jazz — from swing-era standards to modern interpretations — while also adding fresh jazz-inspired arrangements of beloved pop and rock songs.

Expect an energetic, stylish, and entertaining performance filled with rhythm, improvisation, and soul.

description:
Dip your toes into drama workshop!

Join us for a relaxed and enjoyable evening of drama activities designed especially for adults who are curious about theatre, storytelling, creativity, and self-expression.
No previous experience is required. Whether you’ve always fancied trying drama, want to meet new people, build confidence, or simply do something different for Culture Night, this workshop offers a welcoming space to explore the world of acting without pressure or performance expectations.

title: Director’s Tour of the National Library

This Culture Night, Dr Audrey Whitty, Director of the National Library of Ireland, leads a special guided tour of the Library’s historic Victorian building on Kildare Street.

Visitors will discover the history of this remarkable building, explore the iconic Reading Room, and learn about the Library’s connections with some of Ireland’s greatest writers and thinkers. The tour also includes visits to the Richard Hayes Room and the Art Room, offering a unique opportunity to experience spaces not usually explored in depth.

This Culture Night, join Downtown Blues for a 50-minute beginner-friendly workshop introducing the fundamentals of Blues dancing at Mind The Step.

title: Discover St. Michael’s
description:
Discover the history, people and music of St. Michael’s Church this Culture Night through a specially curated programme of free events.

‘The Faces of St. Michael’s Photographic Exhibition’ will take place in the Pastoral Centre from 4pm until 8pm.

‘The People of St. Michael’s Tours of the Church’ will take place at 4:30pm and 7pm, meeting at the main doors of the church. This tour will bring to life some of those whose names are associated with St. Michael’s.

‘The Sounds of St. Michael’s Organ Recital’ led by some of our parish organists will take place from 8pm until 9pm. You are invited to sit and experience the beauty of Pugin’s Romanesque Gem while soaking in the sound of our beautiful church organ.

There is no need to pre-book for any of the above events.

title: Discover the 1926 Census
description: The 1926 Census of Ireland, conducted on 18 April 1926, provides the first detailed demographic snapshot of the Irish Free State, recording 2,971,992 people and offering rich insights into society, occupation, language, and family life. Cork County Council’s Local Studies department will explain how to uncover local history in this extraordinary resource.
fullAddress: Clonakilty Library, Kent Street, Youghals, Clonakilty, County Cork, Ireland

title: Discover the Art and History of The National Maternity Hospital
description:
The National Maternity Hospital is delighted to open its doors to the public for an evening of art and history as part of Culture Night 2026.

The National Maternity Hospital’s historic boardroom will be open on the night, as hospital staff take guests on a unique art and history journey, exploring the hospital through key moments in Irish history. The iconic main complex was completed in the late 1930’s, built on a row of Georgian houses and including the former Antrim House.

Step into this remarkable building, where every corner tells a story. Explore the unique collection of art while discovering the rich past of the hospital which is intertwined with the 1916 rising, literary giant James Joyce and the Hospital Sweepstakes!

Entrance to the hospital for Culture Night 2026 will be via the Mount Street entrance facing Merrion Square North.

title: Discover Your Spanish Level at Instituto Cervantes
description:
Join the Instituto Cervantes this Culture Night and take part in a free language level assessment tests!

This is a great opportunity for visitors to discover their current Spanish level in a friendly and relaxed environment, and find the learning path that’s right for them.

What to expect:

Free language level assessment
Short speaking and/or written tasks
Immediate feedback on your level
Information about our available courses and learning options
On-the-day enrollment with a special discount

Visitors can meet the Instituto Cervantes team, take a free language level assessment, and, if they decide to join, enrol on the day with a special Culture Night discount. 

 

This event is part of the European Culture Trail brought to you by EUNIC Ireland (European Union National Institutes for Culture). You can download the EUNIC passport here and collect stamps at each stop to enter a draw for wonderful prizes!

See other participating venues in the European Culture Trail here.

The event brings together creativity and community through art, music, and shared experiences. Visitors can explore our Recovery Through Art exhibition, which showcases artworks created by our participants from our Recovery, Family Support, Drop In, SMART Recovery, Bothar Nua Group, Community Prison Links, and Youth Services programmes.

Throughout the evening, visitors can:
• Join us at our open house in Boghall Road, Bray
• Meet and chat with staff and participants
• Enjoy a performance by our Harmony Pathways music group
• Take part in an interactive collaborative art experience

Refreshments are provided and all are welcome.

title: DJ Sean Live at Cobh Bandstand
description:
With a reputation for soulful, eclectic selections that move effortlessly between genres and moods, Cork’s own DJ Sean has been spinning records in venues across the city and beyond for more than a quarter of a century.

Inspired by musical tastemakers such as Mr. Scruff, Gilles Peterson, and The Assholes of Monaco, Sean’s sets are rooted in a deep musical curiosity and an unwavering love of great records. A long-time stalwart of The Roundy, he is guided by one simple rule: never play a record you don’t love.

Fresh from a celebrated appearance at the 2026 LIAS festival in Ballyvolane House, and following the long hot summer as a familiar fixture way down west with the South Kerry Social Club, Sean continues to win over dancefloors with warmth, character and impeccable taste.

Don’t miss this one!

title: Donegal Town Culture Night Launch and Information Hub

Culture Night in Donegal Town will be launching in style, with local tour guide and historical fashion enthusiast Niamh Coughlan kicking off proceedings from The Abbey Hotel at 5.00pm, with a free Walking Tour of the area around The Diamond outlining its rich cultural history.

Wearing one of her handmade historical costumes, Niamh’s tour will cover topics from manuscript culture and the historic monastic settlement of Donegal Abbey right up to the present day, rounding out with information and advice on the programme of Culture Night events taking place across the town. The tour will end at the Abbey Hotel with a brief address from Mayor Anna Gallagher and a short performance by the Bluestack Chorale to get everyone in the mood to continue their Culture Night journey.

title: Double Bill Puppet Show : Granny and the Salmon / Documentary Film: Pulling Strings – Eugene Lambert (2004)
description:
A current day account of the folktale The Salmon of Knowledge where granny has discovered that the Salmon of Knowledge is living in her local river and she is out to catch it, sure fishing can’t be that hard! Presented by Little Gem Puppets who are family friendly and have met thousands of children. Their shows are very interactive with a strong emphasis on storytelling. The puppets are curious and colourful and they do love to meet new people. Seen in festivals, theatres, libraries, museums, arts centres and beyond. No two shows are ever the same because every audience arrives with their own version of the story to share with the puppets.

Puppet Show suitable for ages up to 12 / you are welcome to bring your own puppet friend (40 mins)

A short interval 5/10 mins

The  interval will be followed by the screening of Documentary Film: “Pulling Strings – Eugene Lambert“(2004)-Duration:1 Hour- Directed by Damien Farrell.

Synopsis-Eugene Lambert entertained Irish audiences all his life. Three generations of Lamberts entertained children week in, week out, in their puppet theatre in Monkstown, Co Dublin. But family businesses can be difficult and the business of puppetry is no exception. In this documentary, Eugene, his wife Mai and their family talk candidly about pushing buttons and pulling strings.

description:

All ages are welcome to come along for a day of collective art making looking at landscape, memory and transformation through mixed media.

No experience required just a curiosity about contemporary art.
