title: Drums of Memory: Samba de Roda and Cultural Connection
description:
Sementes do Samba de Roda is an Afro-Brazilian cultural project that proposes an immersive celebration of ancestral rhythm, music, dance, and collective expression for Culture Night Galway. Rooted in the traditions of the Recôncavo region of Bahia, Samba de Roda is a UNESCO-recognised Afro-Brazilian cultural expression that emerged from the resistance, creativity, and community life of Afrodescendant communities in Brazil. Through live percussion, call-and-response singing, circular dance, and participatory performance, the event invites audiences into a vibrant experience of living cultural heritage. This event aims not only to present Brazilian popular culture, but also to create a meaningful intercultural dialogue between Brazil and Ireland. In the same way Ireland preserves and celebrates its own traditions through music, dance, storytelling, and communal gathering, Samba de Roda carries ancestral memory, identity, resilience, and collective celebration across generations. Both traditions demonstrate the power of culture to strengthen community and preserve history through artistic expression. The  presentation will combine live music, dance performance, audience interaction, and cultural storytelling, creating an accessible and inclusive experience for diverse audiences attending Culture Night Galway. The event seeks to foster connection, participation, and cultural curiosity while highlighting the richness and diversity of Afro-Brazilian traditions. By bringing this tradition to Galway, the event contributes to the values of multiculturalism, accessibility, community participation, and intercultural exchange that are central to Culture Night. The event will offer audiences an opportunity to engage with an important Afro-diasporic cultural practice in an open, joyful, and welcoming environment, strengthening cultural diversity within Galway’s artistic landscape.

Is tionscadal cultúir Afra-Bhrasaíleach é Sementes do Samba de Roda a bhfuil sé beartaithe leis ceiliúradh tumtha ar rithim, ceol, damhsa agus léiriú comhchoiteann a sinsir a chur ar siúl d’Oíche Chultúir na Gaillimhe. Agus é fréamhaithe i dtraidisiúin an réigiúin Recôncavo i Bahia, is léiriú cultúir Afra-Bhrasaíleach é Samba de Roda atá aitheanta ag UNESCO agus a d’eascair as frithbheartaíocht, cruthaitheacht agus saol na bpobal de shliocht na nAfracach sa mBrasaíl. Úsáidfear cnaguirlisí beo, amhránaíocht glaonna agus freagartha, damhsa ciorclach, agus taibhiú rannpháirteach, agus iarrfar ar an lucht féachana páirt a ghlacadh in eispéireas bríomhar ar oidhreacht chultúrtha atá fós beo. Tá sé mar aidhm leis an ócáid seo, ní hamháin cultúr na ndaoine sa Bhrasaíl a chur i láthair, ach idirphlé idirchultúrtha fiúntach a chruthú freisin idir an Bhrasaíl agus Éire. Díreach mar a chaomhnaíonn agus a cheiliúrann Éire a traidisiúin féin tríd an gceol, damhsa, scéalaíocht, agus teacht le chéile an phobail, iompraíonn Samba de Roda cuimhne a sinsir, a bhféiniúlacht, a dteacht aniar agus a gceiliúradh i bpáirt le chéile anuas tríd na glúnta. Léiríonn an dá thraidisiún an chaoi a bhfuil an cultúr in ann an pobal a neartú agus an stair a chaomhnú trí léiriú ealaíonta. Sa gcur i láthair atá beartaithe, beidh ceol beo, damhsa, idirghníomhaíocht leis an lucht féachana, agus an scéalaíocht chultúrtha measctha le chéile, a chruthóidh eispéireas inrochtana agus cuimsitheach do na cineálacha daoine éagsúla a bheidh ag freastal ar Oíche Chultúir na Gaillimhe. Beidh sé i gceist leis an ócáid muintearas, rannpháirtíocht agus fiosracht faoi chultúir a chothú agus aird a tharraingt ar an saibhreas agus ar an éagsúlacht a bhaineann leis an traidisiún Afra-Bhrasaíleach. Agus an traidisiún seo á thabhairt go Gaillimh leis an tionscadal, cuirfear leis an luach a bhaineann leis an ilchultúrthacht, an inrochtaineacht, rannpháirtíocht an phobail, agus leis an malartú idirchultúrtha atá mar chuid lárnach d’Oíche Chultúir. Tabharfaidh an tionscadal deis don lucht féachana a bheith páirteach i gcleachtas cultúrtha tábhachtach de chuid dhiaspóra na hAfraice i dtimpeallacht oscailte, lúcháireach agus fáilteach, agus neartóidh sé an éagsúlacht chultúrtha a bhaineann le tírdhreach ealaíonta na Gaillimhe.

title: Dublin in James Joyce’s Time at Sweny’s Pharmacy
description:
Step into the world of James Joyce this Culture Night at the historic Sweny’s Pharmacy on Lincoln Place, where Leopold Bloom famously bought his lemon soap on 16 June 1904. Now in its third year, this special event invites visitors to explore Dublin as Joyce knew it and discover how the city has changed over the past century.

Through a guided tour of a carefully curated photographic exhibition, visitors will journey back to the streets, people, and places that inspired Joyce’s writing. Along the way, they will learn more about Joyce’s enduring literary legacy, his place in Irish cultural history, and the important role that Sweny’s Pharmacy continues to play in the global story of one of Ireland’s most celebrated writers.

title: Echoes in the Courtyard: 140 years in one of Ireland’s earliest social homes
description:
Ellis Court on Benburb Street in Dublin’s north inner city was one of Ireland’s first social housing projects, delivered by Dublin City Corporation in the 1880s. It provided social housing until the early 2000s, when it was damaged by fire, and lay vacant until 2023, when Tuath Housing and Dublin City Council refurbished it for modern social housing.

This Culture Night, Tuath Housing in partnership with DCC, created an exhibition exploring the history of Ellis Court, hosted by the National Museum of Ireland at Collins Barracks. Through photographs, archival records, oral histories and personal stories, the exhibition will bring to life the experiences of the generations of individuals and families who called Ellis Court home from the 1880s onwards.

The project aims to preserve and share an important chapter in Dublin’s social history, while highlighting the enduring importance of safe, secure housing in shaping communities. It will also celebrate the people of Ellis Court, past and present, ensuring their voices and experiences remain part of the historical record.

The exhibition is being developed through extensive historical research, collaboration with museum and heritage experts, and engagement with former residents and their descendants. New dedicated Instagram and Facebook accounts for the project will share additional stories, photographs and archival material uncovered during the research.

This drop-in session offers an opportunity to meet the exhibition’s co-curators, who will be available from 16:00 to 16:45 to discuss the exhibition and answer questions.

The session will be followed by an exciting battle of five original bands organised by the Ennis Eccentric Music Society (EEMS), highlighting the incredible talent emerging from the local music scene. title: Eight Tonnes
description:
Ballinasloe Square will host Eight Tonnes, an after-dark performance, installation and tractor parade. Drawing on the much-loved tradition of tractor parades and vintage tractor runs in rural Ireland, Eight Tonnes brings tractors, artists and performers together for a unique Culture Night Late event.

Eight Tonnes brings together an eclectic mix of artistic voices to celebrate Ballinasloe’s agricultural heritage in a new light. Ballinasloe based performers Breda Larkin (comedian and performer) and Ultan Conlon (musician and composer) join Clifden-based dancer and choreographer Linda Schirmer, Dublin-based digital artist Kev Freeney and Limerick native and new media artist Scott Robinson to turn the familiar sight of a tractor parade into a striking night-time experience — part performance, part celebration, part tribute to the machinery and rhythms that shape rural life. The project is proud to have the support of Macra Galway whose links to young farmers reflect the community and agricultural spirit at the heart of Eight Tonnes. Dancers from In-Step Stage School Ballinasloe are also joining the project, working alongside dancer Linda Schirmer.

Eight Tonnes invites audiences to see something every day and essential to Ballinasloe’s identity as the tractor, through an entirely new artistic lens, blending comedy, music, dance and digital art against the backdrop of the town’s historic Square.

The event is free and family-friendly, and audiences from all walks of life are welcome.

Galway County Council Arts Office presents Eight Tonnes, a Culture Night Late event with artists Breda Larkin, Kev Freeney, Linda Schirmer, Scott Robinson and Ultan Conlon. Funded by the Arts Council, Department of Culture, Communications and Sport and Galway County Council. In partnership with Ballinasloe Town Hall Theatre and Macra Galway. Produced by Culture Works.

description:

éist

The programme begins at the Rock Amphitheatre with local talent Múiris, before moving to Ár n-Áit for an eclectic evening of music. Cork drummer and composer Dan Walsh brings FIXITY, his acclaimed experimental project where free jazz, rock, noise and improvisation collide. Dublin’s Living Things bring their genre-defying Afro-soul sound, fusing Afropunk energy, progressive grooves and soul. Formed by musicians from diverse cultural and musical backgrounds, their music is built around groove, connection and a shared belief in music’s ability to bring people together. The evening culminates with Yankari Afrobeat Collective, led by Nigerian composer and bandleader Segun Akano. Their high-energy sound draws on Nigerian musical traditions, combining driving Afrobeat rhythms with jazz-infused horns, guitars, organ and voices. Yankari have performed at Cork Jazz Festival, All Together Now and TradFest, and appeared on RTÉ’s Tommy Tiernan Show and Radio 1’s Arena. DJ sets come from Frawl (Love Universal), Shane Breen (VCR) and Swiss (King Street Sounds). Around 20 musicians and artists will take part, culminating in a collaborative all-artist jam.

Graphic Studio Gallery presents Episodes in the Obscure, a new solo exhibition of large-scale work by Niall Naessens, generously sponsored by IPUT Real Estate Dublin. Meet the Artist from 18:00–19:00 for an opportunity to hear directly from Naessens about the inspiration and ideas behind the exhibition.

Living in rural Kerry, where the night sky remains largely untouched by light pollution, Naessens draws inspiration from the clarity of the Milky Way and constellations overhead. Many works are set along quiet mountain roads and the Kerry coastline, referencing specific places he encounters on his journeys and walks.

Blending observation with memory and invention, Naessens’ new works describe “incidents around the periphery of the night”, creating atmospheric and enigmatic landscapes that sit between the familiar and the imagined.

For over twenty years Eric has travelled the world documenting his experiences in song. He takes influences from just about anywhere. From classical and traditional Irish music – both of which he learned from a young age – to rock, blues, and jazz, Eric uses everything at his disposal to create songs and pieces that are as honest as they are moving, thought provoking and sometimes even humourous.

title: Eslam Abd El Salam Solo Exhibition
description:
Eslam’s work focuses on walking as a pedagogical practice and is centered around the body in motion, in contact with nature and the presence of other bodies. Through the mediums of analogue photography, text and mixed media, Eslam considers notions of synchronicity, specifically in relation to friendship and serendipitous encounters.

You have your mother’s eyes 

 

// 

 

I have been noticing distance, day in and day out, 

few and far in between. As one does. 

I journal about it, go for a walk or take a nap and it’s either on the backburner or an alchemy. 

 

Zein(at), or Noor. 

 

You have your mother’s eyes as you have been told. 

The project is an effort to understand – for lack of a better word – distance and politics and psychogeography, the physicality and the emotion of it.

 

A visual ode to motherly care and labour that lives and breathes miles away, 

by the bridge that is built at birth/ 

by the narrative maintained with our phone calls/ 

by the walk that dismantles the border/ 

by the novelty of the hope/ 

by the plans stuttering the throat/ 

 

writing “to” gets me closer and “in between” makes it all worthwhile. 

 

A visual ode to motherly care and labour that lives and breathes miles away, by the bridge that is built at birth/ 

by the narrative maintained with our phone calls/ 

by the walk that dismantles the border/ 

by the novelty of the hope/ 

by the plans stuttering the throat 

writing “to” gets me closer and “in between” makes it all worthwhile. 

 

The muscles you’re gaining are all memory cells, or notes. What traces does absence leave us?

 

 

 

You have your mother’s eyes is a collection of prose, imagery and objects that morphs into an installation about and for home. Work in progress that forms a wider investigation about displacement, care, distance and belonging.

 

Eslam is an artist from Cairo, now based in Belfast. Through analogue photography, polaroids, text and mixed media, Eslam considers notions of synchronicity, specifically in relation to friendship and serendipitous encounters. 

 

Eslam recently undertook a residency at Tsarino Foundation, Bulgaria. He is a selected artist for FUTURES 2026 European Photography Platform (PhotoIreland, Dublin) and has exhibited in recent years at Centre for Contemporary Art Derry~Londonderry, Catalyst Arts and Kunstverein Aughrim. Eslam will exhibit a continuation of this work in progress at Sirius Arts Centre, Cobh, in November 2026

Paola Bernardelli Studio exhibition at Guildhall Taphouse Studios (Level 2, Guildhall Taphouse, Entrance via Guildhall street)

This micro-exhibition by Paola Bernardelli consists of new variations on her ongoing project Everything is fragile. Floral still-lives reveal and magnify the process of decay, becoming a metaphor for human life. These works pay homage to the still-life genre embraced by Dutch and Flemish women painters during the 17th and 18th centuries. Considered a minor art at the time, still-life allowed women artists to bypass the rigid societal barriers that restricted them from practicing life drawing and figurative painting. Inhabiting the boundary between photography and video, Bernardelli’s works attempt to reimagine and reinterpret the traditional still-life.

title: Exhibition: Rockwell Kent, An American Artist in Donegal
description:
2026 marks the centenary of Rockwell Kent’s visit to the remote valley of Glenlough, near Gleann Choilm Cille, in south-west Donegal. Through the summer of 1926, he created a series of artworks which remain some of the most significant artistic responses to the Donegal landscape. Many of these artworks are now in private collections – the exhibition displays the only two Donegal artworks that remain in Ireland.  Through text, images and objects, the exhibition explores his extraordinary life and particularly the art he created during his time spent in Donegal.

The exhibition is supported through the Heritage Council Stewardship Fund and by the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport as part of the 2026 Commemorations Programme.

title: Finissage Exhibition and Open Studios
description:

This event promises to be an intimate evening of art, conversation, and encounter.

Finissage invites visitors into the working life of the studio—a space where ideas are tested, materials transformed, and artworks emerge. Alongside a presentation of recent works, visitors are invited to experience the atmosphere of one of Dublin’s longest-standing artist communities, hidden within the remarkable Georgian buildings of Henrietta Street. For more than half a century, these eighteenth-century rooms have sheltered generations of artists, offering spaces of experimentation, making, and exchange.

As this extraordinary chapter draws to a close, Finissage marks both an ending and a celebration—a final gathering that honours the creative life of the studios while reflecting on the urgent need to protect affordable workspaces for artists in Dublin.

The exhibition continues until 26 September 2026, open 11am – 5pm Monday to Saturday.

title: Fixity
description:
FIXITY is an avant garde music project formed by Irish multi instrumentalist and producer Dan Walsh in 2015 which moves in the worlds of psychedelic rock, minimalism, krautrock and free improvisation, featuring an ever-growing pool of collaborators. 

In 2024 Fixity released FIXITY8, the most recent installment in a decade spanning series of solo-produced albums. Now Walsh and collaborators present a return to ensemble work for the first time since 2019’s ‘No Man Can Tell’ LP, with a collection of new tunes and sounds expanding Fixity’s sonic territory ranging from expansive punk improv to ecstatic celebrations and minimalist explorations. 

This project represents a new stage in the growth of Fixity’s music at a greater scale, reaching across fresh musical worlds with the addition of strings arranged by NY/Cork based arranger Aine Delaney. 

Half recorded in Studio Sickan, Malmo in 2022 and half in Cork’s Heavy Meitheal Studios HQ in 2023, the album features an extended cast of long-time collaborators augmented with String ensemble. 

ASSURANCE will be released on Vinyl and Digital in Spring 2026 on MOOTAPES label with Artwork by Stephen Morton. 

 

PRESS QUOTES 

“…defined by its disregard for parameters. Few Irish artists push the invisible parameters of sonic exploration quite like Walsh” 

– Brian Coney, The Thin Air 

“The Things In The Room is a deep experience” 

“Fixity’s world is one where grooves, rock & roll, noise, motorik, and free jazz all coexist.” – Tristan Bath, The Quietus 

“[No Man Can Tell] is a brilliantly loose, shapeshifting record that is quite difficult to compare to anything else, a testament to Walsh and his bandmates’ singular vision” 

– Ryan O’Neill, The Thin Air 

-”The sound of a polymath at play.” 

–Mike McGrath Bryan, The Evening Echo 

“[The Thing in the Room] is simply exceptional.” “One of the great albums of this decade.” 

– KFUEL.org

 

“An absolute knockout…”, “…a record that hits a sweet spot between abrasiveness and beauty, as liable to take you on a thrill ride as it is to bring a tear to your eye.”

Eoin Murray, Anois Os Ard

title: Frame by Frame: Inside the World of Stop-Motion
description:
Step behind the scenes of Stiúideo Fia, a professional stop-motion animation studio based in the heart of Conamara, and discover the magic of filmmaking one frame at a time. As part of Culture Night 2026, this free, family-friendly event offers a rare opportunity to explore a working animation studio and meet the artists who create handcrafted worlds for film and television.
Throughout the evening, visitors can explore beautifully crafted puppets, miniature sets, props and costumes while learning how stop-motion animation transforms still objects into living characters. Watch live demonstrations of puppet animation, model making, sculpting and character design, and gain an insight into the creative process behind professional productions.
Short screenings of films created at Stiúideo Fia, together with behind-the-scenes footage, will reveal the craftsmanship and patience involved in every production. Visitors of all ages will also have the chance to try their hand at creating a simple stop-motion animation using professional equipment, with guidance from the studio team.
Presented bilingually in Irish and English, Frame by Frame celebrates imagination, traditional craft skills and the growing creative industries in the west of Ireland. Whether you are a family looking for a unique evening out, an aspiring animator, an artist, or simply curious about how animated films are made, this event offers an inspiring and memorable experience.
Admission is free, no booking is required, and visitors are welcome to drop in at any time between 6.00pm and 9.00pm. Suitable for all ages.

title: Framing Ennis: A Culture Night Photo Walk

Suitable for all experience levels, the walk begins in daylight and continues into dusk, allowing participants to capture the town as it transforms with the changing evening light. Starting in O’Connell Square, the route takes in Abbey Street, Ennis Friary, the River Fergus, Parnell Street laneways, the Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul, and other accessible streets and public spaces that showcase the town’s rich heritage. Throughout the walk, Gary will share practical photography techniques, including composition, storytelling, working with natural light, and photographing architecture and urban environments. Participants are encouraged to use either a camera or smartphone to create their own visual interpretation of Ennis. The event celebrates Ennis’ by encouraging participants to slow down, observe, and appreciate the stories found within its streets, buildings, and public spaces.

title: From Ascendancy to Brexit: Ireland and the EU
description:
Join political historian and international governance expert Dr. Peter Moloney for a captivating exploration of Ireland’s relationship with the European Union. Since Ireland first signed the treaty of accession and officially joined the European Economic Community in 1973, its economic, social, and political landscapes have completely transformed.  Dr. Moloney will track this dynamic evolution, reflecting on over five decades of integration and sharing expert insights on how Ireland navigates modern challenges.  He will dive into the complex, post-Brexit realities of the Northern Ireland Protocol, shifting trade routes, and the ongoing impacts on the island’s geopolitical landscape.
This talk offers a vital perspective for anyone looking to understand Ireland’s past, present, and future role at the heart of Europe.
Dr. Peter Moloney is an academic historian, international relations expert, and corporate communications leader. Holding a PhD in Modern European History from Boston College, he spent over a decade teaching in the United States, including faculty roles in the Management and Business Department at Skidmore College and history departments at Boston College. Currently based in Killarney, County Kerry, he works as a Senior Proposal Writer, Editor, and People Leader, directing high-level bid strategies for major global firms. Alongside his corporate leadership, he continues to write and speak independently as a socio-political commentator specializing in Brexit, globalization, and European politics. He is contributing a chapter to the UCC Press’ Atlas of the GAA, which is forthcoming.
Culture Night Kerry is co-funded by The Arts Council / An Chomhairle Ealaíon and Kerry County Council, with support from Creative Ireland. This event forms part of Cultúr 2026: Sharing Ireland’s Culture, the national cultural programme for Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union, and is supported by the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport through Culture Ireland.There is free admission to this talk, although you can still reserve a ticket online.

Bí i dteannta an staraí pholaitiúil agus an tsaineolaí ar rialachas idirnáisiúnta, an Dr. Peter Moloney, le haghaidh iniúchadh thar a bheith suimiúil ar an gcaidreamh idir Éirinn agus an tAontas Eorpach. Ó ríomhadh conradh aontachais na hÉireann agus ó thosaigh sí go hoifigiúil mar bhall de Chomhphobal Eacnamaíochta na hEorpa i 1973, tá athrú iomlán tagtha ar thimpeallacht eacnamaíoch, shóisialta agus pholaitiúil na tíre. title: From the Forest to the Ocean  Solo Exhibition with Guided Tour, Artist Talk + Poetry Reading
description: Exhibition Open Friday 18 September, 10am-8pm Talk and Guided Tour Friday 18 September, 7-8pm From the Forest to the Ocean is a powerful solo exhibition featuring the work of Irish artist Mary Moynihan. Bringing together photography, poetry, and film, this multidisciplinary exhibition draws inspiration from the physical landscapes of nature and the deep interconnectedness of life — from forests to the ocean. The artworks map physical landscapes and seascapes to landscapes of the soul and are rooted in reflections on nature, journeys of interconnectedness, and the art of letting go, exploring the boundaries between the natural world and the human spirit. The work creates a synergy between the evocative beauty and fragility of the photographic landscapes and seascapes of counties Dublin, Wicklow, Kerry, and France, combined with the emotional impact of poetical texts in written and in a poem-film format. Join us for an engaging guided tour, artist talk and poetry reading exploring the imagery and stories behind the extraordinary exhibition From the Forest to the Ocean. Hear the stories embedded within the exhibition and reflect on nature, spirituality and peace. Artist Mary Moynihan shares insights into her creative journey as audiences gain a deeper understanding of how the work evolves and responds to contemporary contexts. This is a unique opportunity to hear directly from the artist, ask questions, and connect with the work on display. Interwoven throughout the talk, the artist presents live readings of her original poetry offering a poetical reflection on nature, spirituality and our shared responsibility to care for one another and the earth.

description:
Grangegorman Histories invites Culture Night visitors to join them for a walking tour of Grangegorman and visit the brand new exhibition ‘Beyond the Walls’ at TUD Grangegorman.

For centuries Grangegorman was a place of confinement and care. Within its walls were a workhouse, an asylum and a prison, where lives were shaped by hardship – and sometimes hope. Patients, prisoners, inmates and staff all left their mark on this ground. This exhibition invites you to step into their world – a world where the poor and mentally ill had little choice, where a spell in an overcrowded institution was sometimes better than remaining outside these walls. Today, as Grangegorman is transformed into an open, vibrant space, the past still lingers in its buildings, landscape, and memory.

The tour begins in front of the Clocktower Building and finishes in the Academic Hub building. It will last approximately one hour.

If you have any access requirements, please let the Grangegorman Histories team know by contacting their access officer in advance of the event by email: accessofficer@ria.ie. For all other queries, please contact grangegormanhistories@ggda.ie.
fullAddress: TU Dublin Academic Hub and Library, Grangegorman, Dublin 7, Ireland

title: Griffith College Culture Night Campus Tour
description:
Griffith College extends a warm welcome to Culture Night visitors to discover the storied history of its campus. Originally the site of Grimswood’s Nurseries, construction began in 1813 on a remand prison later known as the Richmond Bridewell. Over the years, it housed notable figures such as Daniel O’Connell and James Stephens, and was the site of Joseph Poole’s execution in 1883. The prison held hundreds of inmates, including some involved in the 1916 Easter Rising.

In 1892, the site was converted into Wellington Barracks and later became one of the first barracks handed over following Ireland’s independence. Renamed Griffith Barracks in honour of Arthur Griffith in 1922, the premises were eventually purchased in 1991 to establish a third-level educational institution.

Discover this remarkable legacy and more on a guided campus tour this Culture Night.

Their handcrafted rugs can be found in embassies, hotels, and private collections around the world.

Visitors will explore the beautifully preserved interior while learning about its rich history, from its origins as Dublin’s first galleried church and George Frideric Handel’s connection with the historic Renatus Harris organ, through to its transformation into The Church Café Bar.

Following the tour, visitors are welcome to stay and enjoy the venue’s Culture Night programme of traditional Irish music and dancing, taking place from 18:30 to 21:30.

title: Guided tours of Ireland’s first purpose-built Government building & a performance by Sandymount Gospel Choir
description:
Culture Night visitors are invited to explore the Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment building on a guided tour highlighting its distinctive architecture and historic features and enjoy a performance by the acclaimed Sandymount Gospel Choir

The tour begins at reception, where visitors will be guided through Ireland’s first purpose-built Government building. The tour highlights the building’s unique architectural features, including the Secretary General’s and Minister’s Offices, the boardroom, and the distinctive terrazzo flooring on the rear staircase leading to the basement. Visitors can also view the building’s impressive exterior, featuring sculptural reliefs and its striking five-storey steel window.

The Sandymount Gospel Choir repertoire includes gospel, bluegrass, African and popular music. Founded in 2009 and led by Musical Director Cathy McEvoy, the choir has performed at a wide range of events, including the Dublin Lord Mayor’s Concert, Darkness Into Light, the Bunratty Folk Festival and numerous community events.

title: Harry Clarke at St Joseph’s Terenure
description:
Join author and stained glass historian Dr David Caron, whose Dublin’s Stained Glass: a guide to the finest twentieth-century windows has introduced many to Ireland’s rich ecclesiastical art heritage for a fascinating exploration of the extraordinary stained glass collection in St. Joseph’s Church, Terenure.

This special Culture Night presentation will focus on the genius of Harry Clarke, Ireland’s most celebrated stained glass artist, whose magnificent Adoration of the Cross by Irish Saints (1920), and the exquisite companion windows The Annunciation (1922) and The Coronation of the Virgin in Glory (1923) rank among the finest examples of his work.

David will also examine the remarkable legacy of the Harry Clarke Studios following Clarke’s untimely death in 1931 with particular attention to the artistry of Richard King, Clarke’s most talented assistant, whose windows at St. Joseph’s reveal both the influence of his master and the emergence of his own distinctive artistic voice.

Through stories, images, and close observation of the windows themselves, attendees will gain a deeper appreciation of the craftsmanship, symbolism, colour, and spirituality that make St. Joseph’s one of Dublin’s hidden treasures.

Following the talk, visitors will be invited to remain in the church to view the windows at close quarters, allowing ample opportunity to appreciate the intricate detail and luminous beauty of these remarkable works of Irish art.

title: HENNA-TASTIC! Design your own Henna.
description:
HENNA-TASTIC! Design Your Own Henna is an interactive, family-friendly cultural experience that invites people of all ages, backgrounds, and abilities to explore the beauty and symbolism of traditional henna art in a fun, creative, and inclusive way.

As part of Culture Night Belfast, participants will have the unique opportunity to design their own henna-inspired artwork before or during the event and then have their design professionally applied as natural henna on the night. This transforms visitors from passive observers into active creators, encouraging self-expression, cultural curiosity, and meaningful engagement with an ancient art form that spans generations and continents.

Henna has been used for thousands of years across South Asia, the Middle East, and North Africa as a form of celebration, storytelling, adornment, and connection. Through HENNA-TASTIC!, participants will learn about the cultural significance of henna while creating a design that reflects their own personality, story, or imagination.

The activity is designed to be welcoming and accessible to everyone regardless of age, culture, artistic experience, or ability. Participants can create simple or intricate designs, making the experience equally enjoyable for children, young people, adults, and older generations.

The project will be led by internationall certified henna artist Binder Tohani. Only 100% natural brown henna will be used, ensuring a safe and authentic cultural experience.

Design it. Wear it. Celebrate Culture!

title: Here, Together
description:
Irish photographer JP Keating has conceived and developed a new community photography project, bringing together members of the Riverchapel Ladies Club and Asylum Seekers living at the Courtown Hotel IPAS Centre. The resulting exhibition,” Here, Together. ” opens at 6pm on Friday, 18 September at Christ Church Old School, Gorey, as part of Culture Night 2026. Here, Together. creates a welcoming and informal space in which participants and members of the public can meet, experience the work and consider the connections that can exist between people whose lives may initially appear disparate.
The  exhibition combines photographs created by the participants with Keating’s portraits and documentary work. It explores themes including home, belonging, vulnerability and routine, while drawing attention to both the similarities and contrasts between the participants’ experiences.   The project was conceived, developed and artistically led by JP Keating, with support from Creative Ireland , Wexford County Council Local Authority Integration Team and Age Friendly Wexford.

title: History and Music at Collon Church of Ireland
description:
Collon Church opened in 1815 and was modelled on the Chapel of King’s College, Cambridge. It is collegiate in style, with the seating facing across the aisle.

It was commissioned by Speaker John Foster, the last Speaker of the Irish Parliament, dissolved in 1800.  The splendid plasterwork ceiling was designed by Daniel Augustus Beaufort, reflecting the stone vault of King’s, and was worked on by William Edgeworth, brother of the novelist Maria Edgeworth. The stained-glass windows are unique, especially the east window – a depiction of the night sky with stars, the moon and planets. Outside are the graves of a Russian aristocratic family who escaped the revolution in 1917 and lived in Collon from the 1930s to the 1960s.

One memorial is to a niece of the Foster family who, when in Rome, turned down the attentions of a young man from the papal guard, who in later life entered the priesthood and progressed to become Pope. Another memorial is to a member of the Louth Militia – reflecting the troubled times of the late 18th and early 19th C.

Outside is a memorial to a Victoria Cross recipient and others from World War 1.

The organ is a recently restored original Telford instrument dated 1893.

Reflecting its architectural and historic status, the Church was recently upgraded in the architectural records from regional importance to national importance

On Friday 18 September the programme will be in two parts. In the first part, speakers from the Louth Archaeological and Historical Society will show the building and speak about the history and associations.

In the second part, organists will speak about and play the historic Telford organ along with other musicians and singers.

The programme of historical talks and music will be repeated on the hour every hour, starting at 6 pm and repeated at 7 p.m., 8 p.m. and 9 p.m.

Everybody is welcome to drop in during the above hours for an enjoyable evening of music and local history and to experience the atmosphere of this unique building.

Visitors before 7 p.m. can see the stained glass in daylight.  Admission is free.

title: House Museums Of Language – Identity, Literature and Cultural Memory in Slovenia and Ireland
description:
This Culture Night, the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia opens its doors to present the exhibition House Museums Of Language. The exhibition thematically interweaves figures, places, and ideas from Slovenia and Ireland, exploring the role of language in national revival, poetry and nation building, artists and society, landscape and memory and the world beyond borders.

Through the works and museum houses of key Slovenian and Irish authors and poets, the exhibition explores how language, literature, and cultural circles helped shape the national identity of Slovenia and Ireland even before the emergence of the nation states in their modern forms.

These themes are brought out in the works of: Matija Čop and Douglas Hyde; France Prešeren and W. B. Yeats; Ivan Cankar and Oscar Wilde; Simon Gregorčič and Seamus Heaney; and Alma M. Karlin and James Joyce.

Pairing the homes and contexts authors were brought up in, with the works that they created, museum houses are presented as spaces in which ideas were born, and which preserve the stories of the people who helped shape the linguistic and cultural memory of their nations.

The exhibition has an online introduction at the following page: visitzirovnica.si/en/house-museums-of-language-slovenia-ireland

title: How I Became A Wave
description:
Join us in Kinsale for an evening of music with How I Became A Wave, supported by Róisín Harbison. Set against the beautiful surroundings of St.Catherine’s Cultural Centre, this is sure to be a memorable and magical evening of live music!

How I Became A Wave arrives quietly. The shapeshifting orchestral folk project fronted by Pat Carey brings together some of Ireland’s most respected musicians, who take their places on stage around a small orchestra of guitar, cello, violin, pedal steel, keyboard, saxophone and percussion. For anyone seeing them for the first time, it’s hard to guess what’s coming.

In Ireland, How I Became A Wave shows have become known as places where something happens that can’t quite be repeated. Songs metamorphose mid-performance; a quiet lullaby ripples outward and swells into soaring orchestral harmony – and no two nights sound the same. Carey’s voice anchors it all, vulnerable and powerful in the same breath. Audiences at their sold-out shows describe the songs taking on a life of their own, enveloping the room in an incorporeal beauty that is felt long after the last note has been played.

How I Became A Wave’s self-titled debut album, released in March 2026, was met with instant critical acclaim — praised as “flawless” by The Irish Times, “deeply compelling” by Hot Press, and an album that “begs to be listened to” by RTÉ, among many others.

Though still a young project, How I Became A Wave is Carey’s most ambitious undertaking to date, and one that extends well beyond music. At its core is a deep, multidisciplinary collaborative approach: Carey has drawn a wide circle of respected artists into the HIBAW world, spanning visual art, film, poetry and literature, alongside music.

That circle includes Cormac McCarthy (RTÉ Concert Orchestra, Iarla Ó Lionáird), who arranged strings and keys for the album; David Murphy, whose latest record has drawn praise from Uncut to The Guardian; Carey’s former Hard Ground bandmates Davie Ryan and Hugh Dillon; and his regular touring band — Kealan Kenny, Dylan Howe, Julieanne Quirke, Maria Ryan, Kaitlin Cullen-Verhauz and more.

Over the past 18 months, How I Became A Wave has opened for Lisa O’Neill, Villagers, Gemma Hayes, Lisa Hannigan, Joan Shelley, Ailbhe Reddy, Niamh Regan and John Spillane, and played festivals including Sounds From A Safe Harbour, Quiet Lights, Beyond The Pale, Galway Folk Festival, Forest Fest and Your Roots Are Showing. Their album launch shows at Dublin’s Unitarian Church and Cork’s Coughlan’s both sold out to rave reviews.

The album draws as much from poetry, literature and landscape as it does from music. Echoes of Max Porter, Eavan Boland, Sylvia Plath, Sara Baume and Claire Keegan run through it alongside the influence of Paul Buchanan, Big Thief, Anaïs Mitchell, Bon Iver and Nils Frahm, resulting in music that carries incredible strength in its vulnerability.

How I Became A Wave are currently in the studio working on new material.

 

Róisín Harbison hails from Limerick and has been playing music for over 20 years.

She began with classical violin at the Limerick School of Music and subsequently studied at the Dublin Conservatory of Music, performing with several orchestras including the University of Limerick Orchestra and Hibernian Symphony Orchestra. More recently, she has taken to the stage with Limerick-based rock band Raging Sons, having recorded on their album, 20:20.

Róisín began playing the harp at the age of nine, learning at the Irish Harp Centre in Limerick. As a member of the Irish Harp Orchestra, she has performed throughout Ireland and toured internationally in Germany, Austria, and the UK. She is also a regular contributor to the Irish traditional session scene. Her musical interests span classical, Irish traditional and contemporary music, bringing together the different influences that have shaped her playing throughout her life.

In support of How I Became a Wave, Róisín will perform a range of pieces showcasing the depth, character, and versatility of the Irish harp.

title: Huaquitos, create your own personal interpretation
description:
Huaquitos: Create Your Own Personal Interpretation is a participatory ceramic workshop that invites the public to discover an ancient Peruvian artistic tradition through contemporary making. Inspired by the huacos of pre-Columbian Peru—ceramic vessels that documented everyday life, nature, spirituality, and identity—participants will create their own personal interpretation of this iconic form.

Working with red earthenware clay, participants will explore hand-building techniques while learning about the cultural significance of the asa estribo (stirrup handle), one of the defining features of the huaco. Rather than reproducing historical artefacts, the workshop encourages each participant to respond creatively, transforming the traditional form into a personal expression inspired by animals, people, memories, or stories that are meaningful to them.

The workshop is designed for participants aged eight years and over and is suitable for complete beginners as well as those with previous experience. Through modelling clay and solving the challenge of incorporating the stirrup handle into their design, participants will develop spatial awareness, creative thinking, and confidence in working three-dimensionally. The relaxed pace of the session encourages conversation, curiosity, and shared making.

Using Culture Night as a platform for cultural exchange, this workshop creates a dialogue between Peruvian and Irish communities, celebrating how traditional crafts can connect people across cultures through creativity. All works will be bisque fired after the event, allowing participants to take home a lasting ceramic piece that commemorates both their experience and the cultural story behind it.

Huaquitos: Cruthaigh Do Léirmhíniú Pearsanta Féin

Is ceardlann rannpháirteach chriadóireachta é Huaquitos: Cruthaigh Do Léirmhíniú Pearsanta Féin a thugann deis don phobal traidisiún ársa ceirmeach na Peiriú a fhiosrú trí chruthaitheacht agus trí obair lámhdhéanta. Bunaithe ar na huacos – soithí ceirmeacha ó chultúir réamh-Cholumbacha na Peiriú a léirigh an saol laethúil, an dúlra, an spioradáltacht agus an fhéiniúlacht – tabharfar cuireadh do rannpháirtithe a léirmhíniú pearsanta féin ar an bhfoirm íocónach seo a chruthú.

Ag obair le cré dhearg nádúrtha, foghlaimeoidh rannpháirtithe bunscileanna tógála de láimh agus tabharfar léargas dóibh ar thábhacht an asa estribo (an láimhseáil chorraigh), gné shainiúil den huaco. In ionad cóipeanna de dhéantáin stairiúla a dhéanamh, spreagfar iad chun a gcuid smaointe féin a chur in iúl trí chruthanna atá bunaithe ar ainmhithe, ar dhaoine, ar chuimhní nó ar scéalta pearsanta.

Tá an cheardlann oiriúnach do dhaoine 8 mbliana d’aois agus níos sine, agus níl aon taithí roimh ré ag teastáil. Trí chré a mhúnlú agus an dúshlán a bhaineann leis an láimhseáil chorraigh a chomhtháthú sa dearadh a réiteach, forbróidh rannpháirtithe feasacht spásúil, smaointeoireacht chruthaitheach agus muinín i ndearadh tríthoiseach.

Mar chuid d’Oíche Chultúir, cruthaíonn an tionscadal seo deis do mhalartú cultúrtha idir pobail na hÉireann agus na Peiriú, ag léiriú conas is féidir le ceardaíocht thraidisiúnta daoine a thabhairt le chéile trí chruthaitheacht. Déanfar bácáil bhriosca ar gach píosa i ndiaidh na ceardlainne, ionas go mbeidh cuimhne bhuan ag rannpháirtithe ar an taithí agus ar an gcultúr a spreag í.

Blending fine art photography, storytelling, set design, costume, and collaborative art-making, the exhibition presents a series of cinematic, narrative-driven works that blur the boundaries between photography, installation, and theatre. Through immersive visual storytelling, participants have created handcrafted worlds inspired by imagination, play, curiosity, and human connection.
Alongside large-scale collaborative works, the exhibition features individual photographic projects that reveal each artist’s distinctive creative voice and visual language. Developed through mentoring, experimentation, and collaborative making, New Frames encourages artists to take creative risks, challenge conventional visual narratives, and present ambitious original work to the public.
Featuring works by Sarah Howard, Daiva O’Dwyer, Jenna Barry, Grace Frawley, Cadhla O’Mahony, Meadhbh Hennessy, Karolina Sobocińska, Jack Martin, and Laura Macijauskaitė, Imagined Worlds celebrates accessible arts participation while fostering collaboration, confidence, and cultural engagement through the power of shared creativity.

title: In the Making, Natures Synchrony Art with Caitríona Sheedy
description:
A performance of songs, rhythmic melodies and lyrics inspired by nature and the human spirit, followed by time to explore and interact with the larger project.

Nature’s Synchrony Art is centred on the land in the Burren and explores the energies that flow through us, what nurtures us, and the relationship between mind, matter, creativity and possibility.

A jar will be provided, inviting you to add your hopes and wishes.

Caitríona’s practice is guided intuitively while remaining intentionally focused on the journey. It began with painting 25 years ago, learning to trust the process and explore this guiding phenomenon. Her work examines how the mind and emotions, together with the seen and unseen energies within our environment, express something greater than the initially perceived version of reality. The process evolved into creating immersive spaces and large-scale installations, before expanding into melody making, songwriting and performance.

Now, Caitríona synchronistically weaves together the experience of remote living on the land, surrounded by cliffs and sea, with care for family, friends, nature, the human experience, and research into cognitive science. Ultimately, this work is about our power as creators, both individually and collectively.

title: In the Shadow of the Glen
description:
This Culture Night, Grapefruit Moon Drama Group brings J. M. Synge’s powerful one-act play In the Shadow of the Glen to the intimate setting of Matt Molloy’s Yard Bar in Westport.

First performed in 1903, Synge’s play is a darkly comic and provocative exploration of marriage, loneliness, freedom and the restrictions placed upon women in rural Ireland. Set in a remote cottage in the Wicklow mountains, the story centres on Nora Burke, a young woman trapped in a loveless marriage to Dan. When Dan appears to die suddenly, Nora is confronted with the possibility of freedom — but what initially seems like an escape from an unhappy marriage quickly becomes something far more complicated.

Synge’s work is renowned for its distinctive language, humour and unflinching portrayal of rural Irish life. More than a century after it was written, In the Shadow of the Glen remains surprisingly relevant, raising questions about relationships, independence, social expectations and the choices available to women.

For this Culture Night performance, Grapefruit Moon is particularly interested in bringing Synge’s work out of the traditional theatre and into the community. After a successful summer run in Matt Molloy’s Yard bar, the venue provides an atmospheric and unconventional setting for the play, allowing audiences to experience the drama at close quarters. Rather than creating a formal divide between performer and audience, the pub environment creates an intimate theatrical experience where the audience becomes almost a part of the world of the play.

The performance also reflects the spirit of Culture Night: making culture accessible, bringing people together and celebrating Ireland’s rich artistic heritage in unexpected places.

Grapefruit Moon Drama Group is a local, grassroots theatre group committed to creating opportunities for people to participate in drama and theatre outside traditional theatrical.

The Culture Night performance will offer audiences an opportunity not simply to watch a piece of Irish theatre, but to encounter it in a setting that feels connected to the culture and community from which the play emerged. The atmosphere of Matt Molloy’s Yard, combined with live performance and Synge’s extraordinary language, creates a theatrical experience that is intimate, immediate and distinctly West of Ireland.

By presenting In the Shadow of the Glen in Matt Molloy’s Yard for Culture Night, Grapefruit Moon hopes to demonstrate that theatre does not have to take place behind the doors of a conventional theatre. It can happen in pubs, community spaces and other familiar places, bringing people together and allowing stories that form part of Ireland’s cultural heritage to live again in the communities of today.

A classic Irish play. A local cast. An unconventional stage. One unforgettable night of theatre.

title: In-conversation with Artist John Noel Smith and Curator Margarita Cappock

Born in Dublin, John Noel Smith is a critically acclaimed contemporary artist known for his powerful non-figurative paintings and sculptural installations. Following his art school education in Dublin and Germany, Smith lived and worked in Berlin for more than 20 years. He has been based in Ireland since 2002.

Smith’s paintings explore the convergence of personal memory, cultural history and the formal language of abstraction. These are works with universal resonance that speak of the persistence of conflict and global challenges; contrasting systems are embedded within the fabric of the painting, bridging the interplay between abstraction, narrative, intellect and emotion.

John Noel Smith is a member of Aosdána and his work is included in important museum, institutional and private collections around the world.

title: Indian Classical music concert
description:
Indian Music and Sitar Concepts with Adam Brennan
Adam Brennan has been studying the sitar and Indian classical music for over 10 years. Coming from a background in audio technology and music, he has developed a deep appreciation for Hindustani classical music and enjoys sharing and collaborating across both Indian and Western musical traditions.

Adam has performed with renowned artists such as Liam Ó Maonlaí, including performances for RTÉ, and teaches Hindustani classical music to a growing number of students.

He continues his own studies through weekly lessons with his highly respected teacher, Ustad Dharambir Singh Ji.

For this concert, Adam will present a solo sitar performance alongside a short introduction to the foundations of Hindustani classical music. He will explore the relationship between raag—the melodic framework—and taal—the rhythmic framework—and demonstrate how the two interconnect to create space for improvisation, expression and new musical ideas.

title: Inner Landscape: Photography Lecture & Self-Portrait Workshop
description:
A short lecture on the history of self-portraiture in photography, followed by a hands-on workshop where participants create their own self-portraits using their cameras or smartphones – covering composition, light, and concept.

Participants take home an assignment, and finished images are printed for review and display.

The lecture traces how self-portrait photography emerged and evolved from early experiments to today, exploring the different reasons artists turn the camera on themselves: self-exploration, protest, identity, and documentation.

It also touches on how self-portraiture can positively support mental wellbeing through reflection, self-acceptance, and reclaiming self-representation.

In the workshop, participants will learn core principles of creating a photograph, including composition and working with available light, and put them into practice during the session.

Afterward, participants take home a practical assignment. Once completed, each participant’s finished image will be printed on fine art paper and given a personal review.

On Culture Night, guests will first be welcomed to the IIEA’s Georgian townhouse to view a curated and interactive exhibition, that will showcase Ireland’s European story including debates during the Lisbon and Nice referenda, moments from Eurovision, and other cultural and political moments. Aodhán Ó Ríordáin MEP, Member of the European Parliament
Emma Richardson, Senior Researcher at the IIEA

title: Joyful Stitching – The Harvest Season
description:
Join local textile artist Tamara Fiabane for a joyful, intergenerational stitching workshop celebrating the abundance, stories and traditions of the harvest season.

No previous experience is needed — just curiosity and a willingness to try!

Harvest time has traditionally been a time of gathering, sharing and celebrating what the land provides. Yet with supermarkets offering almost everything all year round, many of us lost the connection with seasonal food, local harvests and the people who grow and produce it.

This workshop reconnects us with those traditions away from technology. Older generations can share stories of sitting around a table with grandparents, knitting, sewing or making lace by candlelight, while younger generations discover these skills and stories for themselves.

For Tamara, stitching is much more than making something beautiful. For over ten years, she has created spaces where people connect through craft. A simple needle, thread and piece of fabric can cross language and generational barriers, allowing people to teach, learn and create together.

Come stitch, share, learn, laugh and create something beautiful together.

title: Kantos Quartet – Centenaries
description:
KANTOS QUARTET
Sarah Sew, violin
Hugh Murray, violin
Alexandros Koustas, viola
Aoife Burke, cello
This is an exciting new string quartet comprising four of our finest and most experienced musicians. Their programme looks both to music and events of the 1920s and to the upcoming bi-centenary of Beethoven’s death in 1827. Beethoven’s B flat quartet moves from a sprightly opening movement, through a gentle adagio and a wildly irregular scherzo, to its heart, a moving slow introduction to the finale which Beethoven entitled La Malinconia. The finale itself is curiously enigmatic, as if unsure how to react to the pathos of its opening.
Pulitzer prize winning composer Caroline Shaw took this Beethoven quartet as the blueprint of her 2016 quartet of that name and its transformation is both fascinating and entertaining. Irish-American composer Swan Hennessy’s beautiful second string quartet was written in memory of Terence MacSwiney, shortly after his death on hunger strike in 1920, the piece was premiered by four Dublin-based musicians at the World Congress of the Irish Race in Paris on the evening of 25 January 1922. The audience included Éamon de Valera, Countess Markievicz and Mary MacSwiney (sister of Terence). Leoš Janáček’s first string quartet Kreutzer Sonata was written in 1923 and inspired by Tolstoy’s novella of the same name, the music is raw, fragmented and intensely direct. Sudden contrasts and restless rhythmic energy create a compelling sense of drama.

‘Shorts for Wee Ones’ – 4:45pm

This collection of seven short films from around the world is sure to delight and amuse our youngest viewers. Featuring curious capybaras, chef mushrooms, colourful body cells, woodland animals, an affectionate (and very hungry) crocodile, a voiceless cockerel, and a little girl who best communicates through drawings; the films in this programme focus on friendship and accepting difference; as well as promoting cooperation and understanding. All of these short films are dialogue free except for one film in English. These magical tales will delight children age 3+ and are a colourful introduction to the cinema experience. Runtime: 50 min.

‘Shorts for Families’ – 6pm

This collection of short films for age 7+ explores how curiosity drives our characters forward: a little girl discovers the universe outside of her phone screen; a robot bee working on a hive on Mars finds out the strange powers of an odd plant; Lola finds a powerful way to communicate with her neurodiverse brother; a child accompanied by an otter-like creature sets out to find a cure for water shortage; and a mischievous little wolf gets everyone involved in a messy, playful way of life. All of these short films are dialogue free except for one film in French with English subtitles. Runtime: 70 min.

Entrance is free, but booking is essential. Booking opens 10am on 29th August.

title: Lakelands Screening
description:
Join Harp Media for a special Culture Night screening of the acclaimed Irish feature film Lakelands, followed by an exclusive live Q&A with the filmmakers.

Set in the Irish Midlands, Lakelands tells the story of Cian, a young man struggling to find purpose after the end of his football career. Quietly powerful and deeply rooted in contemporary rural Ireland, the film explores identity, masculinity, friendship and the challenge of moving forward when life doesn’t unfold as expected.

Written and directed by Longford filmmakers Robert Higgins and Patrick McGivney, Lakelands premiered to critical acclaim, winning Best Irish Film at the Galway Film Fleadh and going on to receive four Irish Film & Television Academy (IFTA) nominations. The film has been praised for its authentic performances, naturalistic storytelling and honest portrayal of life in the Midlands.

Following the screening, audiences will have the opportunity to hear directly from the filmmakers about the making of the film, from writing and financing the project to production, festivals and distribution. There will also be an open audience Q&A, offering a rare opportunity to ask questions about the creative process and the realities of making independent cinema in Ireland.

Whether you’re a film lover, an aspiring filmmaker or simply looking for a unique Culture Night experience, this free event celebrates Irish storytelling, regional creativity and the growing film culture of the Midlands.

Bí páirteach le Harp Media do scannánú speisialta Oíche Chultúir den fhíseán mór Éireannach cáiliúil Lakelands, agus é leanaithe ag Q&A beo eisiach leis na cruthaitheoirí scannáin. Suite i lár-cheantair na hÉireann, insíonn Lakelands scéal Chiana, fear óg ag streachailt chun cuspóra a aimsiú tar éis deireadh a shaoil phearsanta sacar. Cumhachtach gan ifreann agus fréamhaithe go domhain i ndúiche na hÉireann nua-aimseartha, iniúchann an scannán féiniúlacht, firinscne, cairdeas agus dúshlán dul ar aghaidh nuair nach dtéann an saol mar a bheartaítear. Scríofa agus stiúrtha ag cruthaitheoirí scannán Longphort, Robert Higgins agus Patrick McGivney, cuireadh fáilte chriticiúil roimh Lakelands, ag buachan Scannán Éireannach is Fearr ag Fleadh Scannán na Gaillimhe agus ag fáil ceithre ainmniúchán ón nGréasáin Scannán & Teilifís Éireannach (IFTA). Tá an scannán moladh as a léirithe barántúla, scéalaíocht nádúrtha agus cur síos macánta ar shaol i lár na hÉireann.

Scríofa agus stiúrtha ag mórfhimléirí Longfoirt, Robert Higgins agus Patrick McGivney, d’fhóirsteódh Lakelands tosaigh ar léirmheasanna criticiúla, ag buaicphointí Péirseach le Scannán Nua-Éireanach ag Féile Scannán na Gaillimhe agus ag dul ar aghaidh chun ceithre ainmniúchán a fháil ó Acadamh na Scannán & Teilifíse Éireann (IFTA). Tá an scannán molta as a léiriúcháin fhíorúla, scéalaíocht nádúrtha agus léiriú macánta ar an saol sna Lárdchontae.

Tar éis an taispeántais, beidh deis ag an lucht féachana éisteacht go díreach leis na déantóirí faoin gcaoi ar cuireadh an scannán le chéile, ó scríobh agus airgeadas a fháil don tionscadal go dtí táirgeadh, féilte agus dáileadh. Beidh seisiún ceisteanna agus freagraí oscailte ann freisin, ag tairgiú deise annamh do cheisteanna a chur faoin bpróiseas cruthaitheach agus faoi réaltachtaí cinéama neamhspleách a dhéanamh in Éirinn.

Cibé an lucht leanúna scannán tú, eagarthóir scannán ag tús céime, nó díreach ag lorg taithí uathúil oíche na Cultúir, ceiliúrtar an ócáid shábháilte seo scéalaithe Éireannach, cruthaitheacht réigiúnach agus cultúr scannán atá ag fás i lár na tíre.

So, Culture Night 2026 kicks off in style with an exciting warm-up at the Clarke Museum of Irish History, on Walsh Street. Come join us at 6 PM to get the evening started with vibrant energy! We’ll begin with the delightful ‘Cuimsiú’ session, led by the talented Hannah Dunford and her amazing friends, creating a truly inclusive and joyous atmosphere. Following on we will be treated to the dynamic sounds of the Bofield Ceili Band, whose lively tunes will get everyone dancing, along with the mesmerising rhythms of Atlantic Rhythm/Moffatt School of Dancing, bringing a fusion of musical styles that will captivate and energise the crowd.” for the kick-off our “Lanes & Sessions at 7pm,

To follow the sounds and discover all the different types of music hiding around every corner. It’s a musical treasure hunt through the town!

title: LATE EXHIBITION OPENING: Closer Look by Máiréad Holohan
description:
Máiréad Holohan is an artist from Kilkenny, based in the Blackstairs Mountains and her practice is deeply informed by the ecology of her surroundings.

Through a routine of walking and looking, she is drawn to the idea of the ruderal – a plant that takes over areas impacted by human disturbance such as agriculture, habitation and construction. She is specifically interested in the “the things that survive in the cracks” where the natural environment reclaims the manmade stone walls in this local area. This juncture, between the ecological and the human, presents a rich and ancient history that demonstrates the resilience of flora in adapting to these built boundaries.

Máiréad has an eco-friendly practice and uses environmentally kind materials; she is a specialist in natural inks and dyes, creating these from plants in her locality.

For Culture Night, the Tea Houses will host a late opening of the exhibition Closer Look, offering visitors the opportunity to meet Máiréad Holohan and learn more about her practice and the ideas behind the exhibition.

title: Late Gallery Opening: Vanessa Donoso López, ‘(O-O-O)’
description:
Visit Temple Bar Gallery + Studios on Culture Night to see artist Vanessa Donoso López’s solo art exhibition (O-O-O). Reflecting her experiences growing up in Barcelona and living in Ireland for over twenty years, Vanessa Donoso López’s practice explores identity, migration, and cultural behaviours shaped by relocation.

(O-O-O) is shorthand for object oriented ontologies, a metaphysical theory that places all entities: humans, animals, plants, objects, and ideas, and the components that they are made up of, as equal to one another, existing with their own agency and reality. The exhibition explores movement as a strategy for adaptation, resistance and transformation, bringing together many material processes including low-fired ceramics, natural pigments, water and living plants. The resulting immersive installation creates a sensitive ecosystem in a state of ongoing change.

Temple Bar Gallery + Studios is an artists’ studio complex and contemporary art gallery in Dublin City Centre. The Gallery presents five exhibitions annually by Irish and international artists. This is supported by a programme of free talks, tours, screenings and workshops. We produce the annual Dublin Art Book Fair as a platform for artist books and independent publishers with an expansive events programme.

Vanessa Donoso López’s solo art exhibition (O-O-O) is open 24 July — 20 September 2026

title: Lavit Gallery: New Irish Art
description:
New Irish Art brings together a selection of new work by artists working across the island of Ireland.

While Lavit Gallery has a long-standing commitment to championing Cork-based artists, the exhibition also reflects the importance of maintaining a national perspective. By showcasing artists based across Ireland, New Irish Art offers audiences the opportunity to engage with a diverse variety of talent. Many of the featured artists live and work outside their native counties – or indeed their country of origin.

The exhibition title also speaks to the idea of a modern Ireland: one that is less parochial, more fluid and increasingly multicultural, with a national identity that continues to evolve.

Artists participating in the 2026 edition of New Irish Art include Collin Crotty, Gabhann Dunne, Vanessa Jones, Vera Klute, Michael Quane RHA, Michael Kobuladze, Ailbhe Ní Bhriain, Bennie Reilly, John O’Reilly and Charles Tyrrell.

As part of Culture Night, Gallery Director Brian Mac Domhnaill will lead a Collecting Art Talk & Exhibition Tour at 5pm on Friday 18 September. The talk will provide an introduction to the exhibiting artists and their work, while also offering practical insights into starting or developing an art collection, however modest or grand. Suitable for both first-time buyers and established collectors, it is an ideal opportunity to learn more about collecting contemporary Irish art.

Using maps, photographs, recycled materials, drawings, text and personal memories, participants will create individual collage pieces inspired by the places, experiences and communities that make Dublin unique. Throughout the evening these contributions will be assembled into one evolving artwork – a visual portrait of a city shaped by many voices, cultures and perspectives.

The project explores themes of place, belonging, identity and cultural diversity, encouraging conversation and creative exchange between residents, visitors, families and communities from across the city.

As the artwork grows throughout the night, visitors are invited to witness the transformation of individual stories into a collective representation of Dublin’s rich cultural landscape. The completed collage will stand as a celebration of creativity, participation and community spirit at the heart of Culture Night.

title: Life Support
description:
A screening of the urgent new Palestine documentary.

Since October 2023, Gaza has been sealed from the world-except for one group, international doctors. While global media are barred from reporting and governments look away, doctors breach the blockade and what they find is not just a humanitarian crisis, but a calculated dismantling of life itself. Covering the entire two years of the genocide, their first-hand accounts and visceral footage offer a rare and vital chronicle of the daily struggles of healthcare workers as they navigate bombed-out hospitals, dwindling supplies, starvation and the overwhelming influx of casualties – predominantly women and children.

title: Living off the land: Irelands heritage wool crafts from past to present. Demonstration and Talk with Eimear O’Neill
description:
Living off the land: Irelands heritage wool crafts from past to present with Eimear O’Neill.

Wool is an abundant resource in Leitrim, one that was always part of our culture, but has been less valued in recent years.

Eimear O’Neill will show you how to take a sheep’s fleece and turn it into yarn for knitting, just as our ancestors did before us, in a talk and demonstration. Join us to share experiences about this heritage craft, learn how sustainable it is as a method of clothing production (so important in this era of fast fashion!) and see how Irish wool crafts have evolved and modernised in recent years.

This Culture Night, get together with like minded people to share, learn, celebrate the past and start that journey to spin again.

title: Living Willow Dome Workshop
description:
Join us for a hands-on, community-led Living Willow Dome Workshop as part of Culture Night 2026.

Come along and be part of creating something truly special for our community. Together, we will weave, shape and sculpt living willow to create a beautiful natural dome that will become a lasting feature within the park.

This is a collaborative activity where everyone can get involved, learn traditional willow weaving techniques and help bring this unique living structure to life. As the willow grows and changes with the seasons, the dome will become increasingly woven into its surroundings, creating a peaceful and welcoming space for people, families and wildlife to enjoy.

The finished dome will provide a natural place to sit, explore, connect with nature and spend time together. Surrounded by biodiversity-friendly planting, it will offer shade and shelter while becoming a living piece of community art.

Whether you are young or old, experienced or completely new to willow weaving, everyone is welcome to take part. Come along, get your hands involved, meet your neighbours and help us create a living legacy for Durkan Bohola Community Park.

Bring your creativity, enthusiasm and a love of nature and help us grow something wonderful together!

title: Local & International Contemporary Art at Teal House Gallery
description:
On Culture Night, Teal House Gallery becomes a place of encounters—between people and ideas, tradition and innovation, memory and imagination.

Visitors are invited to explore a vibrant creative space where art, design, and making come together. The gallery’s exhibitions, studios, and social spaces will be open throughout the evening, offering a glimpse into the creative journeys that transform simple materials into meaningful works of art.

Artists and makers will share their processes, revealing how inspiration becomes creation through skill, experimentation, and curiosity. Guests can discover painting, illustration, sculpture, contemporary craft, and creative technologies, while taking part in hands-on activities suitable for all ages.

Teal House Gallery is more than an exhibition space. It is a place where cultures meet, stories are shared, and creativity becomes a bridge between generations. Founded on the belief that creativity belongs to everyone, the gallery brings together artists, learners, makers, and the wider community in a spirit of exploration and connection.

Culture Night offers an opportunity not simply to view art, but to become part of a living creative community. Visitors will find an evening filled with discovery, conversation, and inspiration in the heart of Dublin.

Nicola Coughlan (Bridgerton) joins Éanna Hardwicke (The Sixth Commandment) and Siobhán McSweeney (Derry Girls) in John Millington Synge’s riveting play of youth and self-discovery. Pegeen Flaherty’s life is turned upside down when a young man walks into her pub claiming that he’s killed his father. Instead of being shunned, the killer becomes a local hero and begins to win hearts, that is until a second man unexpectedly arrives on the scene.

The Rocket’s Red Glare is a new solo exhibition by Barbara Diener exploring the contested legacy of Wernher von Braun and the ways history is shaped, remembered, and rewritten. Weaving together photography, archival material, and family images

title: Make Your Mark
description:
Make Your Mark: A Printmaking Lab transforms Boomerang Cafe into a temporary public print studio for Culture Night 2026. From 5.30pm–9.30pm, visitors are invited to drop in and take part in free, open-access printmaking activities. There are no scheduled workshops, booking requirements or previous experience needed—people can observe, experiment or create at their own pace.
Throughout the evening, the space operates as a live studio, with the artist and assistant continuously demonstrating techniques, supporting participants and encouraging informal, hands-on engagement. Using pre-prepared lino blocks, stamps, textures and monoprint processes, participants create unique prints through layering, mark-making and creative play. The focus is on exploration and self-expression rather than technical skill, making the activity welcoming and accessible for all ages and abilities.
Using fast-drying, water-based inks, participants can take their finished print home the same evening. They are also invited to contribute a second print to a collaborative display that grows throughout the event, creating a temporary exhibition celebrating the creativity and diversity of everyone who takes part.
The project particularly aims to engage young people while remaining open to all Culture Night visitors. By activating Boomerang Cafe—a venue not traditionally included in the Culture Night programme—it introduces new audiences to printmaking while showcasing the creative potential of the youth centre as a welcoming cultural space.

As the evening progresses, the studio will gradually transform into an immersive artwork built from all of the individual voices, gestures and impressions turning into a collective portrait celebrating creativity, connection and community.

title: Meet Casimir Markievicz: A Polish Artist in Bohemian Dublin
description:
This Culture Night, visitors are invited to the Polish House to meet Casimir Markievicz, the prolific Polish artist who was at the heart of Bohemian Dublin in the early twentieth century, and husband to the remarkable Irish revolutionary Constance Markievicz.

Casimir and Constance will welcome guests and guide them through an exhibition exploring their lives, artistic achievements, and enduring legacy. They may even offer visitors a glass of wine along the way if they fancy!

While the name Markievicz is most often associated with Irish revolutionary heroine Constance, this exhibition shines a spotlight on the life and work of Casimir Markievicz (1874–1932), a painter, playwright, and larger-than-life personality – and his place in Dublin’s bohemian circles on the eve of the Revolution.

Together, Casimir and Constance helped establish key institutions including the United Arts Club and the Municipal Gallery, while Casimir’s plays were performed at venues such as the Abbey Theatre and the Gaiety Theatre.

The panel exhibition brings together compelling examples of Casimir’s art along with artefacts and photographs, drawn from major public and private collections in Ireland and Poland. It also explores links between Ireland, Poland, and Ukraine (where Casimir’s family lived), and the influence of Polish nationalism on Constance’s own political outlook.

 

This event is part of the European Culture Trail – a EUNIC Ireland (European Union National Institutes for Culture) in cooperation with the European Commission Representation in Ireland.

Following international festival seasons, standout performances at Other Voices and Ireland Music Week, and the acclaimed release of her electronic hip-hop project ‘ISSA NEW ERA!’, the Galway-born star continues her rapid rise into 2026. Recent highlights include showcasing at SHARPE in Slovakia, opening for Biig Piig, supporting US rap sensation CupcakKe, and appearances at Cork Jazz Weekend and Other Voices. title: Memory Lane / Historical Art Trail Castlerea
description:
Memory lane is an historical Art trail based around Castlerea Co. Roscommon, comprised of a collection of 2D and 3D artworks created by GRETB art students.

Each artwork is inspired by various historical events and stories based around Castlerea, from the town’s origins to modern times. The Artworks will be on display in the Trinity Arts Centre for Culture Night. The locations of the events that inspired the artworks, are signposted at specified locations around town. The trail incorporates a scenic walk through the Demesne and town centre.

title: Memory of a Free Festival – Late Opening & Gallery Tour
description:
For Culture Night, Wexford Arts Centre are pleased to present a late opening and gallery tour of the
exhibition Memory of a Free Festival.

Memory of a Free Festival responds to the Carnsore Point anti-nuclear festivals that took place in
Wexford between 1978 and 1981. Organised by a coalition of groups, the festivals were attended by
thousands of people. These legions were unified by their shared opposition to what would have been
the first nuclear power plant to be built in Ireland. In addition to musical entertainment and lectures,
the free festivals also included workshops and exhibitions.

Featuring works by Orla Barry, Brian Duggan and Alanna O’Kelly, the exhibition also includes photos by
Derek Speirs and original archival material produced by the Irish Anti-Nuclear Movement.

The gallery tour is free but booking is essential. To book a place please contact Wexford Arts Centre
on 053 9123764 or log on to www.wexfordartscentre.ie.
