title: Milling About – Culture in Every Corner
description:
For Culture Night, Bolands Mills comes alive with music, art, performance and storytelling, with something happening around every corner of the historic Dublin landmark.

Across its squares, studios, cafés, bars, salons and community spaces, the programme brings together some of Ireland’s most exciting creative talent alongside local voices and stories, with street food and bars adding to the atmosphere and making Bolands Mills a place to settle in for the evening.

At The Factory, a building with an extraordinary musical history, three distinctive Irish acts take to the main stage:
● Sorcha Richardson, the Choice Music Prize-nominated songwriter whose first two albums both reached the Irish Top 5, arrives fresh from the release of her third album.
● AE MAK brings her distinctive, theatrical take on contemporary folk, following performances at festivals including Reading & Leeds, Latitude and Iceland Airwaves.
● Zaska, the genre-blurring collective led by guitarist and songwriter Max Zaska, brings together funk, jazz, R&B and hip-hop. Over the years, Max has collaborated with some of Ireland’s most exciting artists, including Hozier, Denise Chaila, Soda Blonde and Gemma Dunleavy.

Out in Bolands Square, street artist Kevin Bohan (K-Bone) and poet Cormac Fitzgerald create a new community-inspired artwork live on the night.

At Grindstone Coffee, DJ and chef Marcus O’Laoire takes to the decks for a vinyl session inspired by artists with connections to Bolands Mills over the years, from Bowie and Britney to Bono.

Inside Don’t Kill My Vibe, In the Chair transforms the salon into an intimate storytelling space, where local people share the memories, humour and experiences of a community that has lived through, and helped shape, the transformation of the area.

At Reformation, free movement micro-sessions offer a chance to slow things down, and take a moment to pause between experiences.

Round off the evening in Daphni, where experimental jazz collective Bricknasty strip things back for an intimate set in one of Bolands Mills’ most atmospheric corners.

Free and open to all from 6.30pm-9.30pm. With music, food and drinks across the site, and the night continuing later at Daphni, Culture Night at Bolands Mills is designed to be explored, experienced and made a night of.

title: Movie Screening: Once Upon a Time in a Cinema
description:
In celebration of Culture Night we present a very special FREE screening of Once Upon a Time in Cinema.
Running a small-town cinema in the mid-1980s has taken its toll on owner Earl Clancy, and he is now considering selling the site. For now, however, the show must go on. On a busy Friday night, Earl must deal with a series of unfolding disasters, from disgruntled customers to unwanted rodent visitors. On top of all that, he’s the projectionist for the night and has to ensure the film stays on screen. As the evening becomes ever more chaotic, Earl grapples with the legacy and future of the cinema he has devoted his life to.
Writer / director David Gleeson’s charming comedy-drama is a celebration of the film-going experience, beautifully recapturing the vibe of a classic, ramshackle and very Irish cinema.

title: Mummers Hat workshop
description:
Come build a Mummer’s Hat at Sigginstown Castle! Join a fun and creative workshop with Street Artist Caoimhe Dunn to make your own straw hat as might have been used in the past by Mummers, Wren Boys and Masquers in Ireland and across Europe. The ancient tradition of Mumming still exists, and Sigginstown Castle regularly hosts a Mumming performance of the folk-play. The Wexford Mummers wear different hats now but may have originated in these straw varieties. Creative possibilities abound.

Join us for two hours of creative collaboration in the historical and beautiful setting of Sigginstown Castle.
The event will be inside the Coach House.

This workshop is designed for adults. Young people aged 13 and over are welcome to attend when accompanied by a parent or guardian.

Booking required.

title: Music in Calary: concert by Lynda O’Connor (violin) and Ailbhe O’Connor (cello)
description:
The concert will be performed by Lynda O’Connor (violin) and Ailbhe O’Connor (cello). They will play pieces by Ailbhe McDonagh, Astor Piazzola, the Handel Halvorsen Passacaglia for violin and cello, Jules Massenet, Johan Sebastian Bach and Ludwig van Beethoven.

Lynda O’Connor is one of Ireland’s leading violinists, celebrated for her dynamic performances and artistic range. She has enjoyed a vibrant international career as soloist, chamber musician and orchestral leader. Lynda has performed with Camerata Ireland, the International Mahler Orchestra and the RTE orchestras, appearing in prestigious venues such as Carnegie Hall, Cadogan Hall and Theatre des Champs Elysees.

A dedicated musician, Lynda is a founding member of the Ficino Ensemble, Belisama Trio and Trio Elatha and has collaborated with musicians including Barry Douglas and John O’Conor.

Ailbhe McDonagh is an internationally recognised cellist and composer, known for her work as both a soloist and chamber musician.

As an accomplished chamber musician, she has collaborated with the acclaimed pianist John O’Conor, with her sister Orla McDonagh, and with violinist Lynda O’Connor. She is a member of the Ficino Ensemble and the traditional Irish music crossover group Trio Elatha.
Ailbhe is also an established composer with over 250 published works and commissions to her name. She is a widely commissioned and celebrated composer with a breadth of works written for orchestra, chamber music and solo instruments.

title: MUTM Culture Night – Jayne Pomplas, Luke Coffey & Patrick Stefan
description:

Their sound combines virtuosic fiddle, driving banjo, intricate guitar, rich vocal harmony, and original material, moving easily between energetic instrumental sets and intimate songs.

Pomplas is a multiple Fleadh Cheoil-winning fiddle player, vocalist, and composer rooted in the New York–Sligo tradition, with releases spanning traditional albums and original songs.

Coffey, one of Ireland’s leading contemporary banjo players, is a founding member of Mules & Men and a key figure in the group’s “acid-Celtgrass” sound.

Stefan is an award-winning Dublin-based singer-songwriter and guitarist whose work has featured on RTÉ Radio 1, BBC’s Across The Line, and Spotify editorial playlists.

Together, they bring deep musical knowledge, extensive touring experience, and a natural instinct for collaboration, creating performances that are technically impressive, emotionally engaging, and full of live energy.

title: Nano Nagle Place – Film Screening, Exhibitions & Open Museum
description:
Nano Nagle Place will host a range of activities this Culture Night.

1. Ceangailte: A New Collaborative Audiovisual Exhibition – Global Hub 5pm to 9pm
Ceangailte by David Mathúna and Jake Riordan explores how media representations shape narratives of colonialism, oppression, and resilience through a dynamic dual-screen display, immersive audio and sculptural elements. Drawing on the Irish word ceangailte (the definitions of which approximate “tied”, “connected”, or “bound”), ‘Ceangailte’ weaves together a multiplicity of perspectives from former colonies of Empire, reflecting on power structures and emancipatory aspirations. By juxtaposing establishment narratives with harsh realities, it invites viewers to confront what is outwardly expressed by mainstream media and what is internally pursued by those in power.
2. Film Screening: Drowned Land – Conference Space
6pm to 8pm
Directed by Choctaw filmmaker Colleen Thurston, Drowned Land is a powerful documentary following Indigenous and local water protectors fighting to preserve Oklahoma’s Kiamichi River from environmental exploitation and water diversion projects. Set within the Choctaw Nation, the film explores environmental justice, cultural heritage, displacement, and community resilience, highlighting the enduring connection between people and place.
3. New exhibition: 250 Years of the Presentation Sisters: Lighting the Way – Goldie Chapel
2pm to 9pm
A new exhibition celebrating 250 years of the Presentation Sisters. The exhibition explores how the vision and values that inspired Nano Nagle have travelled across generations and continents, taking root in diverse communities while continuing to place education, compassion, service and social justice at the heart of the Presentation mission.
4. Free entry to the Museum all day

description:
This Culture Night, experience an unforgettable evening of live orchestral music with the National Symphony Orchestra Ireland, conducted by Alexander Shelley and featuring acclaimed British saxophonist Jess Gillam MBE as guest soloist.

A highlight of Dublin’s annual cultural calendar, this special concert at the National Concert Hall offers an accessible and inspiring musical experience for first-time visitors and seasoned concertgoers alike. The programme spans orchestral favourites and contemporary works, including Bernstein’s Overture to Candide, Bartók’s Romanian Folk Dances, Augusta Holmès’ La nuit et l’amour, John Williams’ iconic Main Title from Star Wars, and Irish premieres of Anna Clyne’s Glasslands and Kati Agócs’ Shenanigan.

Join the National Symphony Orchestra Ireland for an evening celebrating the power, excitement, and diversity of live orchestral music as part of Culture Night.

This concert takes place at 18:30 and 20:30 on Culture Night.

title: New North: A Festival of New Writing for Culture Night Belfast 2026
description:
New North: A Festival of New Writing for Culture Night Belfast 2026
Produced by Prime Cut Productions at the Lyric Naughton Studio and McGrath Suite
Belfast audiences are invited to experience a bold showcase of new writing  from five female playwrights from across Ulster. Presented by Prime Cut Productions as part of Culture Night Belfast, the festival will present readings five new plays starting at 12 noon, throughout the Lyric Theatre on September 18th 2026.
The Programme
Audiences will enjoy rehearsed readings of five eclectic new works:
•     In “The Ache Of It” by Caitlin Magnall Kearns, Two fifty‑somethings find unexpected connection, humour and tenderness in a weekly seaside escape that gently explores desirability, disability and ageing..
•     ”The Girls of the Sacred Heart: by Sarah McKenna Dunne honours the thirty five children and one older woman lost in the 1943 Cavan fire, drawing us gently but powerfully toward the silenced truths, institutional shadows and enduring human dignity behind this overlooked chapter of Irish history
•     “The List” by Fionnuala Kennedy is a  stark, darkly funny and provocative new drama that thrusts us into a clandestine world that channels the power of a punk infused Greek chorus to illuminate the systemic failures facing women in Northern Ireland.
•     Alice Malseed’s “Sticky City” is a sharp, funny and fiercely feminist letter to Belfast, following a woman ready to torch every broken system that shaped her as she rewrites the city’s past, present and future with wit, fire and unapologetic hope.
•     ”The Three Green Fields (And the Fourth One at the Back Door)” by Katie Marie Moore is a sharp, contemporary drama in which a Halloween gathering in suburban Dublin unravels into a fierce, funny, and unsettling battle for Irish identity as four friends confront a mysterious intruder and the fault lines of who truly gets to call Ireland home
Each play will be brought to life by a dynamic ensemble of some of the island of Ireland’s finest actors, directed by critically acclaimed directors : Emma Jordan, Rhiann Jeffrey, Fionnuala Kennedy and Michael McEvoy.

title: Niall McCabe Live at St. Mary’s
description:
Niall McCabe will play at St. Mary’s Collegiate Church in Youghal with support from the YewTonics and Ruairi De Leaster.

Raised on Clare Island off Ireland’s Atlantic coast, Niall McCabe has built a reputation for songs of remarkable emotional depth and humanity. Drawing on the storytelling traditions of Irish folk while embracing the spacious textures of Americana and contemporary acoustic music, his work is carried by a voice that has become instantly recognisable to audiences on both sides of the Atlantic. Whether writing about fishermen, fathers and sons, strangers, or the idea of home itself, McCabe’s songs are marked by quiet observation, emotional honesty and an enduring sense of place.

Following the release of his acclaimed debut album, Rituals, in 2023, McCabe returned two years later with Stranger, a record that cemented his reputation for emotionally resonant songwriting while introducing a broader musical canvas. Traditional Irish instrumentation sits naturally alongside strings, pedal steel and understated band arrangements, creating a sound that feels equally at home in the west of Ireland and the American South. Throughout, however, the focus remains firmly on the songs.

Over the past two years, McCabe’s career has gathered remarkable momentum. In 2025 he made his debut at the Grand Ole Opry, toured throughout Britain with the celebrated Transatlantic Sessions and appeared as an official showcase artist at AmericanaFest in Nashville. As the songs travelled, so did the audience. His live performances have taken him from intimate listening rooms to stages including Cambridge Folk Festival, Celtic Connections, Galway Folk Festival and Doolin Folk Festival, while support appearances have included Chris Isaak, Mary Black and Sharon Shannon. Earlier international touring with Beoga also saw him perform alongside Ed Sheeran and Johnny Swim.

That momentum continued into 2026 with the release of The Heart Remembers. Written on Clare Island, the song reflects on home not simply as a place, but as something remembered, imagined and carried within us. The recording brought together a remarkable group of collaborators, featuring harmony vocals from Sting and Foy Vance, instrumental performances by Jerry Douglas, and arrangements and co-production by John McCusker. Despite the calibre of the musicians involved, the production remains deliberately understated, allowing the song’s emotional core to speak for itself.

Alongside his own headline touring, McCabe spends much of 2026 on the road with Foy Vance and Amble while work continues on his third studio album. Produced by Jerry Douglas and recorded between Ireland and Nashville, the project brings together the strongest creative partnerships of McCabe’s career to date while remaining rooted in the songs that first began life on a small island in the Atlantic.For over twenty years, Ruairí de Leastar has been writing songs and connecting with audiences through honest storytelling and a grounded, soulful sound. An accomplished songwriter from a young age, he has fronted a number of bands and duos, building a reputation for both his musicianship and his presence on stage.

He has toured across Ireland, the UK, Canada and the United States, and has shared the stage with artists including Duke Special, Lisa Hannigan, Jerry Fish, Jack L and Foy Vance.

Ruairí released his debut EP Making Shadows, and has since been steadily releasing singles while working towards his second record.

“Brimming with talent and showmanship, Ruairí de Leastar delivers his well-crafted songs with elan.” -David Teevan, Creative Producer and Arts Manager
(former Artistic Director of Clonmel Junction Festival)

 

The Yewtonics are a band from Youghal, Co. Cork, blending soul, groove, and a mix of other influences along the way.

Formed by long-time collaborators and friends, the band’s sound comes from a shared musical instinct and way of working. Their original songs lean into real-life themes; love, loss, and everything in between.

The Yewtonics showcase layered harmonies, tight musicianship, and a mix of intimate moments and bigger energy. Currently working on their debut EP, The Yewtonics continue to shape a sound that feels honest, expressive, and distinctly their own.

description:

In a time where housing is scarce and affordable community spaces are difficult to find, the ability to make our own commons becomes even more important.

For Culture Night 2026, Adroit Press in collaboration with Cailleach Books presents an evening of community gathering at Barlow House!

We will be hosting a participatory workshop that teaches you how to tie basic knots and lashings used in building shelter or setting up impromptu events. Following this, Cailleach Books will be open for local residents, activists and artists to drop-in, share discussions and browse a selection of DIY publishers in a self-assembled bookshop.

Join us for our workshop session or drop in at any time to explore Cailleach Books. Tea and snacks will be provided throughout the evening.

For more information visit cailleachbooks.ie

Cailleach Books is an experimental bookshop project concerned with the distribution of DIY publishing, zines, book objects and poetry pamphlets from Ireland. A cailleach is an Irish word for witch or crone, a multifaceted, liminal character, and an inspiration for this work. Cailleach Books appears in many forms and iterations, an ever evolving bookshop space and practice.

Adroit Press is a Cork-based, small DIY publisher of zines and other printed things made by Cass Loupe.

title: Night Moves | Culture Night Late | Mismantler
description:
A Film by Andrew Keogh & Steve Stapleton | Music by Nurse with Wound

A fascinating, unique experience, Mismantler is a dark, stream of consciousness fever dream that resembles nothing you’ve seen before.

A collaboration between Director Andrew Keogh, Steven Stapleton & Nurse With Wound, the film grew out of animated visuals for a live Nurse With Wound show. The main character ‘The Mismantler’ is taken from a collage by Stapleton. Post-apocalyptic landscapes are pictured in a number of major films that are now part of the collective unconscious. Terminator, The Road are clear influences for Andrew Keogh. His obstinate, close-up dive into the physicality of surviving, however…is its own thing. As if acknowledging that Eraserhead or The Texas Chain Saw Massacre have as much to tell us about it as Threads does.

“A fascinating and deeply unsettling experiment in audiovisual immersion” CINEUROPA

description:
Blas do Theanga presents a night of original music from three of Drogheda’s latest up and coming artists. Sophie Moon, KIDD and Téga, will take the Odd Mollies stage on the 18th September performing music from their respective projects that have been released this year. 

Sophie is a Drogheda based indie artist whose music drifts through static-filled soundscapes, finding beauty in glitches and ghosts of the digital age. Her songs hum with late-night introspection, soft guitars, flickering synths and layered vocals that feel like they’re playing from another room. Sophie will perform songs from her latest project ‘Stuck to the Screen’ as part of a two piece band.

KIDD is a Meath based rap artist with a sound heavily influenced by 90s hip-hop. KIDD’s music can be describe as high energy hip-hop that matches sharp lyricism and intricate wordplay with classic hip-hop foundations making him one of the most compelling artists on the scene today. He will be performing songs from his two releases ‘Kiddology’ & ‘College Heights’

Téga is a multi-genre producer, songwriter and musician from Drogheda known for unorthodox production and engaging performances. He effortlessly shifts between singing and rapping, often within the same track, never seating neatly within the one genre. He will be joined on stage by a four piece band to perform songs from his debut EP ‘REDEYE!’

title: Night Moves | Culture Night Late Cafe @ The Coffee Box
description:
Night Moves Café as part of Culture Night Late at The Coffee Box on George’s Street, curated by SJ McArdle, and produced by Droichead. Join us each month for an evening of intimate live music, song and conversation from 9pm till late. Drop in, grab a coffee and something sweet, and enjoy the atmosphere. Featuring Green and Shine, Julian Knows, Dagogo Harte & Peadar Connolly. 

GREENE AND SHINE, Mary Greene & Noel Shine have long been an important element of the national Folk and Americana scene. From Noel’s role as one of the founders of Cork Folk Festival, right through to the couple’s work alongside their daughter Ellie as RTE Folk Awards nominated band Greenshine, Noel and Mary have been a constant in the musical firmament. Greene and Shine’s music straddles the boundaries of Indie, Americana and Folk. They have lent their talents to the recordings of Republic of Loose, Christy Moore, Mick Hanly, Frances Black and John Spillane amongst many others, and performed with Mary Black on her farewell tour. 

Julian Knows is the brand-new era of Indie Rock music released under Irish artist David San Clair. 

Dagogo Hart with Peadar Connolly. A poet, playwright and performer, Dagogo Hart has rapidly risen to prominence, securing notable achievements such as performing on the prestigious Tommy Tiernan Show, Other Voices, writing and directing the critically acclaimed play “Mmanwu” at the Dublin Fringe Festival, and representing Ireland on a cultural tour in West Africa. His debut children’s book Lantern Smoke was released in 2025 to much acclaim. Peadar Connolly is a singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist performing on voice, autoharp, and global woodwinds. With a background in ethnomusicology, his work draws on folk and pop traditions from Ireland and beyond. Alongside his solo performances, Peadar has worked internationally as a musician and producer. Both Dagogo and Peadar are currently collaborating on a new theatre piece for Dublin Fringe Festival called Muster.

description:
Internationally acclaimed Congolese guitarist and singer Niwel Tsumbu joins forces with Donegal percussionist Eamonn Cagney for a vibrant celebration of rhythm, melody and musical connection.

Drawing on Rumba, jazz, classical, rock, folk and African traditions, Tsumbu has created a distinctive sound that has captivated audiences around the world. He has performed and collaborated with artists including Sinéad O’Connor, Dónal Lunny, Michael O’Suilleabháin and Taj Mahal, and is currently a member of Rhiannon Giddens’ band and the Silkroad Ensemble.

The Tsumbu and Cagney Duo brings together more than a decade of musical collaboration, combining Congolese guitar, jazz, West African rhythms and Irish traditional music in an electrifying live performance.

For this special concert, they will be joined by Macdara Ó Faoláin, the acclaimed bouzouki player, fiddle player and singer from An Rinn, Co. Waterford, known for his innovative approach to traditional Irish music.

title: No Woman is an Island
description:
A performance lecture about woman’s tireless pursuit of alone time, No Woman is an Island comes to Courthouse Gallery & Studios, Ennistymon, following a sell-out run at Dublin Theatre Festival 2023. Three years ago a theatremaker set out to investigate what it means to be alone. She presents her findings, veering between texts from great female thinkers, banal thoughts about crockery and intimate vignettes from a marriage. No Woman is an Island is a meditation on geographies of the Self. It maps the internal and external spaces in which we live our lives while walking a wonky line through cultural theories and histories of female solitude. With sharp humour and quiet ferocity, the piece creates an intimate and thoughtful space for audiences to consider the relationship between productivity and identity. This special Culture Night performance is part of an Irish tour supported by Arts Council Ireland and an Edinburgh run supported by Culture Ireland. ‘Not to be missed’ – Irish Times

Tar éis a bheith díolta amach ag Féile Amharclannaíochta Bhaile Átha Cliath in 2023, tá No Woman is an Island ag teacht chuig Courthouse Gallery & Studios, Inis Díomáin. Is léacht-léiriú é seo faoi shíor-thóraíocht na mban ar am a bheith acu dóibh féin. Trí bliana ó shin thug amharclannóir faoi iniúchadh a dhéanamh ar cad is brí le bheith i d’aonar. Sa léacht-léiriú seo, roinneann sí torthaí a cuid taighde, le sleachta ó mhórsmaointeoirí ban, fite fuaite le smaointí cistine agus blúiríní pearsanta ó shaol an phósta. Is machnamh é No Woman is an Island ar thírdhreach an duine. Leagann sé amach na spásanna inmheánacha agus seachtracha ina mairimid ár saol, ag tarraingt ar theoiricí cultúrtha agus ar stair aonarachais na mban. Le greann géar agus fíochmhaire chiúin, cruthaíonn an saothar seo spás don lucht féachana le machnamh a dhéanamh faoin gceangal idir táirgiúlacht agus féiniúlacht. Is léiriú speisialta é seo d’Oíche Chultúir atá mar chuid de chamchuairt náisiúnta le tacaíocht ón gComhairle Ealaíon, agus mar chuid de shraith léirithe i nDún Éideann le tacaíocht ó Chultúr Éireann. “Not to be missed” — The Irish Times

description:

title: North Earl Street: Mali Hâf
description:
Mali Hâf is a Welsh witch from Cardiff, bringing together the energy of the city with a deep philosophical connection to nature. Her music blends electronic and alternative beats with her folky Welsh roots and distinctive, gritty, sultry voice.

In 2025, Mali reached the Top 3 of the Glastonbury Emerging Talent Competition, performing on the BBC Introducing Stage in her mother tongue, Cymraeg.

More recently, she has been writing and performing with Irish-language artist James Shannon, creating a new Cymraeg and Gaeilge project that brings two Celtic languages together.

Menter Caerdydd and BÁC le Gaeilge have been working closely together over the past two years, sharing best practice and exploring new ways to strengthen the bonds between Irish and Welsh. At the heart of that collaboration is culture – and particularly music – as a powerful way of bringing our languages and communities together.

The inaugural project of Menter Caerdydd and BÁC le Gaeilge, featuring Mali Hâf and James Shannon, is the first step in what is hoped to become a growing programme of Irish-Welsh collaboration, showcased at festivals in both countries in the years ahead. This project came together thanks to funding from the Welsh Government Office in Dublin and the Consulate General of Ireland in Cardiff.

This event is part of a larger programme at North Earl Street for Culture Night Dublin. Filming and photography will be taking place at this location. By attending, visitors give permission to be photographed or filmed unless a member of the Culture Night team is explicitly notified otherwise.

title: North Earl Street: Zeztra
description:
Dublin-born sisters Avril and Lorna Meade, aka Zeztra, bring their captivating alt-pop sound to North Earl Street this Culture Night. The duo blend blood harmonies with influences spanning pop, alt-rock, R&B and Latin music. Described by Hot Press as having “a polished, alt-pop sound with an international outlook,” Zeztra have quickly established themselves as an exciting force in Irish music.

The duo have toured across Ireland, the UK and US, sharing stages with Maverick Sabre, Damien Dempsey and Pillow Queens, with performances at Brixton Academy, Brooklyn’s Rough Trade, Vicar Street and Dublin’s 3Olympia. They have also performed at the renowned Ruby Sessions, appeared live on BBC Radio London with Gaby Roslin, and played their first London headline show.

Working alongside acclaimed producer John Reynolds and David Prendergast, Zeztra released their debut EP in 2025, showcasing the distinctive harmonies, songwriting and energetic sound that have become central to the duo. Now entering an exciting new chapter, Zeztra are preparing for the release of their debut album in 2027.

Supported by Dublin City Council’s City Co-ordination Office

title: Nrityā Nazākhat
description:
nrityā nazākhat is an original Kathak production by rāas featuring four dancers and a live Hindustani classical musician (tabla). The performance explores nazākhat—subtlety, grace and emotional nuance—through intricate footwork, live music and dialogue between dancers and musicians. Structured across seven short acts, the work moves from expressive storytelling into increasingly virtuosic rhythmic exchanges, culminating in a high-energy finale. It has been conceived as a site-responsive performance, where the architecture of Castletown House becomes an active part of the experience, creating a dialogue between heritage, movement and music.

title: Ó Bhéal go Béal
description:
Ó Bhéal go Béal is a curated evening of sean-nós singing celebrating the songs, singers and recordings that have inspired a younger generation of local singers from the Connemara Gaeltacht. Presented by acclaimed sean-nós singer Síle Denvir, the event will feature invited young singers performing songs that hold a special personal connection for them, while sharing the stories of the singers and traditions that shaped their own musical journey.
Through music and conversation, audiences will experience the living tradition of sean-nós singing and discover how songs continue to be passed from generation to generation through listening, memory and oral tradition.
Taking place in the intimate surroundings of Amharclann Chois Fharraige (Seanscoil Sailearna), this free one-hour event offers a unique opportunity to experience the richness of the Irish-language singing tradition as part of Culture Night 2026.

Is oíche amhránaíochta ar an sean-nós í Ó Bhéal go Béal a dhéanfaidh ceiliúradh ar na hamhráin, na hamhránaithe agus na taifid a spreag glúin óg amhránaithe as Cois Fharraige. Faoi stiúir an amhránaí sean-nóis Síle Denvir, beidh amhránaithe óga áitiúla ag cur amhrán i láthair a bhfuil ceangal pearsanta acu leo, agus ag roinnt scéalta faoi na hamhránaithe agus na traidisiúin a mhúnlaigh a gcuid amhránaíochta féin. Trí amhránaíocht agus comhrá, tabharfar deis don lucht éisteachta blaiseadh a fháil den traidisiún beo sean-nóis agus den tslí a gcuirtear amhráin ó ghlúin go glúin trí éisteacht, cuimhne agus an traidisiún béil. Beidh an ócáid saor in aisce ar siúl in atmaisféar dlúth pearsanta Amharclann Chois Fharraige (Seanscoil Sailearna), agus tabharfaidh sí deis don phobal saibhreas an tsean-nóis agus an traidisiúin amhránaíochta Gaeilge a bhlaiseadh mar chuid d’Oíche Chultúir 2026.

title: O’Connell Street Bandstand: A Night of Rock ’n’ Roll with Thomas Spratt & The Showtime Collective
description:
Step back in time with a high-energy 1950s-inspired dance experience packed with music, movement, personality and plenty of audience interaction!

Led by professional performer, choreographer, presenter and dance teacher Thomas Spratt, the troupe brings the spirit, style and fun of the 1950s to life through exciting choreography, character and audience participation. Thomas is joined by three talented performers who have worked alongside him for many years across theatres, musicals, corporate events and live events throughout Ireland.

More than just a performing troupe, they are long-standing friends and professional collaborators who share a genuine passion for entertaining audiences. With over 20 years of professional experience in the performing arts, the group brings a wealth of experience, energy and personality to every performance.

Following a fantastic audience response to their Culture Night performance last year, they are thrilled to return for 2026 and get audiences dancing, clapping and joining in!

title: Oíche Cheoil le Méabh Ní Bheaglaoich & Cuas
description:
Forbairt na Dromoda presents a special Culture Night concert featuring Méabh Ní Bheaglaoich & Cuas. Rooted in the rich musical traditions of the Kerry Gaeltacht, the group brings together outstanding traditional musicians to perform a vibrant programme of Irish traditional music and song. This free community event celebrates the Irish language, local culture and the living musical heritage of Uíbh Ráthach, offering audiences an unforgettable evening of live performance in the heart of the Gaeltacht.

This event forms part of Cultúr 2026: Sharing Ireland’s Culture, the national cultural programme for Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union, and is supported by the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport through Culture Ireland.

Cuireann Forbairt na Dromoda ceolchoirm speisialta Oíche Chultúir i láthair ina mbeidh Méabh Ní Bheaglaoich & Cuas. Agus iad fréamhaithe i dtraidisiúin shaibhir cheoil Ghaeltacht Chiarraí, tugann an grúpa ceoltóirí traidisiúnta den scoth le chéile chun clár bríomhar de cheol agus d’amhránaíocht thraidisiúnta na hÉireann a léiriú. Déanann an t-imeacht pobail saor in aisce seo ceiliúradh ar an nGaeilge, cultúr na háite agus oidhreacht bheo cheoil Uíbh Ráthach, ag tairiscint oíche gan dearmad de thaibhiú beo i gcroílár na Gaeltachta don lucht féachana.

Tá an ócáid seo mar chuid de Chultúr 2026: Cultúr na hÉireann á Chomhroinnt, an clár cultúrtha náisiúnta do Uachtaránacht na hÉireann ar Chomhairle an Aontais Eorpaigh, agus tá sí á tacú ag an Roinn Cultúir, Cumarsáide agus Spóirt trí Chultúr Éireann.

title: Oíche Scoraíochta – Baile an Chinnéidigh
description:
Join us for an evening of music, song and more in both Irish and English in the beautiful setting of St. Matthew’s Church in Newtownmountkennedy. To kick off proceedings we have a few performers from our monthly Oíche Scoraíochta to play us a tune, sing us a song or perhaps even recite a poem or two. Our monthly Scoraíocht gives people from the local area a chance to show off their talents or perhaps to take their first steps into a world of creativity.

Culture Night presents our branch of Conradh na Gaeilge with a chance to show off two amazing local groups. The Hammonds, from up the road in Bray, will be playing some folk, trad and a bit of Leonard Cohen no doubt. They packed out the Mermaid Arts Centre in Bray, and their harmonies are a joy to behold. Here’s a wee snippet of the guys singing a traditional Wicklow song: https://www.instagram.com/p/DR9mBB1jUQP/

Also joining us on the night will be another fantastic Wicklow group, trad band Céilí Cottage who include a multi–All-Ireland Fleadh Cheoil winner in their midst. Armed with a fiddle, uileann pipes and guitar they’ll be sure to get toes tapping. Here’s a little clip of Céilí Cottage very much doing their thing: https://www.instagram.com/reels/DYNUadEAWYc/

This event is free and is a great opportunity to come out show your support for the arts in Newtownmountkennedy. We look forward to seeing you there. Ní neart go cur le chéile!

Bígí linn le haghaidh oíche ceoil, amhránaíocht agus tuilleadh i suíomh álainn Eaglais Naomh Maitiú i mBaile an Chinnéidigh. Chun tús a chur leis an ócáid, tá roinnt taibheoir againn ónár n-Oíche Scoraíochta míosúil chun fonn a sheinm, amhrán a chanadh nó b’fhéidir fiú dán nó dhó a aithris. Tugann ár Scoraíocht deis do dhaoine áitiúila a gcuid tallann a thaispeáint nó b’fhéidir a gcéad chéimeanna a thógáil i saol na cruthaitheachta.

Tugann Oíche Chultúir deis dár gcraobh de Chonradh na Gaeilge dhá ghrúpa iontacha a thaispeáint. Beidh na Hammonds, as Bré, ag seinm roinnt ceoil tíre, traidisiúnta agus beagán de Leonard Cohen gan amhras. Nuair a bhí siad ag seinm san Mermaid Arts Centre bhí sé plódaithe, agus ba mhór an pléisiúr é a bheith ag breathnú ar a gcuid comhcheol a cloisteáil. Seo píosa beag den grúpa ag canadh amhrán traidisiúnta ón Chill Mhantáin: https://www.instagram.com/p/DR9mBB1jUQP/

Beidh grúpa iontach eile ó Chill Mhantáin linn ar an oíche freisin, an banna traidisiúnta Céilí Cottage, a bhfuil buaiteoir ilchraolta Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann ina measc. Le fidil, píoba uilleann agus giotár, cinnteoidh siad go gcuirfidh siad a ladhracha ag tapáil. Seo gearrthóg bheag de Chéilí Cottage ag taispeáint a chuid scileanna: https://www.instagram.com/reels/DYNUadEAWYc/

Tá an ócáid seo saor in aisce agus is deis iontach í teacht amach chun do thacaíocht a léiriú do na healaíona i mBaile an Chinnéidigh. Táimid ag tnúth le thú a fheiceáil ann. Ní neart go cur le chéile!

title: Open Evening at St. Mary’s for All the Family
description:
Come visit St. Mary’s historic building on Culture Evening from 6pm until 9.30pm!
St. Mary’s Church dates back to 1248, when it formed part of the Maynooth Castle site. It wasn’t just a place of worship – it also played a defensive role, with a stone watchtower and battlements used to guard the surrounding lands. Today, St Mary’s remains at the heart of Maynooth – a place of history, welcome, worship, and community. title: Opening Doors: A Century of Medical Education
description:
What happens when a mental health hospital opens its doors?

In 1956, St John of God University Hospital became the first psychiatric hospital in Ireland to introduce an open-door system. At a time when most mental health hospitals remained locked environments, this represented a striking change in how care was understood. Patients were given greater freedom, while treatment placed new emphasis on activity, rehabilitation, participation and independence.

That moment is one chapter in a much bigger story. For 100 years, doctors have trained at our hospital while psychiatry has transformed around them. This Culture Night, explore that century through new archival research by historian Dr Rebecca Watterson. Discover the people, ideas and turning points that shaped medical education and psychiatric care, from the early training of doctors to the open-door movement and the development of today’s university hospital. This is a story of changing medicine, changing attitudes and a hospital learning alongside the discipline it helped to advance.

title: Paddy Hanna
description:
OYLEGATE, the fifth solo album from Paddy Hanna, was released in 2024 on Strange Brew (Roisin Dubh) and featured in many Irish end-of-year ‘Best of Lists’.

The album, marked by a graceful pop sensibility, is a journey through the euphoric highs and crushing lows of parenthood, delivered with his signature blend of melancholic wit and lush, off-kilter charm. Elation and exhaustion. Love and terror. The weight of responsibility and the strange, disorienting beauty of watching life unfold before your eyes.

Determined to sidestep the usual sentimental trappings of writing about having a child, Hanna found an unlikely creative companion in grim Soviet-era cinema. As he wrote, films like Solaris flickered in the background—bleak, meditative landscapes that mirrored the depths of sleep deprivation and the existential wonder of bringing a new life into the world.

This contrast of warmth and detachment, of intimate revelation and surreal detour, courses through OYLEGATE’s DNA.

Despite its moments of cold introspection, OYLEGATE is sonically rich and enveloping—an effect captured in a single request to producer Daniel Fox (Gilla Band): “sweet, sweet caramel.”

Hanna wanted the music to feel like satin lining the listener’s ears, wrapping them in warmth even when the themes tilt towards darkness.

2026 festival appearance inc. Beyond the Pale, Galway Arts Festival, All Together Now, Another Love Story, Electric Picnic

title: Paella: A Cultural History
description:
The Instituto Cervantes in Dublin, the Spanish cultural and language centre in Ireland, invites all food lovers to join this event that will explore the origins, mythology, and visual history of paella—a dish that has come to represent an entire nation while remaining fiercely regional.

This talk, presented by food writer Blanca Valencia, traces paella from the rice fields of Valencia to modern TV advertising campaigns and to viral comedian critiques. Blanca will examine how a peasant dish cooked over an open fire, and eaten communally, became Spain’s most photographed, most debated, and most misunderstood export.

One of the highlights of the event will be the exploration of paella in popular arts like ceramic tiles and tourism. The content of the talk will unravel the question of the original recipe, the war over chorizo, when to eat it, and why Valencians say that what most of the world eats is not the real dish at all. Blanca will also include information about the restaurants and chefs who shaped the dish’s image, and will examine what paella reveals about Spanish identity, regionalism, and pride.

The evening will culminate with a tasting of an authentic Valencian recipe, paella valenciana, with its rabbit, chicken, beans, and the all-important socarrat, the caramelised crust of rice at the bottom of the pan that separates the masters from the rest. Paella by DonCanizales.

The combination of painting and screen printing transforms each piece into a limited variable edition, with every work sharing a common printed element while remaining completely unique.
This immersive workshop offers a rare opportunity to explore the relationship between fine art and printmaking, learning how layers, texture, and colour interact to create dynamic contemporary artworks. No two pieces will be the same, making each participant’s final work a one-of-a-kind edition.
All materials are provided, and no previous experience is necessary. Enjoy great coffee, creative conversation, and leave with your own signed artwork created in collaboration with Alan Stafford.

description:
Architecture at the Edge creates a series of spaces of encounter for Culture Night, connecting an outdoor installation on Druid Lane, a happening at the Mick Lally Theatre, and a culinary exploration at the Festival Printworks Gallery through the shared theme of belonging. At its heart is an edible installation that takes the form of a Pálás an Phobail—a people’s palace—where the everyday rituals of gathering, eating, listening, and exchanging ideas unfold through food, sound, and conversation. Guests move through a sequence of spaces shaped by stories and sensory encounters, each revealing a different relationship between food, landscape and memory—inviting them to taste a sense of place. Between a canopy of flags stretching across the street and a performative public interior, between solitary moments and shared tables, the evening explores how places—and people—come to belong through the encounters they foster, the stories they carry, and the memories they create.

 

Festival Printworks Gallery, Market St. 

– Start/End Time – Hours: arrive 7:00 PM to 11:00 PM.

Mick Lally Theatre, and on Druid lane. 

– Start/End Time – Hours: 8:00 PM to 1:30 AM.

 

– Key artists names:

 

Blanka Major is a Zurich-based architect with Hungarian roots whose work spans architecture, food, research, teaching, writing, and curation. She explores how everyday infrastructures shape collective life, using cooking as a spatial and social practice. She is part of ZAS*, a LINA Spotlight Fellow 2025, and was nominated for the Swiss Art Award in Architecture (2026).
Hinterland aims to connect food, people and place. The team of Claire Davey, Enda McEvoy & Fergal Anderson are dedicated to community-rooted research, creativity, and action that nourishes just, inclusive and resilient food futures.
Cóilí Collins aka Shampain is a Galway-born DJ and Producer known for his eclectic mix of ambient, bass-driven, club and cinematic electronic sounds. With a decade of experience curating deep, atmospheric sets he blends experimental textures with dancefloor energy. Now a key figure in Ireland’s underground scene, Shampain continues to push boundaries with his unique sonic style.

This event is supported by the Arts Council in partnership with Department of Culture, Communications and Sport under the Night-Time Economy Taskforce

title: Parliamentary Tour of the National Parliament, Dáil and Seanad Éireann
description:
On Culture Night, visitors will have the opportunity to join Parliamentary Ushers in a guided tour of the historic National Parliament building, where they will see both the Dáil and Seanad Chambers and learn about the history of this unique building.

Located in Dublin, in the heart of the South Georgian Quarter, Leinster House was designed and built in the mid-18th century by Richard Castle, the leading architect in Ireland for the Earl of Kildare, James Fitzgerald, the first Duke of Leinster. Later, it became the headquarters of the Royal Dublin Society before taking up its current position as the home of our National Parliament, comprising the two Houses of the Oireachtas, Dáil Éireann (the House of Representatives) and Seanad Éireann (the Senate).

Having recently undergone a major conservation and restoration project, Leinster House will have something for everyone, welcoming families and visitors young and old to enjoy a special evening of entertainment for Culture Night.

General Admission tickets – from 17:00

Irish Language Tour tickets – from 20:00

Ba é Richard Castle, an t-ailtire ba mhó le rá in Éirinn ag an am, a dhear agus a thóg Teach Laighean, atá suite i mBaile Átha Cliath, i gcroílár Cheathrú Sheoirseach Dheisceart na Cathrach, i lár an 18ú haois d’Iarla Chill Dara, James Fitzgerald, an chéad Diúc Laighean. Ina dhiaidh sin, ba é ceanncheathrú Chumann Ríoga Bhaile Átha Cliath é sular tháinig sé chun bheith ina ionad dár bParlaimint Náisiúnta, ina bhfuil dhá Theach an Oireachtais, Dáil Éireann (Teach na nIonadaithe) agus Seanad Éireann (an Seanad).

description: On the 40th anniversary of this iconic masterpiece, Phantom & The Voice – the music of Andrew Lloyd Webber and Sarah Brightman brings to life the love story behind the mask – and the music that followed. title: Phibsborough 1926: A Suburb in Full Swing – Mater Misericordiae University Hospital & Phizzfest
description:

Guest Speaker Grainne MacLochlainn, National Library of Ireland, will present a fascinating talk on the local area of Phibsborough, including the Mater Hospital, one hundred years ago. Step back a century and discover Phibsborough as it was in 1926, a lively sophisticated neighbourhood buzzing with trams, cinemas, churches, wine merchants and bustling public houses while at the same time housing big institutions such as the Mater Hospital and Mountjoy Prison. This richly illustrated talk brings the area’s past to life through remarkable National Library photographs, headline grabbing stories of the day and insights drawn from the recently released 1926 Census.

 

Entry is via the original hospital entrance on Eccles Street (stone steps). Wheelchair and buggy access to this drop-in event is available via the Eccles Street hospital entrance beside the original building.

title: PIPE ORGAN RECITAL
description:
Organist Anne Cullen will give a 30 minutes recital on the 1864 pipe organ in St John’s Cathedral. The programme will span the centuries, featuring music from 17th, 18th, 19th and 20th centuries by Buxtehude, Bach, Franck and Langlais. The breadth of this repertoire will demonstrate the wonderful variety of sounds available on this 46 stop instrument, which has in excess of 2,500 pipes. The pipe organ is truly the King of Instruments, as described by Mozart, and it is said that Franck likened playing the organ to playing an orchestra. Anne will take us on a journey, not just through the centuries, but through the very broad range of styles and sounds at her fingertips.
This organ was built by the renowned firm of Wm. Hill and Son and was a gift to the cathedral from the 3rd Earl of Dunraven, Edward Wyndham Quinn of Adare. It cost £1,000 at the time but is worth in excess of €1,000.000 today. A recital such as this allows us to appreciate the extent of this gift, while also reminding us of the need to preserve this wonderful highly regarded legacy into the future.

Explore Trinity Botany’s unique and historic teaching and research botanic garden, where botanists will share stories of the fascinating lives of plants from around the world, how they have evolved and adapted to sometimes extreme environments, and what they can teach us about our planet and how to help protect it.

The tour will include:

Meet the ‘Witness Trees’ and learn how they absorb information about our changing climate through their leaves.
Discover how some plants can have their pollinators and eat them too!
Hear about amazing plants that have outlived the dinosaurs.
Learn about important plant-animal-environment research taking place at Trinity.

A collaboration between The Glens Arts Centre and Rabbit’s Riot Theatre Company, this is a celebration of creativity, imagination and the thrill of brand-new theatre.

Guided by acclaimed Leitrim playwright Treasa Nealon, participants begin with a scriptwriting workshop before completing their plays overnight.

The following day, professional actors will rehearse each script before presenting them to a live audience in a series of rehearsed readings.

Treasa Nealon’s work has been recognised nationally and internationally. Her short play The Back of the Bus was selected for Fishamble’s The Navigator Project and will be published by Bloomsbury.

Her full-length Boom Boom Bang was selected for Druid Debuts, with recent productions including The World is Falling in Around Us (London’s Union Theatre) and Homesick (Dublin Fringe Festival). Whether you’re a theatre lover, aspiring writer or simply curious, come experience six brand-new stories created in just one day.

title: Portrait Exhibition: Portraits of Heritage in Modern Lines
description:
This Culture Night at the Embassy of the Republic of Moldova, visitors are invited to view Portraits of Heritage in Modern Lines, a contemporary art exhibition presenting a series of portraits created by artist Svetlana Marineac. 

The portraits explore themes of memory, tradition, and belonging, translating ancestral symbols and cultural narratives into a contemporary artistic language. Through expressive colour, light, and composition, each artwork becomes a dialogue between past and present, reflecting the evolving nature of identity in a modern world. Executed in a modern visual style, they remain deeply rooted in cultural identity and heritage. 

This exhibition invites Culture Night visitors to reflect on how heritage continues to shape personal and collective identity, even as styles, environments, and generations change.

 

This event is part of the European Culture Trail – a EUNIC Ireland (European Union National Institutes for Culture) in cooperation with the European Commission Representation in Ireland.

title: Ports of Call
description:
Ports of Call is a solo live performance by Luigi Cirillo, Belfast-based composer and multi-instrumentalist behind the Fusionarium project.
The set takes the form of a musical journey through the cities and cultures that have shaped Cirillo’s work: Naples, Belfast, and beyond. Each song is introduced through the story of a physical object: an instrument found, borrowed or gifted along the way. A Neapolitan mandolin passed on by a Belfast folk musician. A guitar that crossed the Mediterranean. A clarinet that found its way into music it was never meant for.
Using voice, guitars, clarinet, looper and live electronics, Cirillo layers acoustic folk traditions with contemporary sound in real time; building each piece from silence, live on stage, with no backing track and no band. The result is intimate, unhurried, and unlike a standard concert set.
Ports of Call is created specifically for Culture Night Belfast 2026 and reflects the spirit of a city that has always been a place of arrival, departure and exchange.

title: Prayer Flag Making Workshop
description:
Celebrate 35 years of the Dublin Buddhist Centre by contributing to a collaborative prayer flag inspired by a long-standing Himalayan tradition.

Prayer flags are colourful cloth rectangles traditionally strung along mountain ridges, peaks, and temples in the Himalayas. Inscribed with sacred mantras and symbols, they are used by Buddhists to promote peace, compassion, strength, and wisdom. As the wind blows, it is believed to spread goodwill and positive energy into the surrounding space.

Visitors are invited to create a panel for a prayer flag to mark this special anniversary of the Dublin Buddhist Centre. A brief introduction to the tradition will be shared before participants are invited to contribute their own design, reflection, or aspiration.

Materials will be provided and no artistic experience is needed—just curiosity and a willingness to take part. Spaces are limited and offered on a first come first served basis.

title: Pretty Vacant
description:
Carmilla is a former Eurovision sensation turned property mogul who’s here to “Set the Liberties Free”. Leading a community consultation for award-winning property developers U-Lynch, her “visionary” pitch to rebrand the neighbourhood descends into chaos when, to her surprise, the community “simply won’t lie down”. As the session unfolds, polite small talk dissolves into a surreal landscape where raw greed takes control and “community engagement” is the ultimate box-ticking exercise.

This high-octane musical satire skewers the forces behind gentrification and the willingness of the people in power to play along. Set to a jukebox of Euro-pop bangers, Pretty Vacant explores the struggle of an area fighting for its soul and asks how wide the gap between satire and reality actually is.

Pretty Vacant is a scathing, surreal, and deeply funny look at who holds the keys to the city and who is being locked out. Join U-Lynch for a “highly profit-effective” evening – just don’t expect to keep your home.

title: Propagating Otherwise
description:

awareness and collective participation. For Culture Night 2026, Furze Arts will host a two-day cultural
event Propagating Otherwise in collaboration with Soearth Projects. For this year’s theme, we asked
artists to get their hands dirty with gardens (both real and speculative) and their propagations, dealing in
life, death and decay. With a focus on artistic works and practices which take the garden – in all its
possible arrangements – as an entry point for the stories they want to tell. Think of orchards, farms,
kitchen gardens, botanical gardens, secret gardens, forgotten fields, archival arcadia, and digital edens;
overall, the garden as a lens through which to observe a process, investigate a systemic infrastructure, or

title: Race and Place in the City – Culture Night Special
description:
This Culture Night, join historian Richard Carson for Race and Place in the City, a 90-minute walking tour of Lower Gardiner Street and its laneways. Featured on RTÉ Lyric FM and presented as part of Culture Night from 2023–2025, the tour uses the stories of local buildings and places to invite participants to reimagine their relationship with the city and with one another.

Drawing on history, theology, and social commentary, the tour explores how colonial ideas became embedded in Dublin’s north-east inner city and how their legacy continues to shape the area today. Along the way, participants will discover unexpected stories, from a local wedding that united two nineteenth-century colonial worlds on opposite sides of the globe to the surprising history of the site now occupied by Store Street Garda Station, revealing that Dublin’s so-called “new communities” are far from new.

Previous guests have described the tour as “mind-blowing” and “brilliant”, with one participant remarking, “I will never look at these streets the same again.”

This Culture Night, September 18, we will bring music and life back to that room as in the time of the great O’Donoghue Ross Chieftains. For one night only, join us to raise the oak rafters in the company of local traditional musicians Dean and Brandon Griffin. From 7:00pm to 8:00pm they will play a selection of traditional Irish music in the Great Hall, opening a window into bygone times. The Great Hall is located at the top of the tower house and access involves climbing an uneven, medieval staircase of 64 steps. Visitors should also be very vigilant about making their way from the carpark to Ross Castle as there is no lighting.

title: Róisín Harbison (How I Became A Wave Support)
description:
Join us in Kinsale for an evening of music with How I Became A Wave, supported by Róisín Harbison. Set against the beautiful surroundings of St.Catherine’s Cultural Centre, this is sure to be a memorable and magical evening of live music!

Róisín Harbison hails from Limerick and has been playing music for over 20 years.

She began with classical violin at the Limerick School of Music and subsequently studied at the Dublin Conservatory of Music, performing with several orchestras including the University of Limerick Orchestra and Hibernian Symphony Orchestra. More recently, she has taken to the stage with Limerick-based rock band Raging Sons, having recorded on their album, 20:20.

Róisín began playing the harp at the age of nine, learning at the Irish Harp Centre in Limerick. As a member of the Irish Harp Orchestra, she has performed throughout Ireland and toured internationally in Germany, Austria, and the UK. She is also a regular contributor to the Irish traditional session scene. Her musical interests span classical, Irish traditional and contemporary music, bringing together the different influences that have shaped her playing throughout her life.

In support of How I Became a Wave, Róisín will perform a range of pieces showcasing the depth, character, and versatility of the Irish harp.

 

How I Became A Wave arrives quietly. The shapeshifting orchestral folk project fronted by Pat Carey brings together some of Ireland’s most respected musicians, who take their places on stage around a small orchestra of guitar, cello, violin, pedal steel, keyboard, saxophone and percussion. For anyone seeing them for the first time, it’s hard to guess what’s coming.

In Ireland, How I Became A Wave shows have become known as places where something happens that can’t quite be repeated. Songs metamorphose mid-performance; a quiet lullaby ripples outward and swells into soaring orchestral harmony – and no two nights sound the same. Carey’s voice anchors it all, vulnerable and powerful in the same breath. Audiences at their sold-out shows describe the songs taking on a life of their own, enveloping the room in an incorporeal beauty that is felt long after the last note has been played.

How I Became A Wave’s self-titled debut album, released in March 2026, was met with instant critical acclaim — praised as “flawless” by The Irish Times, “deeply compelling” by Hot Press, and an album that “begs to be listened to” by RTÉ, among many others.

Though still a young project, How I Became A Wave is Carey’s most ambitious undertaking to date, and one that extends well beyond music. At its core is a deep, multidisciplinary collaborative approach: Carey has drawn a wide circle of respected artists into the HIBAW world, spanning visual art, film, poetry and literature, alongside music.

That circle includes Cormac McCarthy (RTÉ Concert Orchestra, Iarla Ó Lionáird), who arranged strings and keys for the album; David Murphy, whose latest record has drawn praise from Uncut to The Guardian; Carey’s former Hard Ground bandmates Davie Ryan and Hugh Dillon; and his regular touring band — Kealan Kenny, Dylan Howe, Julieanne Quirke, Maria Ryan, Kaitlin Cullen-Verhauz and more.

Over the past 18 months, How I Became A Wave has opened for Lisa O’Neill, Villagers, Gemma Hayes, Lisa Hannigan, Joan Shelley, Ailbhe Reddy, Niamh Regan and John Spillane, and played festivals including Sounds From A Safe Harbour, Quiet Lights, Beyond The Pale, Galway Folk Festival, Forest Fest and Your Roots Are Showing. Their album launch shows at Dublin’s Unitarian Church and Cork’s Coughlan’s both sold out to rave reviews.

The album draws as much from poetry, literature and landscape as it does from music. Echoes of Max Porter, Eavan Boland, Sylvia Plath, Sara Baume and Claire Keegan run through it alongside the influence of Paul Buchanan, Big Thief, Anaïs Mitchell, Bon Iver and Nils Frahm, resulting in music that carries incredible strength in its vulnerability.

How I Became A Wave are currently in the studio working on new material.

title: Rowe St Church Bellringing Demonstration
description:
The beautiful historic bells of Rowe St church have rung out over the town marking significant life events; births, weddings, funerals and other events both religious and secular since the 1800’s. Although located in a public building, the bell tower is hidden away at the top of a spiral staircase and most people walking past look up when they hear the bells but have no idea that there are people in the tower actually pulling the ropes. Rowe St church is one of only thirty seven towers in Ireland with a set of bells suitable for change – ringing, as the skill is called. The people of Wexford are very proud of the tradition.

On Culture night visitors will be welcomed at the entrance and guided up the narrow spiral staircase to the tower here they will be invited to sit and listen while the ringers demonstrate how it all happens. The bells themselves are further up the tower, separate from the ringing chamber. Expect to spend 20 minutes in the tower. Due to the fact that space in the tower is quite limited with the added danger of moving ropes, this event will not be suitable for children under 12.

Please arrive at 5pm , 5.30pm, 6pm and 6.30pm to join the group and places will be allocated on a first come basis.

Prospective bell ringers are particularly welcomed and should make themselves known to the tower leader. The last group will be admitted at 6.30pm.

title: Running Through Blue
description:
Running Through Blue is an interactive urban art trail and family creative event taking place in Market Square, Castlebar, during Culture Night.

Participants will begin their journey at Market Square, where they will receive a specially designed map guiding them through the town. Following the trail, they will discover selected elements of Fabric of Hydrosphere: Heaviness of Blue, a textile artwork exploring the relationship between denim, water and textile water, alongside pieces created through the MANA Creative Circle clothing upcycling project.

The trail invites participants to explore the town through art, observation and discovery, while reflecting on the journey of clothing and materials from everyday use to potential waste.

After completing the trail participants will return to Market Square for a collaborative textile workshop inspired by sashiko, the Japanese tradition of decorative repair. Using simple running stitches and reclaimed fabric pieces, participants will contribute to a collective textile wave representing water, movement and positive change.

The event aims to encourage families to think differently about unwanted clothing and textiles: rather than seeing them as waste, we can repair, reuse, transform and reimagine them. Through hands-on making, participants will explore how small creative actions can contribute to more sustainable habits and greater care for our waterways and natural environment.

This event is designed for families and welcomes both children and adults. Children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult.

title: Self-Guided Tour of Christ Church Cathedral – 16:00
description:
This Culture Night, visitors can explore the rich history of Christ Church Cathedral with its immersive audio guide, which brings nearly 1,000 years of history to life in a new and exciting way.

The audio guide is available in English, French, German, Spanish, Polish, Portuguese, and Italian. Irish Sign Language and audio-described tours are also available, with English transcriptions provided.

Please download the audio guide onto your own device and bring your earphones/headphones. Visitors are able to choose from three different themes as they explore: ‘Power and Politics’, ‘Christ Church & the City’ and ‘Music & Spirituality’.

There is a limit of 200 spaces available for each self-guided tour and they must be pre-booked in advance. The audio guide must be downloaded onto your own device as physical devices will not be available on the night. The tour lasts around 45 minutes. Latecomers will not be admitted. Please note there are no bathroom facilities on site.

title: Shackleton Experience – A brief introduction to the life and legacy of Kildare born Ernest Shackleton
description:
Step into the World’s greatest Survival Story at The Shackleton Experience in Athy!
Join us for a 30 minute highlights tour – a brief journey through the extraordinary life and adventures of Ernest Shackleton, the legendary polar explorer. The Shackleton Experience in Athy, Co. Kildare, is the only institution in the world dedicated to the extraordinary life and achievements of Ernest Shackleton, the legendary polar explorer who was born just outside Athy in Kilkea.
The Shackleton Experience is a world-class visitor attraction that combines the largest collection of Shackleton artefacts in the world with cutting-edge technology and immersive, interactive exhibits.
Ernest Shackleton’s extraordinary story is brought to life at the Shackleton Experience through dramatic digital storytelling, sensory effects and recreated environments that offer visitors the chance to step into his world. Trace Shackleton’s inspiring journey from his Kildare roots to the vast Polar ice caps, capturing the determination and leadership that defined his legacy. They can also explore in detail the three expeditions he led to the Antarctic, including the legendary Endurance expedition (1914–1917) where Shackleton managed to bring the entire crew home safely without the loss of a single life after their ship sank in a frozen sea hundreds of miles from civilisation.
On Culture Night this highlights tour brings you to the heart of the story, giving you a sense of what there is to explore at The Shackleton Experience.

As Ireland’s principal advocacy organisation for writers, the Irish Writers’ Union represents and supports Irish writers writers of Irish interest publications, wherever they are based, championing their rights through initiatives including the Grand Theft Author campaign, which calls for greater protection of authors’ work from unauthorised use in training large language models.

title: Shouk Party
description:
Based in the heart of Drumcondra, Shouk celebrates life over good food, great music and wonderful people throughout autumn, winter, spring and summer.

For Ireland’s Culture Night 2026, Shouk is delighted to present an evening of fun, dancing and connection, bringing the Shouk Party to the neighbourhood and the vibrant Drumcondra community.

Guests are invited to enjoy the evening in the beautifully renovated garden, featuring a fully covered and heated space with a retractable roof, offering a unique setting for dancing beneath the open sky.

Curating the soundtrack for the evening are long-standing Dublin DJs Declan Comiskey and Matty Faherty. Having spent more than 25 years playing dance floors and vinyl bars across Dublin and beyond, Declan and Matty will keep the beats flowing from sunset to midnight with an eclectic blend of soul, funk, Latin, boogie and house, taking guests on an uplifting musical journey from timeless classics to irresistible grooves as the night unfolds.

Shouk is a family-friendly restaurant, welcoming guests of all ages to celebrate Ireland’s special Culture Night through food, music and community.

title: Sing for Life Choir Performance
description:
The Sing for Life Choir was established over 10 years ago by Cancer Focus NI. It is a non-audition choir that is open to anyone affected by a cancer diagnosis, may that be a patient, carer or family member. The choir is now over 80 members strong and rehearse once a week in Belfast. The fun, friendly and supportive environment provides a therapeutic experience in which individuals can meet others affected by cancer, whilst learning new choral skills along the way. The choir’s repertoire ranges from upbeat & popular music to traditional sacred songs, meaning there is something for everyone. It truly is a remarkable community of people and as our strap line says – ‘it’s no ordinary choir’.
We would provide a single performance of a variety of contemporary and classical songs arranged and conducted by Keith Acheson and performed by approximately 30-50 members of the Cancer Focus Sing for Life Community Choir. We would request that we have collection buckets at the event for fundraising purposes.

 

This is an AccessAble venue: https://www.accessable.co.uk/belfast-city-council/access-guides/victoria-square
host: Cancer Focus NI’s Sing for Life Choir

title: Singer / Songwriter Deirdre Cunningham and Band
description:
Booking requested but not essential  

Deirdre Cunningham is an Irish singer songwriter and guitarist. Deirdre’s writing styles encompass Folk, Rock, Country and Contemporary.  Performing with her Band, a collection of original material from her recorded albums.   Deirdre and her Band will lead you on a magical musical journey to the wilds, open roads, mountain peaks and beyond. Deirdre commands attention and respect like nobody can. A leading light in local  music circles and an accomplished touring and recording artist. Originally from Dundalk, County Louth, Deirdre is now based in Cootehall, Co. Roscommon.

Deirdre  has performed in Ireland, the UK, Europe and Asia. Deirdre will be performing a collection of original material from her recorded albums inspired by nature, ecology, relationships, conservation and everyday happenings. Songs written on the winds of time, life and generations rendered in Deirdre Cunningham’s individual vocal and writing style. Influenced by many but dominated by her own personalized world view –these are songs for the seasons of the mind and heart.

Deirdre has released four albums to date, Sunny Days. City of Tribes, and Cry from the Heart. Her fourth album Good Karma was released in May 2026 on Lake Records and is available now on Digital Streaming Platforms including Spotify, Band Camp and Apple. She has also released the single “Take me for a Fool” produced by Philip Donnelly and EP “Solo” produced by Nicky Ryan.

Deirdre will perform material from her album collection including songs from her latest Album ‘Good Karma’ in this performance. ‘Good Karma’ is an upbeat collection rooted in Folk, Rock, Country and Celtic idioms. Original songs freshly inspired by nature, ecology, relationships, conservation and everyday happenings. Songs written on the winds of time, life and generations rendered in listening ears – Deirdre Cunningham’s voice and songs weave a tapestry of events and happenings, musings and thoughts that bless the ear and tantalize the mind.
fullAddress: King House, Military Road, Boyle, County Roscommon, F52 WR26

title: Singing for the Soul with Róisín Mulliez
description:
Galway County Integration Team are delighted to bring prominent Community Choir Director, Róisín Mulliez to Culture Night 2026.

As an established jazz vocalist, choir director and music educator operating out of Galway City, Róisín brings a rich mix of passion, experience and accessibility to her work.

Helping participants to find their voice in a communal group setting, this workshop will allow attendees to embrace the joy of singing in an open and organic setting. The Singing for the Soul project is a workshop where Róisín will guide participants through a welcoming and nourishing evening of singing.

The session begins with a grounding exercise to calm the mind and bring everyone’s attention into their breath and body. From there, Róisín leads playful vocal warm-ups and group activities that help participants let go of tension.

The main part of the workshop focuses on learning a handful of songs drawn from folk, bluegrass, and gospel traditions. These songs are carefully chosen to be easy to learn, with simple harmonies that allow everyone – regardless of experience – to join in.

By the end of the session, participants will have learned three to five new, uplifting songs. No previous singing experience is needed – just a willingness to join in and share the simple pleasure of raising our voices together!

title: Singing Letts… In a Wexford Village
description:
“Singing Letts… In a Wexford Village” is a unique Culture Night presentation by singer/composer Aileen Lambert with bouzouki player Niall Lacey and flute/whistle player Noreen Kehoe, bringing the poetry of the much-overlooked Winifred M. Letts to life through newly composed airs and traditional-style singing.

Focusing on poems from the chapter In A Wexford Village in Letts’ first collection of poetry, the performance explores the themes, stories, places and distinctive language that shaped Letts’ writing. Through music, storytelling and accompaniment, these evocative poems are revitalised for contemporary audiences, offering a fresh and engaging perspective on Wexford’s literary and cultural heritage.

title: Singing Session with Terence O’Flaherty
description: Terence O’Flaherty is a singer/songwriter from Ennistymon, Co. Clare. He is from a family of singers and learned his earliest songs from local singers and musicians and travelling storytellers and singers. In the early 1970s, he emigrated to London and joined the thriving Irish music scene in the capital. He has performed with musicians from many different backgrounds, including, The Chieftains, Planxty, The Furys and De Danann. He has performed across genres with classical, jazz and funk artists and has performed widely in the UK, Europe and the USA. This is being delivered as part of Drimoleague Singing Festival.

title: Sister Weather Exhibition Opening and DJ Set
description:
This Culture Night, Goethe-Institut Irland, in collaboration with the Crespo Foundation, is delighted to unveil Sister Weather — an exhibition by Mimicri, a collaborative project of German artists Susanne Bürner, Annette Kelm, Alexandra Leykauf, and Ines Kaag. During their three‑month residency at Glenkeen Garden in West Cork, the artists immersed themselves in the spirit of ArtNature / NatureArt, creating works that respond to the landscape, the weather, and the quiet magic of the place. The results are imaginative and deeply atmospheric.

The exhibition opens at 18:00, and the evening continues from 20:00 as the Goethe-Institut Irland transforms into a club with a special DJ set. Stay on to dance the night away and celebrate Culture Night in style.

title: Slovak Folk Instruments, Music and Dances Workshop Performed by Slovak Folk Ensemble FS Ostroha
description:
Experience the rich traditions of Slovakia with the Slovak folk ensemble FS Ostroha, which has been proudly sharing the beauty and authenticity of Slovak folklore in Ireland for many years.

The programme for Culture Night opens with a vibrant singing performance, followed by an introduction to Slovak folk traditions through authentic music, dance, and colourful regional costumes. Audiences will discover the unique sounds of traditional Slovak folk instruments and experience the richness of Slovakia’s musical heritage. This performance also features lively folk dances showcasing the elegance, energy, and traditions of Slovak couple dancing, including the dynamic ‘Hat Dance’, one of the highlights of the programme.

The evening concludes with an interactive dance workshop, giving participants the chance to learn some traditional Slovak folk dance steps and enjoy the joy of dancing themselves.Culture Night at the Embassy of the Slovak Republic is a unique opportunity to experience Slovakia’s living cultural heritage in an engaging and memorable way.

title: Sol Art: Artist Talk & Live Painting Demonstration with Kevin McNamara
description:
This Culture Night, Sol Art Gallery invites visitors to meet artist Kevin McNamara for a talk and live painting demonstration exploring the art of self-portraiture. 

Kevin will discuss his approach to painting and demonstrate how he begins a portrait, sharing the key influences, techniques, and ideas that inform his work. Kevin reflects, “These paintings are essential and useful to me as an artist as well as an opportunity for me to examine and scrutinise my ongoing pursuit of colour.”

This exciting Culture Night event offers a unique opportunity to gain insight into the artist’s creative process, revealing a preview of Kevin McNamara’s forthcoming solo exhibition, which opens at the gallery on 1 October. 

Places are limited and advance booking is recommended. To learn more, contact Sol Art Gallery at info@solart.ie or call 01 675 0972.

title: Something to Say – Summer Exhibition Closing Ceremony
description:
Something To Say looks at the personal and professional friendship between Seamus Heaney and musician, film maker and broadcaster David Hammond, and features screenings with accompanying correspondence and production notes of some of the work they made together.

This exhibition celebrates friendship and collaboration, charting the evolution of ideas through correspondence, in both meanings of the word: letters, faxes, and scribbled notes; but also, the shared understanding that grows between artists as they learn the language of each other’s artforms. Featuring never-before-seen photographs, rarely spotted written materials, and many of the treasures of the SHC Broadcast Archive, the exhibition shows the deep mutual understanding of these co-conspirators and reveals some of the unseen labour behind their work.

In this same spirit of collaboration, this year we made a vinyl record, inspired by Hammond’s Flying Fox broadcast collection, which forms the basis of our archive. ‘

This is it, Yeah’ is an album of poetry and music from writers associated with the Seamus Heaney Centre, with fragments of interviews with Seamus Heaney.

Join us for Culture Night at the Seamus Heaney Centre for hourly tours of the Something To Say exhibition and programme of material from our broadcast archive and poetry album throughout the evening as part of the closing ceremony of our summer exhibition.
fullAddress: The Seamus Heaney Centre, English and Languages Queen's University, University Road, Belfast, UK

title: Songbook Presents: The Carlow Songbook
description:

Built around a shared love of local songwriting and community, the project brings together a group of local musicians to explore familiar songs in a different setting and style using acoustic and traditional instrumentation. The performance is intended to feel informal and collaborative, while also paying tribute to the depth of original music that has emerged from Carlow over the years.

The idea for the project grew organically from chats at local gigs and open mics. Through a shared passion for the local music scene, the group began reworking songs by friends and fellow artists from across Carlow.
