title: Soul Juice Jam at Bewleys Grafton Street
description:
Soul Juice is Dublin’s live improvised music community, bringing together musicians, vocalists, rappers, poets, and music lovers for an evening of spontaneous creation. Inspired by London’s thriving jam scene, Soul Juice creates a space where collaboration comes before perfection and every performance is unique.

On Culture Night at Bewleys, the evening opens with a performance from Q and the Soul Juice house band before evolving through a series of 15-minute musician rotations. One by one, members of the house band step off, and new artists step in, creating entirely new combinations of musicians and fresh sounds throughout the evening. There are no set lists, no rehearsed arrangements, and no expectations, just creativity in the moment.

With a full backline provided, performers simply bring their instrument and join the rotation. Whether you’re taking part or watching from the audience, Soul Juice offers a one-of-a-kind experience celebrating improvisation, community, and the incredible talent across Dublin’s R&B, hip hop, jazz, soul, funk, Afro, Latin, trad, rap, and spoken word scenes.

title: St. Conal’s: Walking tour of Letterkenny’s Largest Building
description:
Hovering at the edge of our image of Letterkenny is ‘The Mental’, the former St. Conal’s Psychiatric Hospital, a massive institution built to deal with the incomprehensible problem of the apparent growth in people classed as insane in nineteenth-century Ireland.

A place people feared to be sent, and also an asylum from the world, where a crude form of what could be called ‘welfare’ was available. Were such enormous buildings needed, and what can we make of them now?

In a brief dusk walking tour, Barry Ramsay, a former resident and latterly a senior staff member, with happy memories of growing up within its walls, and Colm Murray, an architectural historian researching how these buildings were brought into existence, will explore complementary cultural meanings of St. Conal’s.

Meet: In front of St. Conal’s Hospital,  F92 FW6Y

6.30pm – 7.30pm (Duration 1 hour) No booking required.

 

This event is supported by the County Donegal Heritage Office and The Heritage Council as part of the implementation of the County Donegal Heritage Plan.

Image Credit: Courtesy of the National Library of Ireland.

title: St. Luke’s: 2FM Rising LIVE
description:
The 2FM Rising X Culture Night Live From St Luke’s Cork will feature performances from 2FM Rising artists MOIO,  Mischa and the Bear,  Run The Red, Chubby Cat and a live DJ set from 2FM DJ Graham Smyth.

(The gig will be broadcast simultaneously on RTE2FM in a special show hosted by 2FM New Music Show presenter Beta Da Silva)

Date: Friday 18th September
Doors: 7:00pm
DJ: 7:30pm
First band: 8:00pm

The event is 18+. Advanced booking is required via the link below.
Walk-up’s accommodated where space allows.
Please arrive before 8pm or your ticket may be reallocated.

MOIO doesn’t just make music, he commands emotion. In fact, the Nigerian-Irish singer, songwriter, producer, and multi-instrumentalist chases emotion with every lyric he pens, melody he sings, and beat, bassline, or guitar riff he plays. This pursuit has brought him to a space between genres, co-existing in the realms of R&B, indie, alternative, and soul—yet cleverly never committing to one above the other. By helming every aspect of his artistry, he’s able to operate fluidly, and his vision resonates across boundaries.

During 2023, he dropped “SUNBEAMING” followed by “Open Your Eyes,” which amassed over 2.3 million Spotify streams. On its heels, MOIO’s single “Moments,” started to go viral a year after its release, climbing north of 19 million Spotify streams and notably catapulted to number one on Spotify’s Viral 50 chart in the US, UK, Ireland, Canada, Norway, Denmark, and New Zealand. Along the way, he incited the applause of HYPEBEAST, Fashionably Early, Dancing Astronaut, and more in addition to performing at the likes of Dublin’s Forbidden Fruit Festival. Generating tens of millions of streams independently and attracting a growing fan base, he conjures palpable emotion on his 2025 “Earth Day” EP.  He released his latest single “Remember My Name” in July.

mischa and the bear are a Dublin-based alt-pop duo exploring the fragility of the human experience through unsettling synth-led soundscapes and stark lyrical honesty. The project features producer Danny “Mischa” Rooney and vocalist Fírinne “Bear” McIntyre whose creative partnership blends glitchy textures with haunting melodies and lyrics that linger like bruises. Since emerging in early 2025, they have quickly built a reputation for emotionally intelligent pop that does not flinch. With each track, mischa and the bear construct a vivid emotional atmosphere whether unpacking the toxic intensity of a fractured friendship “Forever Ago” or the strange comfort of emotional collapse in “Get Away”. Their music is deeply personal yet feels uncannily universal.

Chubby Cat

Chubby Cat has rapidly emerged as one of Ireland’s most exciting alt-pop voices. Known for her distinct individuality and sharp sense of style, she has made a strong impact across Ireland and the UK over the past two years. In early 2024, she received an RTÉ Choice Music Prize ‘Song of the Year’ nomination for Big Dog Barking, alongside recognition as an RTÉ 2FM Rising Artist and a Gay Times Breakthrough Act. That same year saw her perform at major festivals including Primavera Pro, Forbidden Fruit, Electric Picnic, Boardmasters, Brighton Pride, The Great Escape, Other Voices Dingle, Cardiff & Radar Festival in Zurich. She later earned nominations for Single of the Year and BBC Introducing Artist of the Year at the NI Music Prize. In 2025, Chubby Cat appeared on The Tommy Tiernan Show, received a second Choice Music Prize nomination for QUIET, and went viral performing with the RTÉ Concert Orchestra.

RuntheRed is an emerging Irish indie-alternative band formed in 2024 and based out of Meath, Dublin and Offaly. Their debut single “In Georgia” was released in October 2024, and since then they’ve been busy crafting a fresh sound for the Irish music scene. In less than a year as a fully formed band, RuntheRed earned a place on the RTÉ 2FM Rising List for 2026, marking them as one of Ireland’s most exciting new acts. Inspired by artists such as The Cranberries, The Frames, and boygenius, RuntheRed blends intimate storytelling with atmospheric indie soundscapes, exploring themes of love, identity, loss, and growing up. With their first headline show set for later in 2026 and work already underway on an ambitious concept album, RuntheRed continues to establish itself as one of Ireland’s most promising new bands.

title: Step back in time in The Liberties – Iveagh Trust Tour
description:
Explore the historic Iveagh Trust buildings and discover a remarkable chapter in Dublin’s social and architectural history this Culture Night. Founded by Edward Cecil Guinness, the Iveagh Trust was created to provide high-quality housing for Dublin’s working communities, and its red-brick buildings remain an enduring symbol of that vision.

 

Visitors are invited to take a tour of the Iveagh Trust building and time-travel to an era when social housing was a grand philanthropic gesture. Imagine red-brick facades rising proudly, hinting at the forward-thinking vision of Edward Cecil Guinness, who dreamt of better homes for Dublin’s working class. As you wander through the carefully preserved rooms, you can almost hear the echoes of families bustling about, the clatter of pots on the old range, and perhaps even the lively tunes from a piano in a cosy living room. It’s a delightful peek into a crucial chapter of Dublin’s history, showcasing not just architecture, but the very heart and soul of a community built with purpose and a surprising touch of elegance.

Tá turas ar thógra Imeacha Iveagh cosúil le taisteal tríd an am go tréimhse nuair a bhí tithíocht shóisialta, go hiontasach, ina ghníomh flaithiúil mór! Samhlaigh aghaidhí bricí dearga ag ardú go bródúil, ag leagan le fios ar fhís réamhghnóthach Edward Cecil Guinness, a bhrionglóidigh faoi thithe níos fearr do rang oibre Bhaile Átha Cliath. Agus tú ag siúl trí na seomraí a coimeádadh go cúramach, is féidir leat beagán go cloisteáil macallaí teaghlaigh ag gluaiseacht thart, torann potaí ar an seastán bán seanbhunaithe, agus b’fhéidir fiú na ceolchoirmeacha beoga ó phianó i seomra suí teolaí. Is léargas deas é ar chaibidil thábhachtach de stair Bhaile Átha Cliath, ag taispeáint ní hamháin ailtireacht, ach croí agus spiorad an phobail a tógadh le cuspóir agus le teagmháil iontasach áilleachta.

title: Still Standing: An exhibition by Edward (Ed) Quinn
description:
Edward Quinn was born in Belfast, where he studied at The Ulster College of Art and Design, gaining an Honours Degree in Fine Art.

He has lived in Co. Cork for over 40 years, and is well-known, both as a teacher of Art, at Regina Mundi College, Douglas, and as an artist himself. Many young, and not so young, students have been inspired by the passion he exudes for every aspect of his subject.

Ed’s retirement has given him the freedom to explore new pathways, drawing him into the wonders of the natural world that is Ireland, with its mountains, rivers, lakes and wild, rugged coastline: in particular, he has become fascinated by  the forests of Ireland, whose mysterious ancient trees never cease to captivate him, as they change in shape, colour and mood, from season to season.

More recently, he returned to the world of abstract art, with free-flowing, vibrant images which border on the surreal. He feels that a strange symbiosis has developed between the “impressionist” landscape work and these newer, more strident pieces, as they seem to co-exist, unexpectedly, with his inspiration passing between the two styles quite freely.

This wonderfully bright summer of 2026 has pulled Ed back to his love of flowers, both wild and cultivated, giving him an exciting new perspective, which can be clearly seen in many of the pieces showing here.

This exhibition is a reflection of the three pathways he has been following.

Edwards paintings can  be seen in several galleries around Ireland, including….

 

The Purcell Gallery, Kenmare, Co. Kerry

The Castlemartyr House Gallery, East Cork

Draiocht, Adare, Co. Limerick

The Aisling, Ballydehob

 

and in private collections, both here and abroad..

 

exhibition by Kildorrery artist, Edward (Ed) Quinn is courtesy of Blackwater Valley Makers, Fermoy

title: Stories from the Poor House with Mary Ann McCracken
description:
Step inside Clifton House, Belfast’s Grade A listed former Poor House, and discover the remarkable stories held within its walls.

Be warmly welcomed by Mary Ann McCracken before embarking on a short 30 minute guided journey through the social history of the Poor House, exploring the lives of the people who sought sanctuary here and discovering a legacy shaped by compassion, reform and resilience.

Opened in 1774, Clifton House provided shelter and support to thousands of people over the centuries — from young children and older citizens to local residents and passing sailors.

Come and uncover the history, hear the stories, and experience the enduring legacy of one of Belfast’s most significant historic buildings.

title: Storytelling Session: A Cosmic Apprenticeship – Stories from The Life and Liberation of Padmasambhava
description:
Discover the story of one of the most influential figures in Tibetan Buddhism in this storytelling session at the Dublin Buddhist Centre.

‘The Life and Liberation of Padmasambhava’ is a glittering, multi-faceted jewel of world literature, an epic poem that offers a vivid introduction to the history, mythology, and rich, evocative culture of Tibet. The eponymous Padmasambhava, a historical figure who travelled from India in the 8th century, is revered in Tibet as a second Buddha and is celebrated for his role in establishing and spreading Buddhism across the region over the past 1200 years.

In this storytelling session, Vidyasakhi will introduce audiences to Padmasambhava at the moment he begins a forty-year journey of training on the path to becoming a Bodhisattva—an enlightened being dedicated to the liberation of all others. The story culminates in his extraordinary encounter with Princess Mandarava, his companion and a woman renowned for her courage, wisdom, and determination.

title: Substance to Shadows Exhibition
description:
Kyrre Mogster presents Substance to Shadows, a body of paintings depicting a kind of hedonism and human folly. Made with ink and oil stick on canvas, the series uses excess, indulgence, and collapse as an allegory for what results from dogmatic thinking — when ideas harden and refuse to be questioned.

The inspiration for the work comes from a series of books by American sociologist Alvin Gouldner that addresses the dangers of failing to confront and interrogate our ideological biases. For Mogster, Gouldner’s warning becomes visual. In these monotone paintings, figures gorge, posture, and unravel. Pleasure turns to excess. Certainty turns to shadow. The work asks what happens when we stop testing our beliefs against the world.

Recurring motifs — vessels, limbs, tools, empty thrones — suggest rituals of consumption and authority. These are not portraits of specific people, but allegories. They depict the moment when conviction becomes performance, and performance becomes folly.

Substance to Shadows does not offer resolution. In the spirit of Gouldner, it asks us to stay with contradiction. To look at the dark side of the dialectic, where thesis and antithesis refuse to synthesize. In a time of fixed positions, the paintings propose a slower look: at texture, at doubt, and at what remains when certainty falls away.

Discover Substance to Shadows at TØN Gallery this Culture Night.

title: SUBTERRA: What’s Lost & What’s Left
description:
SUBTERRA: What’s Lost & What’s Left is a deep-listening experience created and produced
under the banner of saltstate. Attendees are invited to enter into a dedicated deep listening
environment, to be still and to immerse themselves into a gentle sensory deprivation, where
they will listen to experimental, electronic music performed by an Irish-based artist.
For Culture Night 2026, we are coming to SOLAS Visitor Centre, Aghleam Co. Mayo. We
have drawn inspiration from local history; of the lighthouse that was lost to the Atlantic, and
the four towers that remain to this day, a story that prompted us to reflect upon “What’s Lost
& What’s Left”.
Performing artists are invited to step away from high-energy dancefloor sets and explore
atmospheric, hypnotic, and experimental selections rarely heard in standard venues. The
lineup features live electronic artist and producer, Dashamlav and Dublin-based DJ, SAZ.
The event is structured into two distinct sessions to cater to different listening dynamics:
● Session 1: 4PM-7PM (All Ages Suitable): Soundtracked by Dashamlav, offering an
accessible, ambient-leaning soundscape suitable for all ages.
Born in India and based in Ireland, Dashamlav is a live electronic artist and producer
shaping intimate, atmospheric sets influenced by displacement, memory, and the
search for home.
● Session 2: 7PM-10PM (Older Audiences): Soundtracked by SAZ, drawing deeper
elements from club culture with a louder, darker sound profile, best suited to older
participants.
SAZ is a Dublin-based DJ and radio host with a deep-rooted love for the Irish dance
scene and a passion for championing local talent. Her sets move fluidly across
electronic music, from groovy and playful to darker, harder and more hypnotic,
always guided by the energy of the room.
**Please ensure to choose the correct session to suit your needs.
Both sessions operate under a shared agreement of audience silence, turning the focus
entirely to sound. Listeners are invited to sit back, feel the physical frequencies, and
submerge in the experience of listening to electronic music outside of a crowded club
setting. Each performance is followed by a social reception.
At its core, SUBTERRA champions the vital importance of communal gathering; by
committing to a shared silence, the audience actively shapes the environment, collectively
enhancing the deep listening experience for both themselves and everyone around them.
This event is supported by funding from Mayo County Council for Culture Night 2026.
fullAddress: Aghleam, County Mayo, Ireland

title: Such Sweet Sorrow at The Pearse Centre
description:
This Culture Night, The Pearse Centre presents Such Sweet Sorrow, a heartfelt Irish drama exploring love, memory, and the lives we imagine for ourselves.

Blending humour with emotional honesty, the play follows two people as they reflect on the dreams they once shared and the realities that shaped who they became. Set against the backdrop of the creative world, it explores the sacrifices demanded by ambition, the pressures of family expectations, and the uncertainty of choosing passion over security.

Rich in wit, warmth, and distinctly Irish charm, Such Sweet Sorrow is a moving exploration of first love, friendship, regret, and gratitude. As past and present intertwine, the play reflects on growing older, holding on to cherished memories, and finding beauty in the bittersweet act of looking back.

title: Swift’s Dublin: A Walking Tour
description:
St Patrick’s Mental Health Services invites Culture Night visitors to step into the world of Jonathan Swift on a guided walking tour exploring the streets, stories and characters that shaped 18th-century Dublin.

Led by the Archivist at St Patrick’s Mental Health Services, the tour traces Swift’s life and legacy through the city he called home, exploring his role as Dean of St Patrick’s Cathedral, his advocacy for the poor and his enduring influence on Irish literature and society. Along the route, visitors will encounter artworks inspired by Gulliver’s Travels, created to mark the 300th anniversary of the publication of Swift’s celebrated work.

The tour concludes at St Patrick’s University Hospital, founded through Swift’s remarkable bequest of £12,000 in 1745. Opened in 1746, it was the first psychiatric hospital in Ireland and among the first in the world.

This free one-hour walking tour begins near Christ Church Cathedral and finishes at St Patrick’s University Hospital.

title: Textile and Mixed Media Art Installations
description:
Mary Palmer is the founder of Marimu Designs and has been creating textile art and quilts since 2006. With more than 25 years of involvement in the Cork quilting community, she has contributed through exhibitions, teaching, and leadership roles in national quilting organisations.

Rooted in the traditions of quilting, her practice explores new ways of interpreting the medium and challenges conventional expectations. Inspired by music, colour, memory, history, social justice, and politics, her work invites viewers to reconsider how they perceive the world. 

Pamela Hardesty is an American-born textile artist based in Ireland whose work explores materiality, memory, and spirituality. Combining textiles with drawing, paint, paper, and mixed media, she creates layered works that bridge textile art and fine art.

Through stitching, layering, and mark-making, she investigates themes of faith, contemplation, and human experience. Treating cloth as a conceptual rather than purely functional medium, Hardesty transforms traditional textile techniques into contemporary visual expressions that encourage reflection on memory, place, and the sacred in everyday life.

Together, the artists present textiles as a dynamic contemporary art form, encouraging visitors to experience the medium in unexpected ways. Their works address social, environmental, and personal narratives, highlighting the versatility of textiles as a vehicle for both creative expression and critical reflection.

title: The Art of Conversation – Photography Exhibition
description:
The Art of Conversation is an exhibition of documentary portraits of the people of Lanesboro, Co. Longford.
Over the past few years, I have been photographing people from around the town. Alongside each portrait is a short snippet from a conversation we had, remembered afterwards and chosen because it captured something about the person or the moment we shared.

The photographs were taken in places that are familiar to each person, whether that was their home, workplace or somewhere that formed part of their everyday life. Together, the images and words offer a glimpse into the people who make Lanesboro what it is.

Many of those featured have lived in Lanesboro all their lives and have seen the town change over the years. Sadly, some have passed away since they were photographed, making these portraits an important record of people whose presence and stories remain part of the community.

This exhibition invites visitors to take their time, look beyond the photograph and read the words beside it. You may recognise a neighbour, a friend or someone you have known for years. My hope is that The Art of Conversation reminds us of the value of stopping to talk, to listen and to appreciate the people around us before those moments become memories.

Is taispeántas é ‘Ealaín na Comhrá’ de phortráidí doiciméadaithe de mhuintir Lanesboro, Co. Longfort. Le cúpla bliain anuas, bhí mé ag glacadh grianghraf de dhaoine ar fud an bhaile. In aice le gach portráid tá píosa beag as comhrá a bhí againn, cuimhneamh ina dhiaidh sin agus roghnaithe toisc gur ghlac sé rud éigin den duine nó den nóiméad a roinn muid. Tógadh na grianghraif i gceantair atá eolach ar gach duine, bíodh sin ina mbaile, in áit oibre nó áit a bhí mar chuid dá saol laethúil. Le chéile, tairgeann na híomhánna agus na focail spléachadh ar na daoine a dhéanann Lanesboro mar atá sé.

Tá go leor de na daoine a bhfuil siad le feiceáil anseo ina gcónaí i Lanesboro ar feadh a saoil go léir agus tá siad feicthe ag an mbaile ag athrú thar na blianta. Ar an drochuair, tá cuid acu imithe ar shlí na fírinne ó fuarthas a ngrianghraif, ag déanamh na portráidí seo ina thaifead tábhachtach d’fhir agus de mhná a bhfuil a láithreacht agus a scéalta fós mar chuid den phobal.

Tugann an taispeántas seo cuireadh do chuairteoirí a gcuid ama a ghlacadh, féachaint níos faide ná an grianghraf agus na focail atá in aice leis a léamh. B’fhéidir go aithneoidh tú comharsan, cara nó éinne a bhfuil aithne agat air le blianta. Tá súil agam go gcuimhneoidh The Art of Conversation orainn ar luach na stopadh chun labhairt, chun éisteacht agus chun meas a bheith againn ar na daoine mórthimpeall orainn sula mbíonn na chuimhneacháin sin ina cuimhní.

title: The Banking Hall: A Dublin Landmark
description:
Step inside The Banking Hall at The College Green Hotel this Culture Night and discover a remarkable piece of Dublin’s architectural and cultural history.

Originally established in 1813 by the Royal Irish Institution to promote the arts in Ireland through exhibitions of Old Master works, the building was demolished in 1863 and rebuilt in 1866 as the headquarters of the Provincial Bank. Designed by architect William G. Murray, the impressive three-storey, seven-bay building features a grand pediment and imposing columns, reflecting the ambition and elegance of Victorian Dublin. For more than a century, the building served as a working bank. In 1966, it became a branch of the newly formed Allied Irish Bank.

Despite its changing role, the Banking Hall retained many of its original architectural features, including encaustic tiled floors, high ceilings, ornate plasterwork and magnificent marble columns. A major restoration project, beginning in 1999, returned the Banking Hall to much of its former grandeur. Original hand-carved details, decorative plasterwork and encaustic tiles were carefully restored, while the historic bank logo remains visible. One of the most striking features visitors can experience today is the series of four replica crystal chandeliers, each made from more than 8,000 pieces of Waterford Crystal and suspended from the spectacular 15-metre-high ceilings. The restored stained-glass roof adds another layer of colour and character to this extraordinary historic space.

title: The Blue In Between, a public artwork by Silvina Sisterna
description:
Silvina Sisterna’s Flags, The Blue In Between, convey her experience of migration as the space that exists between places, belonging not as a destination but something that forms slowly through repetition, movement, and everyday encounters with the landscape.

On Wellington Quay, the Flags will continue to move with the weather, staying in conversation with the changing river below.

Sisterna writes:
“My Flags emerged from walks on my way to and from my studio, returning to the same stretch of river and observing how it shifts through tides, weather, light and the movement of the city. As a migrant woman living in Dublin, this repeated journey has helped me learn about the city. The river feels familiar, yet elusive; it is always moving and never entirely fixed.”

Blending cyanotype with mixed media, she allows water and chance actively shape the work and respond to the river’s rhythms. The material’s process’s uncertainty reflects the artist’s experience of migration, where identity and belonging are continually negotiated rather than set in stone.

Silvina Sisterna is a Dublin based visual artist whose practice explores migration, belonging, memory, and relationships between people and place through alternative photographic processes, walking, writing and socially engaged collaborative practice.

The Blue In Between Flags will fly throughout the week of Culture Night. Silvina Sisterna will also be hosting a drop-in workshop which will take place from 14:00-20:00 on Culture Night.

title: The Bovinity – A reading and Q&A session of a play by Rory Nevin
description:
A reading and Q&A session of a play by Rory Nevin. This is a work in progress that explores a future dystopian Ireland where dairy cows are charge.

A one-person show where the story is from the perspective of one of the scientists who was responsible for the “Super cows” known as “The Mook”. The creatures were developed using genetic engineering and two types of AI – Artificial Insemination and Artificial Intelligence.

Things got out of hand and somehow they now rule the country and perhaps the planet. They hunt the scientist who has gone into hiding.

The play explores the dairy industry, methods and processes of dairy farming, treatment of animals (and cruelty) in terms of making profits, Irish mythology and language and cows.

The reading will be performed by an actor. The writer and actor will take any questions on its conclusion.

title: The Caochaleleles
description:
Step into the historic Donaghmore Corn Mill and Kiln for a lively Culture Night celebration of music, community and vintage heritage. The evening brings together the feel-good sound of The Caochaleleles with an introduction to I.V.E.T.A.’s work restoring this remarkable mill complex and developing its future as a museum.

The Caochaleleles began in September 2025 as a community initiative inviting people to meet, laugh, chat and enjoy learning the ukulele together. Based at Caoch O’Leary’s in Ballacolla, the group meets every Monday evening under the musical guidance of Valerie Cassin and has grown from 15 founding members to more than 60 players.

Joined by talented local musicians, the group brings an uplifting, fun-loving sound to favourites by The Pogues, The Saw Doctors, The Cranberries, Johnny Cash and more. Their recent appearances for Aghaboe Senior Citizens, at The Tower Inn in Timahoe and at Abbeyleix House and Farm have built their reputation as a warm, energetic ensemble ready to leave Culture Night audiences smiling.

The Irish Vintage Engine and Tractor Association, I.V.E.T.A., is a leading presence in Ireland’s vintage community, representing more than 12,500 enthusiasts in every county as well as members overseas.

Since purchasing Donaghmore Corn Mill and Kiln in 2012, I.V.E.T.A. has been steadily restoring the historic buildings and surrounding grounds while improving access and visitor facilities. Its long-term vision is to create an on-site museum showcasing the mill complex alongside selected vintage equipment.

title: THE CHAPTER CLINIC- a writing workshop for novelists and aspiring novelists
description:
A Once Off Workshop with author and writing tutor Martin J. P. Devaney

Booking requested but not essential – drop in ! 

A novel lives or dies by its opening pages. The first chapter must capture a reader’s attention, establish character and voice, create curiosity, and persuade readers to turn the page. It is also the section most likely to determine whether an agent, editor or publisher continues reading.

Drawing on techniques from his book  The Art of Writing a Novel – The XYZ Method, this practical workshop will help participants develop, refine and strengthen the opening chapter of their novel. Through discussion, analysis, exercises and feedback, writers will learn how to create an opening that engages editors from the very first page.

Participants will examine successful examples from contemporary fiction and apply these techniques directly to their own work.

The crucial dos and don’ts of novel submissions are covered.

The workshop is open to writers at all levels—beginner, intermediate and advanced.

Martin JP Devaney

Martin J. P. Devaney is a novelist, playwright, screenwriter, broadcaster and writing tutor with more than three decades of professional experience across literature, theatre, radio and television.

He is the author of The RTÉ Writer’s Guide and the recently published The Art of Writing a Novel – The XYZ Method. His work has been produced and broadcast by RTÉ, the BBC, the Abbey Theatre and theatres in Ireland and internationally. He has written radio dramas, comedy series, short stories, television programmes and short films, and has produced more than ninety-nine television programmes.

Alongside his own writing career, Martin has taught creative writing workshops for many years and has worked with numerous emerging writers at the beginning of their careers.

His most recent novel was published in the UK in 2024. He lives in Ireland and continues to teach workshops on fiction, storytelling and the craft of writing.

For more information please visit martinjpdevaney.com

title: The Common Tune with the Ceoltóirí Bianconi Collective, Culture Night Special Event
description:
The Common Tune with the Ceoltóirí Bianconi Collective, Culture Night Special Event is a community music project Ag Ceiliúradh Bhanlaochra Pheil Cheatharlach , celebrating the football heroines of Carlow through music and providing a participatory musical experience.

The Ceoltóirí Bianconi Collective have commissioned Leitrim singer/songwriter Michael McKenna to create a new song celebrating the remarkable achievements of the Carlow women’s football team. The song will be played as part of Culture Night alongside a some of the more common traditional tunes and folk songs, designed to encourage participation, connection and shared enjoyment.

At the heart of this event is the collective’s warm welcome — bringing people together across generations and backgrounds in a spirit of creativity, community and celebration.

This project builds on previous successful community collaborations by the collective, including the recording, teaching and public performance of Michael McKenna’s Carlow of My Dreams’ a song that resonated strongly with Carlow audiences at home and abroad and demonstrated the power of music to foster local pride, belonging and cultural connection.

description:
Step into The Craft Studios this Culture Night for an evening of creativity, craft and making by hand.

Taking place at the College of FET Mulgrave Street Campus, these special studio sessions offer the chance to explore both ceramics and textile crafts in a fun and welcoming environment.

Discover the fascinating process of yarn spinning on a traditional wheel with live demonstrations showing how raw fleece is transformed into beautiful handmade yarn.

Explore alpaca and sheep fleece at different stages of processing, learn about traditional spinning techniques and see finished examples created from both single and two-ply yarn.
Alongside this, participants can get hands-on with clay and experiment with shaping, forming and surface decoration techniques while learning more about the ceramic process in a relaxed studio setting.

Whether you are curious about traditional crafts, looking to try something new or simply want to spend an evening surrounded by creativity, The Craft Studios offers a unique Culture Night experience celebrating making, materials and imagination.

description:
“The Crossroads” is a Culture Night event hosted by ‘Clogh Writers’ celebrating local heritage, memories, creativity and community spirit. Through a varied programme of performances, readings and presentations, audiences will be invited to take a journey “Down Memory Lane”.

The evening will feature poetry and short story readings by members of our writers’ group, music and dance performances, and a one-act drama by a local  group. A highlight of the programme will be the screening of highlights of ‘A New Landlord’ by Brian Stynes, a short film produced locally with the support of community members who contributed acting roles, props, premises, sets, hair and makeup.

Adding to the atmosphere, local participants in period costume will bring elements of our shared history to life. The event aims to celebrate culture, storytelling, collaboration and the rich heritage of our community.

title: The Culture of Bread – Bretzel Bakery
description:
Bretzel Bakery – The Culture of Bread Bretzel Bakery, Lennox St. | September 18th, 5pm–9pm

At Bretzel, bread is a measure of character, care and culture. It means choosing patience over instant gratification, using honest ingredients, and keeping connections alive with the communities we bake for and the people who grow with us. For Culture Night 2026, we invite visitors to experience “The Culture of Bread”, an evening celebrating traditional baking, craftsmanship and community!

The evening will be complete with: Live Baking Demonstrations Throughout the evening, our bakers will demonstrate the baking of three traditional breads: Focaccia – exploring stretching and shaping techniques. Sourdough – from mixing and natural fermentation to the importance of time. French baguettes – highlighting their distinct shaping and baking process. Tastings

Visitors can enjoy fresh sourdough, crispy baguettes, and focaccia variations. This will also give us an opportunity to engage with our local community and gather feedback as we prepare to introduce new sandwich varieties at the bakery. Traditional Irish Music Live traditional music will create a warm, welcoming atmosphere and celebrate Bretzel’s role as a neighbourhood bakery, connecting food, culture and community. Take Home a Sourdough Starter Reviving one of Bretzel’s most successful Covid-era community initiatives, visitors can take home their own sourdough starter and continue the experience and tradition of baking at home.

The Culture of Bread brings Irish and European baking traditions together through food, craft, music and participation, making artisan bread accessible, engaging and deeply connected to community.

title: The Dead House by Martin Beanz Warde
description: Patrick is an Irish Traveller who hasn’t been home in 10 years but returns from self-exile for his grandfather’s funeral. Comedian and writer Martin Beanz Warde’s debut play is a powerful and moving dark comedy that explores complex themes of family, tradition, and self-acceptance. Set in the house of the deceased, the play is a testament to the resilience of the human spirit and the importance of finding one’s voice and identity. The show has previously enjoyed sold-out runs at Dublin Theatre Festival, Galway Theatre Festival and Kilkenny Arts Festvial, and has toured internationally.

title: The Disappearing
description:
The Disappearing is an installation of sculptures in and along the river in Gort by artists Bríd Kivneen and Diana Rogerson with music from Eugene Lambe.

The sculptures are designed to disappear in time, celebrating the river and biodiversity in Gort. We will be using mixed media, materials like clay, straw, nettles, reeds, wool, bones, sticks and found objects to create a story of installations along and in the river. Including a local professional piper / instrument maker who will play Irish traditional music on the bridge which spans the river. He will be playing music to the launch of a sculpture (bio degradable) piece into the river to celebrate the movement of the water. The start of the walk will be welcoming people with a violin player and a person dressed as a rabbit, to remind us that we are in wonderland. This will take place in twilight and finish with a celebration of food and drink with leaflets to document the sculptural pieces.

title: The Evening Chapter
description:
Join us as Edgeworthstown comes alive for an unforgettable evening celebrating creativity, community and culture.

From 5pm until late, the town will transform into a vibrant cultural trail, with live performances, music, dance, art, film and heritage experiences taking place across multiple venues. Wander through the Maria Edgeworth Visitor Centre, enjoy an outdoor concert on The Green featuring local performers alongside multicultural community groups, discover local artists and filmmakers at Co:Worx, and relax with live music in participating cafés.

As darkness falls, make your way to the Library Plaza where everyone is invited to take part in a lively outdoor set dancing session with Shane Ryan and the Joe Callaghan Group. Whether you choose to dance or simply enjoy the atmosphere, this promises to be a memorable finale to the evening.

With free admission to all events, Edgeworthstown United: A Night of Culture celebrates everything that makes our town unique—its rich heritage, talented artists, welcoming businesses and growing, diverse community. By linking venues across the town centre into one shared cultural experience, the event encourages visitors to explore, connect and discover something new around every corner.

Bring your family, meet your neighbours, support local businesses and experience an evening where music, storytelling, history, creativity and community come together in the heart of Edgeworthstown. Everyone is welcome.

Bí linn agus Edgeworthstown ag teacht beo le haghaidh oíche nach ndéanfar dearmad uirthi chun cruthaitheacht, pobal agus cultúr a cheiliúradh. Ó 5in go déanach san oíche, athróidh an baile ina rian cultúrtha beoga, le léirithe beo, ceol, damhsa, ealaín, scannán agus taithí oidhreachta ag tarlú i go leor áiteanna éagsúla. Siúil trí Lárionad Cuairteoirí Maria Edgeworth, bain sult as ceolchoirm lasmuigh ar The Green le ceoltóirí áitiúla chomh maith le grúpaí pobail ilchultúrtha, faigh amach ealaíontóirí agus scannánadóirí áitiúla ag Co:Worx, agus suanú le ceol beo i gcáiféanna rannpháirteacha. Nuair a thagann dorchadas, téigh go dtí Plaza na Leabharlainne áit a bhfuil gach duine fásta le hathnuachaint ar sheisiún damhsóireachta lasmuigh beo le Shane Ryan agus Grúpa Joe Callaghan. Cibé an roghnaíonn tú damhsa nó taitneamh a bhaint as an atmaisféar amháin, geallann sé seo a bheith ina chríoch chuimhneacháin ar an oíche.

Le hiontráil saor in aisce chuig gach imeacht, Edgeworthstown United: Oíche Cultúir ceiliúrann gach rud a dhéanann ár mbaile uathúil—a oidhreacht shaibhir, ealaíontóirí cumasacha, gnóthaí fáilteacha agus pobal ag fás, ilchineálach. Trí láithreacha a nascadh timpeall lár na cathrach le chéile in aon taithí chultúrtha roinnte, spreagann an t-imeacht cuairteoirí chun iniúchadh a dhéanamh, ceangal a dhéanamh agus rud éigin nua a fháil i ngach cúinne.

Tóg do theaghlach leat, bualadh le do chomharsana, tacú le gnóthaí áitiúla agus taithí a fháil ar oíche ina dtagann ceol, scéalta, stair, cruthaitheacht agus pobail le chéile i gcroílár Edgeworthstown. Fáilte roimh chách.

Visitors will have the opportunity to watch a selection of short films and take part in a Q&A with some of the featured filmmakers, offering a unique insight into the creative process behind the work.

title: The Fire Next Time – Culture Night Special
description:
This Culture Night, join historian Richard Carson for The Fire Next Time, a new walking tour of Marlborough Street exploring the intertwined histories of deferred justice, secularity, gender, and social change through the stories of five fires spanning more than 270 years.

Following the success of Carson’s Race and Place in the City walking tour, featured on RTÉ Lyric FM and presented as part of Culture Night from 2023–2025, this tour brings together history, sociology, theology, and place to reveal unexpected stories that transform our imaginations of the place. Along the way, participants will encounter a divided mob united against a surprising common enemy, a terrorist attack that took an unexpected turn, and the forgotten twentieth-century laundry where women were once confined as ‘inmates’.

Advance booking is essential, as places are limited.

description:
On the occasion of Culture Night 2026, the Italian Institute of Culture in Dublin opens the doors of Sala Bellini for an evening of live music, performances, community, and cultural exchange.

The Floor is Yours at the IIC on Culture Night is an initiative designed to give a platform to Italian artists, musicians, performers, and entertainers living in Ireland, as well as those inspired by Italian culture, offering them the opportunity to showcase their talent and create new connections through art and culture.

Throughout the evening, a diverse programme of performances spanning different genres and disciplines will give audiences the chance to discover emerging talent, experience the vibrant Italian—and wider—artistic community in Ireland, and enjoy the Institute as an open, dynamic, and inclusive cultural space.

Through this initiative, the Italian Institute of Culture aims to embrace the spirit of Culture Night by promoting intercultural dialogue, creativity, and community participation, while offering an authentic and engaging cultural experience in the heart of Dublin.

This Culture Night, Photo Museum Ireland, the national centre for contemporary photography, invites visitors to Temple Bar for free guided tours of its current exhibition, Robert Ellis: The Forbidden Sun.

Through photography, video and ambient sound, this major new body of work explores the experience of growing up queer and closeted in rural Ireland. Ellis creates a haunting landscape where natural and industrial forces collide, reflecting on silence, shame, desire and emotional endurance.

Join the Museum team for a guided tour and gain deeper insight into the ideas and personal experiences that have shaped this exhibition.

Tours take place every hour from 16:00 until late.

title: The Fynches
description:
The Fynches are an Irish folk-rock band led by brothers Ferdia and Oisín Walsh-Peelo, blending early-70s swagger with rich vocal harmonies, soulful keys, evocative lyricism and soaring strings. Completing the line-up are Cian O’Sullivan (drums), Fionn O’Neill (bass) and Julianne Quirke (cello).

Raised in a musical family in County Wicklow, Ferdia and Oisín have spent the past decade developing their songwriting partnership, built around interlocking harmonies and a shared love of experimentation. Their self-titled debut album was released in October 2025, followed by extensive Irish, UK and European touring. Renowned as an electrifying live act, the band’s music ranges from brooding ballads to raucous crowd-pleasers.

Oisín has toured and recorded with Villagers, Flyte, Hudson Taylor and Bombay Bicycle Club, while Ferdia is known for starring in Sing Street, CODA, Pistol and Four Letters of Love. The Fynches have also earned acclaim through RTÉ Radio 1, The Late Late Show and live performances across Ireland.

In June 2026, the band recorded their second album at Middle Farm Studios in Devon with producer Pete Miles. Written, recorded, mixed and mastered in just one month, the album marks a new chapter in their songwriting and is set for release in March 2027.

For Culture Night The Fynches will present a special preformance of their material as a trio for what is sure to be a special occasion!

title: The Gravedigger Ghost Bus Tour
description:
This Culture Night, step aboard the Gravedigger Ghost Bus Tour for a spine-tingling journey through Dublin’s darker history. Departing from Trinity College Dublin, visitors will be transported back through six centuries of plague, mystery, and folklore by costumed guides who bring the city’s most chilling stories to life.

The tour visits some of Dublin’s most intriguing historic sites, including St Audoen’s Church, long associated with tales of restless spirits, and Kilmainham Gaol, the setting for many of Ireland’s most significant and tragic events. Visitors will also explore a centuries-old cemetery said to hold the remains of hundreds of thousands of people, including victims linked to the notorious body-snatching trade.

The evening concludes at the famous Gravediggers Pub, where guests can enjoy a complimentary Ghoulish Brew.

Combining history, storytelling, and theatrical performance, this immersive experience offers a fascinating glimpse into Dublin’s haunted past and the legends that continue to captivate audiences today.

title: The Great Debate: An Election Night
description:
The Great Debate is a live satirical political performance by Red Bird Youth Collective, presented as the culmination of a 2026 project supported by the Arts Council’s Children and Young People’s Project Award and Galway City Council. Audiences are invited to witness campaign speeches, political promises, public debates and election drama as members embody characters from three fictional political parties: the Pangea Party, Green Party and Other Party. Developed through a year-long sculptural and world-building project, each party has its own visual identity, campaign aesthetics and political agenda. Blending performance, sculpture, costume, satire and youth voices, this engaging cultural experience invites audiences to engage with contemporary questions about democracy, media, identity and political spectacle. Audience members will be encouraged to ask questions, interact with candidates and cast votes in a mock election. A unique feature of the performance is the participation of a Green Party candidate joining the debate live on screen from Finland. Having relocated during the project, they remain an active member of the collective and will participate remotely, bringing an international dimension to the event

Is taibhiú polaitiúil beo, aorach é The Great Debate de chuid an Red Bird Youth Collective, a chuirtear i láthair mar bhuaicphointe ar thionscadal 2026 le tacaíocht ó Dhámhachtain Tionscadail Leanaí agus Daoine Óga na Comhairle Ealaíon agus Chomhairle Cathrach na Gaillimhe. Tugtar cuireadh don lucht féachana óráidí feachtais, geallúintí polaitiúla, díospóireachtaí poiblí agus corraíl toghcháin a fheiceáil agus na baill i bpáirt carachtair ó thrí pháirtí polaitiúla ficseanúla: an Páirtí Pangea, an Páirtí Glas agus an Páirtí Eile. Forbraíodh é trí thionscadal dealbhóireachta agus tógála domhain a mhair ar feadh bliana, agus tá a bhféiniúlacht fhisiúil, aeistéitic feachtais agus clár oibre polaitiúil féin ag gach páirtí acu. Agus an taibhiú, dealbhóireacht, an gléasadh, an aoir agus guthanna na hóige á meascadh le chéile, tabharfar cuireadh don lucht féachana leis an eispéireas cultúrtha tarraingteach seo aghaidh a thabhairt ar cheisteanna comhaimseartha faoin daonlathas, faoi na meáin, faoin bhféiniúlacht agus faoi shaol aisteach na polaitíochta. Spreagfar an lucht féachana le ceisteanna a chur, idirghníomhú leis na hiarrthóirí agus vótaí a chaitheamh i dtoghchán bréige. Gné thar a bheith spéisiúil den taibhiú is ea go mbeidh iarrthóir ón bPáirtí Glas sa bhFionlainn ag glacadh páirt sa díospóireacht agus é beo ar an scáileán ón bhFionlainn. Featuring live music, a Polish choir, authentic traditional costumes, storytelling, and folk dance demonstrations, this unique Culture Night event brings the spirit of a Polish wedding to life. Discover the customs surrounding the giving away of the bride, explore regional traditions, and learn about the role of music and community in Polish celebrations.
Most importantly, this is not a performance to simply watch—it’s an experience to join. Audience members will be encouraged to participate in traditional dances, learn simple folk dance steps, sing along, and become part of the celebration.
This family-friendly event celebrates cultural diversity, community connection, and shared experiences through music and dance. Whether you have Polish roots or are discovering Polish culture for the first time, come along and enjoy an unforgettable evening filled with laughter, live music, movement, and tradition.
No dance experience required—just bring your enthusiasm and join the party!

title: The Mansion House: Self Guided Tour
description:
This Culture Night, visitors are invited to explore the public rooms of the Mansion House, the official residence of Dublin’s Lord Mayor. Built by Joshua Dawson and the setting for important civic and historic events for more than 300 years, the Mansion House offers a fascinating glimpse into Dublin’s political and cultural history.

Visitors can enjoy a self-guided tour of the Oak Room, Drawing Room, Dining Room, and Lady Mayoress Parlour, with staff on hand throughout the evening to answer questions and provide assistance.

The highlight of the tour is the Oak Room, created as part of the original purchase agreement with Joshua Dawson. As its name suggests, the room is panelled entirely in oak, with some of the original panelling still preserved. Designed for civic receptions over three centuries ago, it continues to serve that purpose today. The room also houses notable portraits, including that of Charles Stewart Parnell, founder of the Home Rule Party, and displays the individual coats of arms created for Dublin’s Lord Mayors in consultation with the Chief Herald of Ireland.

Siúil tríd na seomraí phoiblí den áras cónaithe oifigiúil an Ard-Mhéara, tógtha ag Joshua Dawson agus  a bhí ina láthair d’imeachtaí sibhialta agus stairiúla tábhachtacha le breis agus 300 bliain. Féach ar Seomra Darach, an Seomra Líníochta, an Proinnseomra, agus Parlús bean an Ardmhéara. Beidh foireann ar fáil chun cabhrú. Tógadh an Seomra Darach mar choinníoll den chomhaontú ceannaigh le Joshua Dawson. Mar a thugann an t-ainm le fios, tá sé painéalta go hiomlán as darach, agus cuid den phainéal bunaidh fós ina áit.

Dearadh é breis agus 300 bliain ó shin le haghaidh fáiltithe sibhialta, agus úsáidtear é chun na cuspóir seo fós inniu.

Tá roinnt portráidí breátha sa seomra, ina measc portráidí de Charles Stewart Parnell, bunaitheoir Pháirtí an Rialtais Dúchais. Tá armas aonair Ardmhéaraí Bhaile Átha Cliath ar taispeáint anseo chomh maith.

Buaileann gach Ardmhéara le Príomh-Aralt na hÉireann, atá lonnaithe sa Leabharlann Náisiúnta, le chéile chun comhaontú maidir le Cóta Armais a léiríonn a saol.

title: The Night Institute
description:
The Night Institute is bringing its brand of Belfast nightlife to Hill Street on Culture Night.

From 6 -11pm, the outdoor space at the 44 Hill Street restaurant will become home to The Night Institute while serving up pizza, small plates, beers, wines and spirits, with a soundtrack provided by TNI residents Timmy Stewart & Jordan Nocturne.

The Night Institute is an independent Belfast club night, creative community and record label, built around a love of great electronic music and good people. Over the years, its parties have popped up everywhere from clubs and pubs to open-air spaces, developing a reputation for energetic nights that move freely between house, disco, techno and everything in between.

title: The Ocean Beacon: Interactive Stained-Glass Sunset Workshop &  Installation
description:
Welcome to “The Ocean Beacon” workshop at Miltown Malbay Library!

This interactive event uses the beautiful Atlantic sunset as its main inspiration. A cosy art station with safe, battery-operated LED tea-lights and glass holders will be set up for participants to create their own glowing artwork.

With step-by-step guidance, participants will paint their own interpretation of the ocean waves and coastal twilight using quick-drying acrylic glass markers. This is a very accessible technique, so no previous art experience is required. Once complete, an LED tea-light will be placed inside the decorated glass, transforming it into a glowing mini-beacon.

Participants will have the opportunity to add their finished piece to a collective light display in the library before taking it home as a special handmade souvenir.

The workshop runs from 4:00 PM to 7:00 PM, with three sessions taking place at approximately 4:00 PM, 5:00 PM, and 6:00 PM. The first session is particularly suitable for younger children and families.

The event follows a flexible drop-in format, so anyone passing by is welcome to join if a seat is available. Booking online is strongly recommended to secure a place, but visitors are encouraged to drop in and check for availability.

title: The One
description:
The One is a contemporary dance performance about a forgotten saviour whose story has faded with time. As people struggle, they call again on the figure they once believed would save them. Is The One a god, a king, a forgotten hero or simply a symbol of hope? The audience is invited to decide.

The work brings together four young dancers from the Laois Youth Dance Ensemble — Claudia, Hannah, Sheron and Iryna — with three professional performers.

Ramakrishnan Rengarajan, known as Bubblelock, leads the professional ensemble. With more than 20 years of dance practice and over six years of professional performance experience in Ireland, he specialises in hip-hop and locking, alongside Indian and street dance influences.

Suriya Priya is a professional performing artist with 18 years of dance experience and more than eight years of performance experience. She has performed at national and international events and in film, and is trained in hip-hop, Indian classical dance and other styles.

Vidhyutha is a Bharatanatyam dancer with 15 years of experience. Returning to performance after a short break, she brings the depth, discipline and storytelling tradition of Indian classical dance to the work.

Together, the dancers explore memory, struggle, belief and the human need for a saviour, leaving the identity of The One in the hands of the audience.

The tour begins at the entrance to Ringsend and Irishtown Community Centre, where visitors will meet representatives from Codema and the Ringsend and District Historical Society. title: The Ripple Event
description:
This Thing is a group of community artists who have one thing in common, a love for our home of Drogheda. In collaboration with Upstate Theatre Project and Development Perspectives, we invite you to join us for an evening of theatre and discussion as we explore collaborative and positive ways to affect change on a community level.

 

After a year of workshops, our community is excited to share our work with the wider Drogheda network, and hope to spark conversation, so join us in The Little Duke Performance space at 7pm on Culture Night as we create the first ripple that will build in to a wave of change in Drogheda!

 

Audiences can expect traditional theatre performances, as well as a chance to interact and change the scene as they are guided through forum theatre techniques by our experienced team of facilitators and performers. These scenes will explore every day injustices, as well as macro factors that affect day to day life in Drogheda. We hope you come along, be inspired, and stay for the chats afterward!

No booking required, for any further information email tailtiutheatre@gmail.com

Is grúpa pobail é “This Thing”,  d’ealaíontoirí le rud amhain i bpáirt acu – an grá dár mbaile dhúcais Droichead Átha.

Ag obair i bpáirt le Upstate Theatre Project agus Development Perspective, tugaimid cuireadh duit chun tráthnóna lán le drámaíocht agus comhrá a caitheamh linn, nuair a bhrathnaímid ar bheallachaí dearfacha agus comhoibríocha chun athrú a spreagadh ar léibhéal pobail.

 

Tá bliain iomlán caite againn ag obair le chéile i gceardlainne, agus tá ár n-ealaíontóirí ar bís chun ár gcuid oibre a chur i láthair do mhuintir na háite, agus tá súil againn go spreagann an cur i láthair seo comhrá nua i masc ár lucht féachanna. Buail linn sa Little Duke Performance Space ag  7.in ar Oíche Chultúir nuair a cuirimíd tús leis a rabhartha athraithe anseo i nDroichead Átha

 

Beadh an lucht féachanna ag súil le cur i láthair thradisiúnta drámaíochta, chomh maith leis an deis chun an radharc a athrú le linn an cur i láthair, nuair atá siad stiúrtha leis na ceannairí agus aisteoirí le teicníc forum theatre. Breathnóidh na radharcanna ar éagóir sa lá atá inniu ann, chomh maith leis na toisce le tionchar ar an gnáthsaol anseo i nDroichead Átha. Tá fáilte romhat teacht linn, píosa spreagadh a fháill, agus comhrá a dhéanamh linn ar an oíche!

 

Ní gá aon áirithint a dhéanamh, agus más maith leat eolas breise, is féidir ríomhphoist a sheoladh chuig tailtiutheatre@gmail.com

description:

Who decides what to do when nobody knows?

Join a storyteller at the National Leprechaun Museum in a mysterious tale of the unforgiving sea. Based on ‘The Sea Baby’, collected from Pat Sheridan of Gurtheghane, Kilglass, Co. Sligo — The Schools’ Collection, National Folklore Collection, UCD (Vol. 0164, Kilglass NS, 1930s).

 

Image www.brendanatkins.com

title: The Sound of Appalachia in the Liberties
description:
The Dublin Sacred Harp Singers bring the sound of traditional American country-gospel singing to The Liberties this Culture Night.

Familiar from the soundtrack of films such as ‘Cold Mountain’ or ‘Lawless’, Shapenote singing is a truly original American music form. This four-part a cappella music dates from the 16th through the 20th centuries, and is characterised by haunting harmonies, traditional modes, raucous songs, serene hymns, fast fugues, and high-energy anthems. The notation is written in shapes that correspond to degrees of the scale, making it easy to sight-sing. This tradition is democratic and egalitarian.

Come along and join Sacred Harp Singers of Dublin as they glory in the powerful and joyful experience of singing their hearts out together. All voices, both newcomers and beginners, are welcome.

title: The Stonewall Builder – A West Cork Musical
description:
Join singer-songwriter and theatre maker Liz Clark for a special Culture Night presentation of an original piece, The Stonewall Builder, at The Gallery on Heir Island. Part concert, part theatre, The Stonewall Builder weaves original songs, storytelling and live performance to explore identity, belonging, courage and connection across generations. Inspired by Liz’s years-long work as resident musician in community hospitals across West Cork, the piece tells the story of navigating what it means to come out as a gay woman while building a relationship with an older generation whose lives and experiences were often very different. This Culture Night event offers audiences an opportunity to experience the work during its creative residency on Heir Island, where the performers will have spent the last few days rehearsing and refining the show before taking it to other West Cork communities.
This evening will be followed by an informal conversation with the artists about how the work has been developed and how rural communities continue to shape the project. The Stonewall Builder asks universal questions about finding the courage to be yourself and celebrates the surprising conversations that can happen between generations and the way music brings people together. Whether you are interested in music, theatre, storytelling, LGBTQ+ experiences, or simply enjoy hearing original work in a beautiful island setting, everyone is warmly welcome.

title: The Unsung Artists: Exploring the Familiar Stories and Handiwork of Matriarchs
description:
This Culture Night, the Embassy of Mexico in Ireland welcomes visitors to The Unsung Artists, an exhibition by Anne Callanan and guest artist Fernanda Olivares exploring the legacy of female craftspeople through new works inspired by the textile traditions of Ireland and Mexico.

Bringing together contemporary art and traditional craft, the exhibition celebrates the knowledge, resilience, and creativity of women whose skills have been passed down through generations. Inspired by the historic Limerick Lace collection at Limerick Museum, the project reflects on the social history of women whose intricate needlework sustained local economies while often remaining anonymous.

Using paint, charcoal, and textiles, Callanan also weaves in the story of her own grandmother, a lace maker from County Tyrone, whose life embodied both physical labour and exceptional craftsmanship. By placing the craft traditions of Ireland and Mexico in dialogue, the exhibition responds to these histories through a contemporary visual language that explores hidden labour, inheritance, and memory.

title: The Wall of Wonder at Imagination Station
description:
The Wall of Wonder is a collaborative community art project that celebrates intergenerational creativity, imagination and environmental awareness through the transformation of discarded materials into a beautiful public artwork.
Using hundreds of recycled clear cupcake containers donated by local businesses, every participant will create their own miniature artwork inside a transparent display box, filling their container with reclaimed and natural materials such as bottle tops, fabric scraps, buttons, paper, leaves, feathers, shells and other rescued objects, creating a unique “cabinet of curiosity” that reflects their personality, interests and imagination.
Each individual artwork becomes one small piece of a much larger installation. As the containers are assembled together, they form a vibrant and ever-growing Wall of Wonder, demonstrating how many individual contributions can come together to create something extraordinary.
Unlike a traditional exhibition, the installation will remain on permanent display and will continue to grow over time as more children contribute, allowing families to revisit and locate their own child’s artwork for years to come.
On Culture Night, this project will encourage children, parents and grandparents to view everyday waste materials as valuable creative resources while promoting sustainability, creativity, confidence and community pride.
fullAddress: Imagination Station, The Waterways, Osberstown, Sallins, Co. Kildare, Ireland

title: The Weave of Home: A Community Poetry Gathering
description: A participatory poetry event celebrating home, place, and belonging. Community poetry submission will be gathered into a printed booklet, followed by shared readings and a collaborative poetry writing activity that invites everyone to contribute their voice.

title: The Wildwood Flower – An Evening of Storytelling and Song
description:
Join us for a memorable evening as Garage Theatre’s Artists in Residence, acclaimed writer Pat McCabe and singer-songwriter Grainne Duffy, present a newly polished and updated version of The Wildwood Flower. This captivating production stars Grainne Duffy, Aisling McCormilla, Claragh McDermott, and Pat Deery, with a special guest appearance from Pat McCabe himself.

Blending powerful storytelling with live music and guitar, The Wildwood Flower is a beautifully crafted performance that celebrates the richness of local talent, creativity, and artistic collaboration in Monaghan. Don’t miss this unique theatrical experience — an inspiring showcase of music, drama, and community spirit.

A post-show Q&A session with the artists will follow the performance.

title: The Wishing Station
description: At “The Wishing Station” Angela Vaughan presents her artwork “Altar to the Aos Sì” (Fairy Altar) and audience are invited to engage with the work by performing a ribbon tying ritual. As participants tie their ribbon onto the contemporary ‘Fairy’ statue , they are encouraged to silently say a Prayer, ask for a Blessing or Make a Wish . As the night progresses , and with this collective participation, the “Fairy” will be transformed by your wishes and the ribbon adornments . The Fairy altar becomes a symbol for our community working together and Culture Night celebrations. A guest book is also available if you wish to add any comments or reflections. This event is user friendly and suitable for all with the artist on site for the duration.

title: The World through Different Lenses
description: Mallow Camera Club will celebrate its 40th anniversary with a slideshow exhibition featuring images created by members across a wide range of photographic styles and subjects.
fullAddress: Mallow, County Cork, Ireland

title: The Wran
description: Hailing from the Comeragh Mountains of County Waterford, The Wran are four brothers: Tommy, Danny, Seán and Stephen Dunford. They bring a fresh voice to Irish music, blending trad with punk and a hint of psychedelia to create music that feels both timeless and new. Drawing inspiration from Planxty, The Pogues and Lankum, The Wran combines traditional and modern instrumentation, including banjo, harmonium, acoustic guitar, bass VI and drums. They are dedicated to keeping the Irish language, traditional songs and storytelling alive while continuing to push it forward in their own way. After an explosive live debut in 2025, including accoladed performances at Glastonbury, Green Man, All Together Now, and Electric Picnic, the band went on to support The Scratch and Kíla, play Dublin’s Notable NYD festival, and sell out their first Irish tour. Beginning 2026 with a sold-out UK tour, The Wran are fast establishing themselves as one of Ireland’s most vital new bands.
fullAddress: Tawnies Upper, Clonakilty, County Cork, P85 RH95, Ireland

title: There is No Planet B: a Walking Tour of the IFSC in a Time of Climate Breakdown
description:
This Culture Night, Financial Justice Ireland invites visitors to discover a new way of seeing Dublin’s Docklands on a lively walking tour blending protest and performance at the heart of the city’s financial district.

Explore the role of the IFSC in fossil fuel investment, its outsized role contributing to a climate crisis setting the planet ablaze with wildfires, consuming fossil fuels with dirty investments and diverting clean energy into limitless data centre expansion.

A range of speakers will invite attendees to consider how these interconnected crises can be resisted by illuminating pathways toward a just transition that places human flourishing and well-being ahead of profit, growth-at-all-costs economic thinking, and ecological devastation.

Featuring a wide range of brilliant speakers and timely perspectives, this is a tour not to simply attend but to join. Expect to walk, question, and sing!

 

This tour is co-funded by the European Union. Its contents are the sole responsibility of Financial Justice Ireland and do not necessarily reflect the views of the European Union.
fullAddress: James Connolly Memorial, North Wall, Dublin, Ireland

title: Thin Places: Exploring Connections through Music and Art
description:
Join uilleann piper Eoin Dillon, ecological artist Siobhan Madden and artists and creators from across West Wicklow in a very special Culture Night event rooted in the village of Donard

The Wicklow Hills Arts Collective presents this interactive evening of music, history, heritage and visual art that brings participants to the heritage sites of Donard’s graveyard and ogham stone before ending in Donard Community Hall with an evening of music and art. Meet the artists, discover works in the making – and stay for tea after!

The evening, in collaboration with the community in Donard, builds on the Don’t trilogy by Noel Brennan and James Grace, developed over several years with the support of the Dunlavin Arts Festival and culminating in Don’t Look at Me That Way, recipient of the Innovation Award from Wicklow Arts Office and Creative Ireland.

The event will start in Donard Community Hall at 7pm

This event includes both outdoor and indoor elements, with a short guided walk between locations. Please contact wicklowhills@mailbox.org with any queries.

title: This Is Not Nostalgia – The Write Stuff at The James Joyce Centre
description:
This Culture Night, The Write Stuff presents This Is Not Nostalgia, an evening of storytelling, poetry, music, and memory celebrating the people and places that have shaped Dublin’s character.

Following the success of its inaugural Culture Night event in 2025, and a series of collaborations with venues including Chapters Bookstore, The Hendrick Smithfield, The Liberty Market, the James Joyce Centre, Dublin by Dusk, and the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport, The Write Stuff returns with a specially curated programme hosted by Dublin writer Steve O’Toole.

The evening features award-winning storyteller Sinéad O’Brien of Wandering Stories Theatre, singer-songwriter Tony St Ledger, award-winning playwright Frank Shouldice, and iconic Dublin DJ Dandelion. Together, they will present an original blend of stories, poems, and songs, accompanied by a digital backdrop celebrating Dublin’s distinctive people and places.

From Brendan Behan and Bang Bang to Arthur Fields, Pat Ingoldsby, Thom McGinty (The Diceman), Dancing Mary Margaret Dunne, Pat Tierney, and many of the city’s beloved street buskers, This Is Not Nostalgia reflects on a Dublin that has changed, celebrating the characters whose lives continue to shape the cultural memory of the city’s streets.
fullAddress: James Joyce Centre, 35 North Great George's Street, Rotunda, Basement, D01 WK44, Ireland

title: Threads between us
description:
What Threads Us Together is a free community street embroidery gathering on Culture Night, hosted outside LIV Vintage Studio under a canopy on the street from 4pm to 7pm.A large shared cloth is laid out on a communal frame, alongside stamps of Chinese symbols, Ogham marks, spirals and symbols of protection. Passers-by are invited to contribute however they like stamp a symbol, draw freehand, embroider on top, or simply add a knot. Drawing and stitching sit side by side. You choose your own way in. Three community embroiderers will work on the cloth for the full three hours, drawing and stitching continuously — teaching by doing, inspiring by being present. The cloth grows across the evening, mark by mark, stitch by stitch. The simple knot stitch is the anchor technique — the same stitch for everyone.

Is teacht le chéile sráide dírithe ar bhróidnéireacht atá saor in aisce don phobal ar Oíche Chultúir é An Nasc Eadrainn a bheidh ar siúl faoi cheannbhrat ar an tsráid taobh amuigh de Stiúideo Vintage LIV idir 4in agus 7in. Beidh píosa mór éadaigh leagtha ar fhráma comhroinnte agus beidh stampaí ar a mbeidh siombailí de chuid na Síne, marcanna Oghaim, bíseanna agus siombailí cosanta ar fáil. Iarrfar ar na daoine a bheidh ag dul thar bráid cur leis de réir mar is mian leo trí shiombail a chur air, saorlíníocht a dhéanamh air, bróidnéireacht a dhéanamh ar a bharr, nó díreach snaidhm a chur leis. title: Threads of Belonging: Sewing Solidarity Banner Exhibition
description:
Threads of Belonging: Sewing Solidarity Banner Exhibition

Join Donegal Intercultural Platform for a special Culture Night exhibition celebrating the creativity, identity and diversity of communities across County Donegal. The exhibition will showcase a collection of community banners created collaboratively through the PEACEPLUS Sewing Solidarity programme.

Each banner tells a unique story, reflecting the cultures, heritage, experiences and sense of belonging of the people who created it. A photographic display will also document the creative process and the relationships formed during workshops delivered in community centres across Donegal.

Members of the public are warmly invited to view the banners, learn more about the Sewing Solidarity programme and celebrate the creativity, skills and shared experiences of Donegal’s diverse communities.

6.00pm – 10.00pm
fullAddress: Intercultural Platform, St Oliver Plunkett Rd, Letterkenny, County Donegal, Ireland

title: Threads of Creativity
description:
Join us for an evening celebrating sustainable textiles and prints, showcasing the skills and creative processes developed during our nine-week summer workshop series at The Dock.

Enjoy three interactive textile demonstrations and explore an exhibition highlighting the work created throughout the programme.

Master craft maker Annie Gambrill will demonstrate traditional spinning on a restored antique spinning wheel. Participants can experience spinning their own wool and learn about Annie’s passion for locally sourced fibre, from fleece to finished cloth, and her commitment to preserving traditional textile skills. Felt artist Belinda Reid will demonstrate how to create 3D needle-felted flower pots using wire, a special barbed needle and 100% wool.

Participants aged 18+ can try this delicate and creative technique while discovering the versatility and beauty of felt.

Professional feltmaker Karen Bowden will demonstrate wet felting, creating flowers and beads using merino wool, water and friction. Karen will also showcase different types of wool and explain their suitability for wet felting. Children aged 8+ can join in the flowery fun!

Meet the artists, discover traditional techniques with a contemporary twist, and celebrate creativity, sustainability and the rich possibilities of wool.
fullAddress: The Leitrim Design House, St George's Terrace, Townparks, Carrick-On-Shannon, County Leitrim, N41 T2X2, Ireland

title: Threads of Culture
description:
Step into a vibrant celebration of colour, creativity and culture at Threads of Culture, a free Culture Night event showcasing the artistry and heritage of African fashion. Discover the beauty and stories behind traditional and contemporary African clothing as local designers and community models take to the catwalk in a lively fashion showcase. Browse displays of stunning African fabrics, meet local textile vendors and learn how fashion reflects identity, history and cultural expression across the African continent.

Explore the creative world of sustainable fashion through demonstrations of clothing upcycling and fabric repurposing, highlighting how textiles can be given a new life while reducing waste. Whether you’re a fashion enthusiast, interested in sustainability or simply curious to experience something new, there will be plenty to inspire visitors of all ages.

Throughout the evening, enjoy a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere with a live DJ playing an uplifting mix of African and world music, creating the perfect soundtrack for this unique cultural experience. Light refreshments will be available, offering an opportunity to meet designers, makers and members of Longford’s diverse communities.

Join us for an unforgettable evening that celebrates creativity, cultural diversity and community. Threads of Culture invites everyone to experience the richness of African fashion and discover how art, culture and sustainability can bring people together through shared stories, style and inspiration.

Téigh isteach i gceiliúradh geal dathanna, cruthaitheachta agus cultúir ag Threads of Culture, ócáid Culture Night saor in aisce a léiríonn ealaín agus oidhreacht faisin Afraice. Faigh amach áilleacht agus scéalta na bhféilte traidisiúnta agus comhaimseartha Afracach agus de réir mar a ghlacann dearthóirí áitiúla agus samhlacha pobail páirte sa rian faisin beo. Trí oíche, bain sult as atmaisféar socair fáilteach le DJ beo ag seinm meascán spreagúil de cheol Afraiceach agus ceol domhanda, ag cruthú an fhuaimchlár foirfe don taithí chultúrtha uathúil seo. title: Threads of Heritage: Traveller Craft, Story & Making
description:
The event celebrates Traveller cultural heritage through craft, storytelling, design, and community-led creative practice.

The public are invited into Shuttleknit’s working creative space for an afternoon of live demonstrations, informal talks, exhibitions, and hands-on participation led by Traveller women makers. Activities will include knitting and textile demonstrations, storytelling, heritage displays, workshops, and a showcase of culturally informed knitwear and homeware collections developed through Shuttleknit’s social enterprise model.

The event explores heritage as a living and evolving practice carried through memory, oral tradition, creativity, and intergenerational knowledge-sharing.

Visitors will have opportunities to engage directly with makers, contribute to a collaborative textile or storytelling artwork, and learn about Traveller identity and indigenous cultural expression through accessible cultural experiences.
fullAddress: Shuttle Knit, Crinion Park, Corporation Lands, Wicklow, Ireland

title: Threads through time: Discovering Limerick Lace
description:
Step into the intricate world of Limerick lace guided by Friends of Lace Limerick at this special Culture Night pop-up exhibition. Explore a beautiful collection of antique and contemporary lace pieces, with a particular focus on Limerick lace, alongside examples of Carrickmacross, Borris, Headford and Clones lace traditions.
Discover how lace continues to inspire creativity through innovative textile repair techniques, and gain insight into the skill, artistry and heritage behind these remarkable handcrafted works.
Visitors can also take part in one of two interactive Limerick lace demonstration sessions at 6:00 PM and 7:00 PM, featuring hands-on opportunities to try traditional lace stitches for themselves. Each session is limited to 10 participants. Admission is free, but advance booking is essential.
Whether you’re curious, creative, or simply captivated by fine handwork, join us and thread your way through Limerick’s lace legacy—one stitch at a time.
