title: Three Potters, Three Styles: The Stories and Styles of Three Local Potters
description: Embody the spirit of Culture Night by demystifying the craft of Irish pottery. This event offers an intimate, behind-the-scenes look into the inspirations and techniques of the work of three local potters; Cora Cummins, Amanda Murphy and Jackie Dee. While bound by friendship and a shared passion for clay, their artistic journeys are very different. This event gives the audience a glimpse into the day to day life of working as a small scale potter in Ireland today, while also getting to see three very different sources of inspiration and making techniques of their very distinct ranges.
fullAddress: Main Street, Villierstown, Co. Waterford, Ireland

title: Three Ways of Seeing
description:
Opening reception for an exciting group exhibition of recent paintings by artists Noelle Angley, Josephine Boland, and Vanya Savov.

The different personalities and backgrounds of each artist make for a lively contrast of influences, styles and interpretations of the rich cultural heritages of Ireland and the Balkans. Paintings range from expressive, atmospheric, neo-impressionistic interpretations to more stylistic and representational work.

With professional careers in architecture and education Noelle and Josephine both share a passion for plein air painting, their work demonstrating a great love of the outdoors and Ireland’s stunning landscapes. Vanya, with a background in psychology, is by contrast a studio painter, and her highly expressive works are often gestural and emotional responses to a scene.

The exhibition will be introduced by the award-winning artist Trish Findlater, performing the opening ceremony on Culture Night, Friday 18th of September, 7pm-8.30pm.  All are welcome. The Three Ways of Seeing exhibition will continue through Sunday 27th September open daily 11am-6pm.

This opening will be followed by Jazz by the wonderful ‘Small Floor Trio’ from 9pm in the same venue – a free walk-in event with musicians Paul O’Driscoll, Eanna Ryder and Andy O’Farrell.

These events in the KAVA Courthouse are just two of the many free events which will be happening during Culture Night as part of the Kinvara Art and Culture Trail – details available on www.kinvaramusic.com, www.kava.ie and www.kinvarapleinair.ie
fullAddress: Kinvarra, County Galway, H91 K5T9, Ireland

title: THRESHOLD: A Curated Digital Art Exhibition
description:
Experience a curated exhibition of contemporary digital art presented across the Market House campus. Throughout the evening, digital screens and large-scale projections will transform the site into a dynamic exhibition space, showcasing selected works from an open call featuring artists from across Ireland and beyond.

As part of its 200th anniversary celebrations, Market House Dunleer is delighted to present its first Culture Night event. THRESHOLD opens Culture Night with an exhibition bringing together 15 artists to explore the spaces, ideas and possibilities that exist between us. We are excited to share this special evening of art, culture and conversation with the public.

Curated by Adrian+Shane, alongside Els Bogart and Declan Kelly, the exhibition features a diverse range of moving image, digital and screen-based artworks.

Visitors are invited to explore the Market House campus, discover the artworks at their own pace, and experience contemporary art in an accessible and engaging public setting as part of Culture Night.

title: Through A Charcoal Lens
description:
The exhibition ‘Through a Charcoal Lens | an Spéir ARK and its Native Plants’ by environmental artist Jen Castle will be taking place from Monday 7th to Saturday 19th September in the Mayfair Library, Kilkenny.

To celebrate Culture Night Kilkenny on Friday 18th September, there will be a participatory ‘drop-in’ event taking place in the exhibition space. During the evening, visitors of all ages and abilities will be invited to engage with the exhibition through a hands-on charcoal drawing workshop inspired by the charcoal and egg tempera artworks of plants on display.

Participants will work from freshly gathered plants and flowers sourced from the re-wilded land of an Spéir ARK, while experiencing an original soundscape created from field recordings made on-site by guest musician Kate Powell.

During the evening of Culture Night, Kate Powell will perform live alongside the soundscape installation.

Light refreshments will be provided.

title: Through Our Eyes
description:
Friends of Kilconly Wetlands presents ‘Through Our Eyes’, a celebration of our community art collective, Bog Fam. Over the last year, the members of Bog Fam have been exploring their relationship to Cloonbar Bog with artist facilitator Sarah Deane. Together they have walked the bog with their cameras, finding new ways to see a landscape they thought they already knew.
‘Through Our Eyes’ is an exhibition of this work and includes photographs, words, installation and moving image.
Visitors are invited to contribute by sharing their own connections and perspectives of the bog as part of the evening
through our interactive space.
Whether you grew up with the bog or are only getting to know it, we invite the people of Kilconly and beyond to come and share Culture Night with us.

title: Tigh Maighne Rhythms + Vibes
description:
Join Rhythms + Vibes at Tigh Maighne: an interactive music, culture and presentation exploring traditional and indigenous instruments, including the didgeridoo, jew harp, different drums and a variety of sound healing instruments/tools.

The session will introduce participants to the history, cultural significance and unique sounds of each instrument through live demonstrations and audience participation.

Advanced classes available at the end of session.
fullAddress: Tigh Maighne, Moynetemple, Moyne, County Tipperary, Ireland

title: Tiny Mutiny x BROEI
description:
Tiny Mutiny x BROEI is a free and family friendly Culture Night event at The Mall Theatre, Tuam showcasing original work by creative teenagers and young people from Galway County and Fryslân, The Netherlands.

Both Tiny Mutiny and BROEI are youth-led arts projects that give teenagers and young people support to bring their creative ideas to life and to an audience. Expect amazing art, panel discussions, performances, screenings, and plenty of chances for audiences to ask questions!

Tiny Mutiny 2026 Project Award artists are: Alannah Caddye (literature), Lauren Caine (film), Liam O’Connor (music) and Harlow Slattery Madden (sculpture). Tiny Mutiny 2026 First Sparks Bursary artists are: Abigale Heavey (poetry), Lainey Tighe and Lia Mae Coen (illustration).

BROEI artists are: Jennisja Palstra (music), Laura van der Heide (poetry), Lise Sophia Bijma (music), Ramlo Huseen (theatre), Roy Heitbrink (podcast) and Sander Van Den Bogert (film).

Tiny Mutiny 2026 is commissioned by Galway County Arts Office in partnership with Sparkcatchers!. This Culture Night event is supported by Arts Council, BROEI, Creative Ireland, Culture Programme for Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union 2026, Galway County Council and produced by Sparkcatchers!.

Artists from Tiny Mutiny, BROEI and Sparkcatchers! Creative Youth Committee will network and take part in a series of workshops the following day exploring artistic connections and shared interests.
fullAddress: The Mall Theatre and Arts Centre, Stable Lane, Townparks (2nd Division), Tuam, County Galway, Ireland

title: Tiny Theatre
description:
Join Kilkenny’s ‘Bare Bones’ playwriting group for a Culture Night series of 3 x 10 minute short plays, interspaced with 3 x 10 minute interviews with the playwrights.

This ‘Tiny Theatre’ event will present an audience of 30-40 people, with a set of three site-specific plays, stripped back to their ‘bares bones’, as performed by two actors.

Each play will be Interspaced by a short interview with it’s writer, to give Culture Night Audiences, and anyone interested in playwrighting, a ‘behind the scenes’ view into the creative process of each play, and a ‘sneak peek’ into the process of short play making in Kilkenny.

Set in the unique location of The Drawing Room at the Clubhouse Hotel, the tiny theatre audience of 30-40 people will be seated beside the action, to experience these ‘Bare Bones’ short plays; and the relationship between creators, creating and audience.

The Drawing Room at The Club House Hotel, 22 & 23 Lower Patrick Street, Kilkenny. Eircode:  R95 PX68

title: Tipperary in Song and Story with Derek Ryan
description:
A premier cultural evening of music, poetry, and storytelling led by Tipperary’s own proud “Premier Man” and internationally acclaimed performer, Derek Ryan.

This event explores the rich historical tapestry of Tipperary. The performance weaves together pivotal historical narratives – ranging from the March of the Ulster men through Clonoulty and the Battle of Kinsale, to local folklore regarding St. Patrick’s historic visit to the Rock of Cashel and the stories of Brian Boru of Killaloe. It even touches on modern cultural crossovers, such as Johnny Cash and his Tipperary girl.

Musical Repertoire: The evening features rousing, poignant renditions of iconic local and national ballads, including Slievenamon, Forty Shades of Green, Sweet Aherlow, The Galtee Mountain Boy, Off To Philadelphia, and Leaving Tipperary. Derek will also pay special tribute to Mary Cummins’s SianseSuire, reminiscing on his time with the original cast at the Milwaukee Irish Fest.

Over four decades, the branch has nurtured generations of talent, achieving top honours at County, Provincial, and All-Ireland Fleadhanna Cheoil across solo, duet, trio, céilí band, and grúpaí cheoil competitions. Mitchelstown welcomes the return the Gaelic Traditional Games interactive display for Culture night 2026!

Emerald Isle’s Iconic game ~ Fastest field game on the grass played over 3,000 years and inspired by the warrior Cú Chulainn. Long Puckers invited.

2. 56 lb / 28 lb / 5 lb WEIGHT FOR DISTANCE

A true test of brawn and strength.

3. Risqué POLE HOPPING over Ditches.

Balance, bravery and banter.

Experience how rural people crossed ditches in pre-road Ireland and how invaders crossed Norman castle moates.

4. Scintillating SKITTLES

Precision, skill and plenty of laughs

5. Wobbly WELLY-BOOT Throwing

Fun for all abilities – measured by distance.

6.Rustic ROAD BOWLING

Hurling 28-oz metal bowl on rural roads

Speed, strategy and competitive spirit – measuring tape decides

7. Wheel pulling

Rural Ireland meets relay madness

8.Rustic HORSESHOE Throwing

Accuracy, heritage and friendly rivalry.

9. Tracing of Sporting HEROES / SCOUNDRELS via Irish Family Search.

Ideal For Sport-mad, Like-minded Humans

title: Traditions & Their Transformations
description:
This Culture Night, visit the Embassy of Bulgaria to explore the ancient tradition of Kukeri through exhibitions, photography, an artist talk, and a live performance celebrating ritual, transformation, and cultural heritage.

Kukeri is an ancient winter ritual in which participants wear elaborate masks and costumes made of fur, feathers, and other natural materials. Historians trace its origins to Thracian times. The ritual symbolizes the death of winter and the rebirth of nature in spring, expressing the eternal cycle of renewal and fertility.

Dr. Niki Collier presents her solo exhibition, “Monsters and Me,” inspired by a year-long exploration of festivals celebrating fear, loss, and transformation. Drawing on research into Bulgarian Kukeri and Welsh and Irish Mummers traditions, the exhibition features costumes, masks, and puppets exploring identity, ritual, and collective memory. The program also includes a live performance and an artist talk. A Dublin-based multidisciplinary visual artist, educator, and designer, Dr. Collier is internationally recognized for her innovative fiber art, large-scale installations, and socially engaged practice.

Photographer Diana Dimitrova presents an outdoor exhibition at the Embassy of Bulgaria in Dublin, capturing the spirit of the Kukeri tradition. Featuring images from Bulgaria’s renowned Surova in Pernik (inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity) and Starchevata in Razlog festivals, her work reveals the mystery, energy, and cultural richness of this centuries-old ritual.

 

This event is part of the European Culture Trail – a EUNIC Ireland (European Union National Institutes for Culture) in cooperation with the European Commission Representation in Ireland. title: Trails & Tales at Ligoniel
description:
“Join the Ligoniel Improvement Association for a vibrant, two-part celebration of heritage, nature, and community in the heart of North Belfast. Running from 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM, “”Trails and Tales at Ligoniel”” offers an escape into local history and a welcoming space to connect.

The evening begins at 4:00 PM making the most of the late afternoon light with a guided walk around the beautiful, historic Ligoniel Dams. Led by knowledgeable local guides, this accessible outdoor trail will immerse visitors in the rich Celtic folklore and environmental heritage of the area. It is a brilliant opportunity for families and visitors to experience the natural landscape right on the city’s doorstep.

At 5:30 PM, as the autumn evening draws in, the event moves indoors to the warmth of the fully accessible Wolfhill Centre. The second half of the night operates on a relaxed, drop-in basis until 9:00 PM. Visitors will be welcomed with hot food prepared in our community kitchen and treated to an evening of traditional live music and cultural celebration.

Whether you are walking the trails from the very start or simply hopping off the bus at our front door later in the evening for some tunes and a warm meal, this is a completely free, family-friendly event designed to bring people together and showcase the very best of Ligoniel.”

title: TRANSITION: Exhibition – Irish Peatlands in a Changing Climate
description:

Rooted in the Midlands, the exhibition unfolds through an evocative A–Z sequence of photographs from the book TRANSITION, capturing peatlands at a pivotal moment of environmental and cultural change.

Set within one of Birr Castle Demesne’s historic gallery spaces, the exhibition connects with the site’s legacy of science, engineering and discovery. Visitors of all ages are invited to explore this layered story, with a fun A–Z scavenger hunt providing an interactive element for families and younger audiences.

Join us for this free Culture Night event and experience a unique artistic perspective on where we have come from and where we are going.

description:
This Culture Night, Pavee Point welcomes acclaimed Scottish Traveller writer and storyteller Jess Smith for a special evening of storytelling celebrating Traveller culture and oral tradition.

Inspired by a lifelong commitment to preserving her community’s stories, Jess has written extensively about Traveller life and growing up in Scotland. “Humanity is in the story and the story lives through humanity”, she says. “The story is a living element between the storyteller and the listener,” she says. “If the teller has been good at sharing that story, the listener will share it and [the story] doesn’t die.” Help us to keep the stories alive with Jess at Pavee Point this Culture Night.

title: Travelling Light – Eóin Heaney
description: Join artist and filmmaker Eóin Heaney for the premiere of Travelling Light, a new hybrid documentary. Presented within the atmospheric setting of St. Mona’s Church on Sherkin Island, the film explores migration, ecology, perception, and resilience through the interconnected lives of island communities, wildlife, and the surrounding Atlantic Ocean. Blending documentary, observation, and poetic imagery, Travelling Light reflects on the visible and invisible forces that shape island life, from seasonal movements of birds and marine life to the memories, traditions, and lived experiences of those who call the islands home. The film will screen continuously from 5.00pm until 10.00pm, allowing visitors to arrive and depart at any time throughout the evening. The church will be softly darkened so that the moving image becomes the primary source of light, with vivid colour sequences illuminating the historic interior and creating an immersive viewing experience. Eóin Heaney will be present throughout the evening and welcomes visitors to discuss the project, its development, and the stories and ideas that inspired the film. This work has been created as part of the Ocean & Environment project supported by Creative Places West Cork Isalnds.

title: Trí Shráideanna Chlár Chlainne Mhuiris | Through The Streets of Claremorris 1900-1925
description:
Claremorris Historical Society will host a special double event in Claremorris Town Hall on Culture Night 2026, which takes place on Friday 18th September.

From 4.30 to 7.30 the images featured in its recent presentation entitled ‘Through the streets of Claremorris 1900-1925’ will be on exhibition in the Town Hall Studio.

This exhibition marks the recent publication of the 1926 Census allowing the viewer  to step back in time and experience life in Claremorris as it was in the first quarter of the twentieth century, just before the census was taken.

This will be followed at 7.45 in the main hall by an illustrated talk entitled ‘Images of Claremorris 1926-1960’. For this special bilingual event dozens of photographs of people, shops and streetscapes from the Main Street Gathering archives have been carefully restored in full colour by Andrew Newman. Local historian Colmán Ó Raghallaigh will present the fascinating stories behind each of them.

Cuirfidh Cumann Staire Chlár Chlainne Mhuiris ócáid dhúbailte speisialta ar fáil don phobal i Halla Baile Chlár Chlainne Mhuiris ar Oíche Chultúir 2026, Dé hAoine, an 18 Meán Fómhair.

Idir 4.30 agus 7.30, beidh na híomhánna a cuireadh i láthair le déanaí, dar teideal ‘Trí shráideanna Chlár Chlainne Mhuiris 1900-1925’, ar taispeáint i Stiúideo an Halla Baile.

Tá an taispeántas seo á reáchtáil chun foilsiú dhaonáireamh na bliana 1926 a chomóradh. Tig leat dul siar sa stair agus blaiseadh den saol i gClár Chlainne Mhuiris mar a bhí sé sa chéad ráithe den fhichiú haois, díreach sula ndearnadh an daonáireamh.

Ina dhiaidh sin, ar 7.45 sa phríomh halla, tabharfar caint léirithe dar teideal ‘Íomhánna de Chlár Chlainne Mhuiris 1926-1960’. Don ócáid speisialta dátheangach seo, tá athchóiriú lándaite déanta ag Andrew Newman ar 65 ghrianghraf de dhaoine, de shiopaí agus de radharcanna sráide ó chartlann an ‘Main Street Gathering’. Cuirfidh an staraí áitiúil Colmán Ó Raghallaigh na scéalta suimiúla a bhaineann le gach ceann acu i láthair.

Beidh cead isteach saor in aisce agus fáilte roimh chách.

title: Triskel Arts Centre: Irish Baroque Orchestra: Handel’s Band Off Duty
description:
A shamelessly entertaining evening of great tunes from 18th century Ireland and beyond.

What if Handel’s Band took a night off?
For this performance, the Irish Baroque Orchestra will move away from the traditional recital format. Instead, we are creating an immersive, high-energy session that imagines the music Handel and his contemporaries would have heard in the informal
settings of the 1740s – where Baroque virtuosity met the living Irish traditional music of the day.

This programme imagines the musical influences in Dublin during Handel’s stay and draws together works by Handel alongside traditional Irish music.

Curated by Cork’s Marja Gaynor with uilleann piper David Power, nine specialist musicians, including soprano Aisling Kenny, will perform in Triskel for Culture Night 2026, creating a vibrant salon atmosphere. Handel’s Band Off-Duty is about stripping
away the formal veneer of the modern concert hall to reveal the vibrant, social music that animated 18th-century Ireland.

The IBO will also perform this programme in venues in Kerry and Dublin.

Marja Gaynor, director
David Power, uilleann pipes
Aisling Kenny, soprano

Tickets will be released at 10am on Friday 18 September 2026.

title: Trust Artists Unconditionally – Public Art of 1990’s Waterford
description:
Trust Artists Unconditionally’ is an exhibition that explores the innovation of a series of flagship public art commissions initiated by Garter Lane Arts Centre and artist Garrett Phelan between 1995 and 1999. On streets, in football fields, a library and newspapers, artworks appeared without announcement or explanation – rather, they intervened into, confronted and contributed to the everyday life of the city. Phelan, alongside then Garter Lane director Annette Clancy, gave no title to the programme or identified any of the events or encounters that occurred explicitly as art. Bypassing established ways in which art typically appears in public and embracing unconventional approaches and risk taking, the impact of these artworks three decades on still seem revelatory, with an abiding belief in artists to act and find new ways to critique, celebrate and investigate society. ‘Trust Artists Unconditionally’ features contributions from each of the 6 artists involved in the programme, alongside documents unearthed from Garter Lane’s archives.
There will be a discussion & exhibition walkthrough at 6pm followed by official opening at 7pm with Sean Lynch, curator.

title: Tullyfin at Athlone Little Theatre
description:

Rooted in Celtic mythology and folklore, the script follows Ali and her mother Evelyn as they return home to Evelyn’s birthplace; the fictional island of Tullyfin. Rooted in a dynamically-performed fictional narrative, the show is a thematic exploration of island life, familial lines, secrets and the complexities of biological inheritance and adoption. title: Two Short Films about Love and Friendship
description:
This Culture Night, the Irish Film Institute presents two short films exploring the experience of people with intellectual and physical disabilities as they find love and friendship.

 

GRACE

Grace is a poignant coming-of-age drama centred on a woman in her late 20s with Down Syndrome, navigating the complexities of adulthood, independence and first love. When Grace pushes the boundaries set for her, the consequences ripple through her carefully managed world.

Directed by Anna Rodgers/ 26 mins / 2025

 

THE WATER BOYS

Jim and Gary have served as the water boys for their local hurling team, Carrickshock Kilkenny, for over 40 years. Both men have cerebral palsy, but they do not allow their condition to stand in the way of their participation in the hurling team that both their fathers played for. This sensitive and charming documentary explores the daily routines of both men and their unbreakable commitment to their team and their community.

Places are limited, so register in advance to secure your spot!

 

All attendants under 18 must be accompanied by an adult at all times.
Attendants must arrive within 20 minutes of their allocated slot or their space will be allocated to someone else.
There will be no food or drinks available. However some of the activities will be in a room that is used for food production so please be aware of this if you have any severe food allergies.

title: U2 Dublin Walking Tour by Around Ireland – 50th Anniversary
description:

Starting at the Gaiety Theatre, the tour takes in key locations including the former Dandelion Market, Trinity College and Hanover Quay, where U2 continue to record their music. Along the way, discover how Dublin influenced the band and how U2, in turn, left their mark on the city.

The tour also explores fascinating historical and cultural stories from Dublin’s past, offering a broader look at the city alongside U2’s story.

title: Urban Sketching in Glaslough
description:

Participants are invited to explore the village and create their own sketches of the buildings, streets and surrounding scenery. People are welcome to bring your own sketching materials, and there will also be some simple materials available for anyone who would like to come along and have a go.

The emphasis is on participation rather than instruction — there is no pressure to produce a finished artwork or to have any previous experience. It is simply an opportunity to slow down, look at the village in a different way, enjoy being creative outdoors and meet others who enjoy drawing and art.

The end of the sketching session, will culminate in a small open-air exhibition, with participants invited to peg up their sketches for an informal show-and-tell, investigate each others work, chat and enjoy the opportunity to connect with other artists and sketchers.

title: View Boyle Civic Art Collection / King House
description:
Boyle Civic Art Collection

Culture Night provides an opportunity to view the Boyle Civic Art Collection that is on view in King House. The 2024-2026 Exhibition at King House presents 90 pieces of painting and sculpture, showcasing a broad range of media and the best of contemporary Irish artists, capturing the essence of the Boyle Civic Art Collection. It includes the first two pieces acquired in 1990 from artists Joe Hanley and John Moore – exhibited in the Main Salon on the first floor.

Founded in 1990, the Boyle Civic Art Collection, totaling over 300 pieces of contemporary Irish artworks, is one of the most prominent civic art collections in the country. The majority of works were acquired using the sales commission earned at Boyle Arts Festival Exhibitions 1990 to 2012. Several pieces were donated by the Haverty Trust, Friends of the National Collections of Ireland, The Contemporary Irish Art Society and the artists themselves. A number of pieces were also donated by private collectors.

The Collection is maintained by the trustees for the people of Boyle and, thanks to Roscommon County Council, is housed mainly in King House where the collection is managed for exhibition and storage. Other works are located in multiple buildings in the town of Boyle.
fullAddress: King House Interpretive Galleries & Museum, Military Road, Knocknashee, Boyle, County Roscommon, Ireland

title: Waterside Together: Outdoor Screenings
description:
On Culture Night, join Waterside Together and Eastside Cinema from 7–9pm for our third and final outdoor cinema screening at Woodburn Urban Park.

For this final screening, we’ll showcase short films by Roberta Cantow and Buster Keaton, alongside a miniature short film created by local children from Top of the Hill and Lincoln Courts.

The children’s film is the result of a workshop delivered in spring 2025, inspired by archival footage of the Waterside from the NI Screen collection. Participants explored the sounds of the past, using found and everyday materials to recreate the noises heard in the historic footage. The result is a playful new interpretation of the Waterside’s history, created by children who live in the area today.

Waterside Together is a PEACEPLUS Shared Green Spaces project that brings together members of the Protestant, Catholic and BAME communities in the Waterside, creating opportunities for people to connect, participate and share outdoor spaces. Through a programme of events and activities, the project aims to reanimate these spaces as places where everyone can feel welcome and where communities can come together.

Woodburn Urban Park sits at a meeting point between communities. It is a place where people walk their dogs, go for a run, take a shortcut or simply pass through on their way somewhere else. Over the past year, Waterside Together has been developing activities in the park that encourage people to stop, stay and experience the space together.

Our outdoor cinema screenings with Eastside Cinema and Excite offer another way of doing just that. By bringing people together to watch films outdoors, the screenings invite us to think about what it means to live in a community, to share a place, and to share the histories that have shaped it.

 

The screening will take place under a marquee, so there’s no need to worry about the September weather! We’ll have blankets available to get cosy, along with popcorn to enjoy during the films. Come along, settle in and join us under the marquee for an evening of film, community and local history.

Waterside Together is kindly funded by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by SEUPB (Special EU Programmes Body).

 

Eastside Cinema is a community film initiative sharing diverse stories and perspectives through screenings.

 

Excite is a community multi-media programme for young people in the Waterside.

 

More details about the films:

Roberta Cantow’s Clothelines (1981)

Clothes flapping in the wind, a soft polyphony of voices. Clotheslines are a physical and metaphorical thread of a shared history: communication between women, households, streets, families, and generations; the signs given by different articles of clothing, the chatter across the fence or through the window.

Buster Keaton’s Neighbors (1920)

Under a shared clothesline, two families are divided by a single wooden fence. Around this fence, ladders, laundry, and bodies collide, exposing the arbitrary nature of physical boundaries and their disproportionate influence on social relationships.

In Buster Keaton’s One Week (1920)

A newlywed couple’s self-assembled house is undone by an escalating series of forces: malice, accident, nature, and industry itself. A progression that exposes the false promise of autonomous domestic construction.

title: We Make The City
description:
This Culture Night, Segotia invites visitors to imagine a different Dublin through a communal pottery experience, live music, and the closing night of Rich Gilligan’s exhibition, Earth Tourist.

What if we had the power to recreate our city exactly as we wanted? Imagine rebuilding Dublin one stone, one brick, one tree at a time. Tatiana Smith-St Kitts of Folly Design Studio will facilitate a communal pottery experience that invites participants to imagine, shape, and build a city together.

One long table in the centre of the room starts empty as a blank slate, inviting participants to contribute a small clay object representing something they love that belongs in their ideal Dublin cityscape. Over the evening, each piece made by participants will be added to the table gradually creating a vibrant miniature city.

Children and adults entering the space can join the activity at any time and the installation evolves organically as more people arrive. By the end of the night, guests will have moulded a utopian city together.

Music will be provided by local dj BLKCVNS in Segotia’s garden, along with a special DJ set from photographer Rich Gilligan, guiding guests through the space and supplying the sonic backdrop for making, gathering and dancing amongst friendly faces old and new as the collective city takes shape.

A powerful Culture Night event celebrating the creativity, courage and resilience of survivors of sexual violence, inspired by stories shared through WeSpeak.ie, an anonymous online community where survivors can share their story, messages of healing and messages of hope in their own words, in their own time.

Survivors have taken part in a series of creative workshops exploring storytelling, poetry, art and songwriting, recognising that we all share our stories in different ways.

Throughout the day, visitors can explore a gallery of the written, visual and multimedia works created during these workshops and contribute their own “Line of Hope” to a growing community scroll, creating a collective message of solidarity, empathy, and support.

In the evening, the exhibition comes to life with a special live performance, creating a moving celebration of healing, hope and the power of creative expression.

title: Where History Met in Secret: 3 Mountjoy Square and the First Dáil
description:
Discover one of Dublin’s most remarkable hidden historic houses as 3 Mountjoy Square opens its doors for Culture Night 2026. Behind its elegant Georgian façade lies a building that played a pivotal role in Ireland’s journey to independence.

Owned by Walter Cole, a close associate of Arthur Griffith, No. 3 became a discreet meeting place for the leaders of the independence movement. Following the suppression of the First Dáil in 1919, the house hosted secret meetings of Dáil Éireann, with key figures including Michael Collins, Arthur Griffith, and other revolutionary leaders gathering here to shape the future of the nation.
The house offers a rare opportunity to experience both the beauty of Georgian Dublin and the stories of courage, vision and determination that unfolded within its walls.

Join the Dublin Adult Learning Centre this Culture Night and uncover the extraordinary history hidden behind one of Dublin’s finest Georgian doors.

Every city is built on stories. Some are passed down through generations, while others arrive with people who have made Belfast their home from different parts of the world. Through a facilitated conversation and live storytelling, local residents and members of the Indian community will share personal experiences, cultural traditions, and memories that reveal the many ways we connect with our city.

From childhood recollections and family customs to migration journeys and neighbourhood experiences, this event will uncover the hidden stories that shape Belfast’s cultural identity. Audiences will be encouraged to reflect on how culture influences belonging, community, and our understanding of home.

In the spirit of A City Explorer, participants will embark on a journey through Belfast’s diverse voices, discovering the city not through maps and landmarks, but through the people and stories that bring it to life.

title: Where the Slaney Remembers
description:

The short film is a reflective and evocative journey into Wexford’s past, told through the eyes and voices of its people. Produced by Alan Boland and Chris Hayes from Crannog Media in conjunction with Archaeologist Barry Lacey of Slaneyside Heritage this production follows the Slaney from Bunclody to Scarawalsh bridge meeting locals who tell us about the stories, incidents and people from the past along its banks.
This documentary is not a recounting of major historical events. Instead, it is a collection of personal stories passed down through generations exploring how these inherited memories help us understand the very local experience of history. By listening to these voices, viewers are invited to connect with the past in a way that feels intimate
and immediate.
The film is approx 25 minutes and the screening will be followed by an informal Q & A.

title: Who/What/Why a DJ? – A Vinyl History of the Dancefloor.
description:
Join us this Culture Night for a journey tracing the roots of dance music & club culture.

Four local selectors, each with a unique short set, featuring a 3-minute introduction tracking a major musical evolution:

1. The Dub Revolution

Discover how 1970s Jamaican sound system culture invented the “remix”with dub laden b-sides.

2. Disco Origins to the Masterpiece

The dancefloor shift from the massive live orchestras of the mid-70s to the reveal of a fully synthetic 1977 masterpiece that changed music forever.

3. Post-Punk to Synth-Pop (1979–1982)

The flashpoint where youth subcultures traded guitars for drum machines and synthesizers.

4. The History of House

Mapping the mid-1980s Chicago warehouse culture that took electronic energy and built the blueprint for modern clubbing today.

Strictly vinyl, Strictly standard-setting tracks. Drop in, listen to the history, and stay for the dance!

title: Wood Quay Amphitheatre: Aleon
description:
Dublin-born professional Bboy Leon, known by his stage name Aleon, has made a significant mark on the international breaking scene with his distinctive style and dynamic floorwork. Competing globally since 2009, he has represented Ireland at the highest level, taking part in hundreds of international events, multiple world finals, and winning 31 international battles.

Aleon made history as the first Irish Bboy to qualify for an Olympic qualifier and is a five-time National Irish Olympic Champion. He has won the Red Bull BC One Irish National Qualifiers for the past two years, reached the World Finals Top 16 last year, and will represent Ireland again in Toronto this year. He has won 31 international battles and was a finalist at the prestigious UK Bboy Champs World Finals.

Beyond competition, Aleon works across commercials, performances, collaborations, and teaching, having partnered with brands including Google, Nike, JD Sports, Adidas, and Lifestyle Sports. He has also performed alongside major artists including The Black Eyed Peas and Rudimental and is currently supported by Guinness.

An experienced teacher and mentor, Aleon’s background in ballet has influenced his distinctive approach to movement and teaching. He works with dancers of all levels and regularly teaches classes and workshops across Ireland. His commitment to developing the next generation of dancers includes work with Team Ireland on a training programme that reached more than 120,000 students and 4,000 teachers.

Through competition, performance, and education, Aleon continues to inspire dancers and help shape the future of breaking in Ireland.

Through ritual dance, ceremonial attire, and ancestral instruments, the group brings stories, traditions, and spiritual practices passed down through generations to new audiences. The name Mictlan reflects the group’s connection with ancestors and the spiritual journey at the heart of Mexica cosmology. As a calpulli, meaning “great house” or “community”, the group provides a space for learning, cultural exchange, and collective practice.

title: Wood Quay Amphitheatre: St James Street Brass & Reed Band
description:
Founded in 1800, St James’s Brass and Reed Band is Ireland’s oldest band, with early records dating back to 1737. Based in Mount Brown, Dublin 8, the band has played a remarkable role in the city’s history, performing at events associated with figures including Daniel O’Connell and Charles Stewart Parnell, and at the funerals of Michael Collins, Thomas Ashe and O’Donovan Rossa.

In 1917, the band performed the first public rendition of The Soldiers’ Song by a band, which later became Ireland’s national anthem. More recently, St James’s has performed at the National Concert Hall, recorded for RTÉ Radio, and played at Áras an Uachtaráin.

Today, the band has over 50 members and performs a diverse repertoire spanning marches, overtures, popular music and more. This Culture Night, St James’s Brass & Reed Band brings its centuries-old musical tradition to Wood Quay Amphitheatre.

title: Worlds Collide on Culture Night at Powerscourt Townhouse Centre
description:
On Friday 18th September 2026, Powerscourt Townhouse will open the doors of the historic home of Richard & Amelia Wingfield for a special Culture Night experience.

Visitors are invited to explore three newly renovated rooms within the eighteenth century Townhouse, where history meets contemporary design. Decorated with a twenty first century twist, the spaces demonstrate that when worlds collide, something magical is created.

Discover The Stapleton, named after master plasterer Michael Stapleton, where Lord Powerscourt’s former Breakfast Room & Study is now a luxurious Lounge. Visit Amelia’s Table, once the Dining Room where The Wingfields entertained their guests, now a vibrant daytime café. Follow the notes of the harp to The Music Room, where Bethany Woolley performs eighteenth century music beneath the magnificent ceiling watched over by Minerva, the goddess of wisdom and music.

Visitors can also experience The World Outside, an exhibition of new paintings by John Fitzsimons at SO Fine Art Editions. The Culwick Choral Society will also perform on the night.

On Culture Night you’ll be surprised how the past and present come together. History really does have a way of repeating itself!

Improvised scenes, ritual games and comic encounters will be shaped by audience suggestions, choices and participation, culminating in a séance where the audience themselves become the “spirits” and help determine what happens next.

Blending Sligo’s literary heritage with live comedy, mysticism and communal play, the event offers a playful and accessible take on Yeats. With no two performances the same, audiences are invited to laugh, imagine and participate together.

title: You Are The Signal
description:
You Are the Signal is an interactive audiovisual installation where audience movement becomes part of the artwork.

Visitors are invited to step into the installation which uses a motion-tracking system to detect movement and use it to generate and transform projected visuals and sound in real time. Walking, gesturing or dancing can change what the audience sees and hears, creating an evolving audiovisual environment that is different every time someone interacts with it. The installation is an open, drop-in experience, with no need  forany experience of dance, music or technology – simply come in, explore and see how  movements affects the space around you.

Developed by Leitrim-based musician, audio engineer and creative technologist Mat Warren, the project combines sound, generative technology and interactive visual systems to explore the relationship between people, movement and their environment. Come and experiment with the system, watch others interact with it, or simply step inside and see what you can create.

Within the medieval walls of the jewel, coastal town of Youghal lies the fascinating Youghal Gate Clock Tower. As the most visible landmark in the centre of Youghal Main Street, the tower has been inextricably linked with the surrounding landscape and community across more than 700 years of history.

 

Today, visitors can move through the inner stairs of the four storey, 89 feet/24 metres high tower to learn about its diverse past as a local time-keeper, gaol and centre of trade.
